guides.title: Account and access
guides.summary: Accept invitations, protect sign-in, select a Department, and manage access within organization and Department roles.

sections.heading: Account and access
sections.text: An organization administrator is optional. A Company can operate through administrators of its active Departments. Department administrators act only within their assigned Departments; ask Phaeno to handle company-wide setup, invitations or roles when no organization administrator is available. Your Portal access is created through an organization invitation. The current organization, selected Department, and your role determine which Customer records and actions are available.

sections.heading: Accept an invitation
sections.text: Open the newest invitation link sent for your organization. Review your name, organization, invited email, and Access after acceptance on the invitation page. Select Continue with your email. This goes directly to verification for the invited address; the email cannot be edited. Complete any required password or authenticator steps. Portal then returns you to the invitation for review and acceptance. Select Accept invitation to join, or Decline invitation. Known names do not need to be entered again. After accepting, the welcome message confirms your organization. Select Open Portal to continue. When creating your password, enter it once and use Show password or Hide password to check your entry. If another account is signed in, select Switch account. After sign-in, use Continue invitation if shown, then review and accept the saved invitation. An invitation link is private and can expire, be revoked, or be replaced by a newer link. Do not forward it. Phaeno tracks whether the invitation email was queued, delivered, bounced, or needs attention separately from whether the invitation is still pending or accepted. If an address hard-bounces, Phaeno must revoke the invitation and issue a new one to the corrected address. The identity service handles password verification and recovery. Complete the secure sign-in steps shown in Portal, and use Forgot password? when offered to recover access. Phaeno can adjust the proposed Organization role or Department access on your existing pending invitation. The same link remains valid until its original expiry; changing access does not send another invitation. If the access changes after you review it, Portal displays the updated access and asks you to select Accept invitation again. An expired invitation must be resent before it can be accepted. Once your membership is active, authorized role and Department-access changes apply immediately. You receive an informational email and do not need to accept another invitation. A deactivated membership still requires a fresh invitation and acceptance to restore access.

sections.heading: Protect your account
sections.text: After your first sign-in step, connect an authenticator app and confirm the code it displays. Save the one-time backup codes shown during setup somewhere private and separate from the device running the authenticator. Never send an authenticator or backup code to Phaeno or your organization administrator. If you lose the authenticator but still have a backup code, use that code to sign in, then contact Phaeno to reset the authenticator enrollment. If you lose both the authenticator and every backup code, contact Phaeno directly. Phaeno will verify your identity and organization before resetting MFA; all active sessions are revoked and you must connect a new authenticator before Portal access resumes. Email can start the support request but does not itself bypass MFA.

sections.heading: Confirm the current organization
sections.text: The header shows the organization active in your current session. That organization scopes every portal read and action. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is shown, stop before opening a job or Data Library record and contact Phaeno. If an expected record or action is missing, confirm the current organization before reporting a problem.

sections.heading: Work within a department
sections.text: The header identifies your current organization and department. If you have access to more than one department, open the user menu and choose Department before opening or creating work. With a single available department, it is selected for you. Changing departments closes the previous workspace; finish or save your work before switching. Your selected department is remembered when you refresh this browser. If that department is no longer available, Portal selects an available department after checking your current access. Signing out clears the remembered selection. Members see only their assigned departments. Organization administrators can select any active department in their organization, but the selected department still determines the records displayed. A department administrator's operational authority applies only to that department; it is not organization-wide access. Organization-wide data grants may be available in each department. If a department is unavailable or an expected Customer record is missing, ask your organization administrator or Phaeno to review the assignment. Do not change URLs to try to access another department. Organization and department administrators can open Departments from the user menu to manage the departments within their authority.

sections.heading: Manage department access and settings
sections.text: When adding a department, enter its name and optional settings. The system assigns a reference such as DEPT-000123 when you save; you do not enter a Code. References are unique within the organization and stay the same when a department is renamed or deactivated. The department name remains its main label. Existing references, including GENERAL, are retained and shown as read-only context when editing. Organization administrators manage all departments, organization defaults, the default department, and department lifecycle. Department administrators manage settings and member access only in their assigned departments. A person can be an administrator in Research and a member in Operations; granting one department role does not grant organization-wide administrator rights. In Departments, use a department's actions menu to Edit settings or Manage members. To add an existing organization member, enter their exact email, choose Find member, and review the access change before confirming. Only an organization administrator can invite someone new through User management or change an organization role. Organization administrators already have access to every department and cannot be restricted by a department admin. An active member must retain at least one active department assignment. Organization administrators use Edit organization defaults to set the purchase-order rule, billing and notification email, and shipping and result instructions. A department override takes precedence; a blank override inherits the organization value, then the existing system or commercial fallback. Saved shipping and accepted-quote snapshots retain their recorded values. Result instructions do not change the storage destination or grant an ordering service. Invitations require reviewed department access for members. Select each department and grant its administrator role only when needed. Organization administrators receive access to every department, including future additions. If settings changed while you were editing, review your preserved entries against the latest version before saving again. Closing an unsaved form asks whether to discard the changes.

sections.heading: Understand roles
sections.text: Member can review the work in their selected, assigned Department and download files that have been released. Department administrator can also create and submit laboratory requests, accept quotes, request cancellations, and manage Department access and settings within assigned Departments. Organization administrator can perform those actions in every active Department and manage organization membership, defaults, and Department structure. Actions remain hidden or unavailable when the current organization or your role does not permit them. Phaeno can assist with access, but it cannot bypass the organization boundary to expose another Customer’s records.

sections.heading: Manage Customer members
sections.text: Customer organization administrators manage membership only for their current organization. In User management, active members and invited people appear in one list. A Pending invitation status means the invitation has not been accepted and the offered access is not active. The person may already have a sign-in account. Use the card’s actions menu to resend or revoke that invitation, edit an active member’s organization role, or deactivate another member’s membership. An administrator cannot deactivate their own membership from User management. Enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, but never copy or request an invitation token. A deactivated membership is restored only through a fresh invitation and acceptance. Contact Phaeno for a globally disabled account or an action the organization administrator cannot complete. For a Member invitation, select at least one Department. If you clear all Departments and select Send invitation, the form returns focus to Department access and explains what to select. Your entries are retained and no invitation is sent until the required information is valid.

sections.heading: Resolve common access states
sections.text: | What you see | What to do | | --- | --- | | Invitation link unavailable | Ask an administrator to confirm the invitation access state and email-delivery state. Resend only a still-valid address; after a hard bounce, request revoke/reissue to the corrected address. Use only the newest link. | | Email does not match | Sign out and use the email address that received the invitation, or request a corrected invitation. | | No active memberships | Ask your Customer administrator to coordinate a fresh invitation with Phaeno. | | Wrong organization shown | Stop before opening records and contact Phaeno to verify the active membership. | | Organization unavailable | Ask Phaeno whether the organization is inactive. | | Account disabled | Contact Phaeno. A Customer administrator cannot override a globally disabled account. | | Authenticator lost, backup code available | Use one backup code to sign in, then contact Phaeno for an MFA reset. | | Authenticator and backup codes lost | Contact Phaeno for identity verification and an MFA reset. Do not send old codes. | | Expected action missing | Confirm the current organization and Department, then ask an administrator to review your role and Department assignments. | Never send a password, sign-in code, invitation token, or browser storage value in a support message.

guides.title: Data Library and organization access
guides.summary: Distinguish Job results from curated data, manage organization access, and track transportation kits at delivery locations.

sections.heading: Data Library and organization access
sections.text: The Data Library contains Phaeno-curated example data explicitly shared with your organization or department. Your own laboratory results remain with their job.

sections.heading: Open results for a lab job
sections.text: Open the job under Lab services, then find Files and results. This is the single place to review its released result versions, download available files, and check retention. Scientific approval and Phaeno release determine availability; payment does not block PSeq result release. An older job-specific Data Library link now opens that job's results section automatically.

sections.heading: Use the Data Library
sections.text: The organization Data Library shows active curated-package grants shared across your organization or assigned to your selected department. These packages are separate from laboratory job inputs and results. Each grant points to an exact, immutable package version. A later package publication does not silently change the version your organization received. You can review the package summary, scientific context, quality information, file manifest, and checksums. Active organization members can download individual files or a complete archive. The archive includes the manifest and every file in that version. Curated packages are read-only. Customer users cannot edit, republish, or grant them to another organization.

sections.heading: Understand access changes
sections.text: Phaeno may grant, upgrade, revoke, quarantine, or retire a package. Revocation or quarantine blocks new viewing and downloads but cannot recall copies already downloaded. If a prior download needs action, the portal gives organization administrators Customer-safe guidance. Organization and department administrators can review curated download history for the selected department. This includes downloads from packages shared across the organization. Organization administrators can switch departments to review each department's activity. Department administrators see only activity within their assigned departments. Older download records without a recorded department remain available only to organization administrators, for organization-wide grants or grants assigned to the selected department. Changing a person's department assignments does not move or erase their earlier download records.

sections.heading: Manage organization members
sections.text: Organization administrators use User management to invite people, review Department access, and manage organization membership. Department administrators use Departments for member access and settings within their assigned Departments. See Account and access for the role boundaries and invitation steps. The User management screen saves invitations, eligible role changes, and membership deactivation to the Portal account system. Deactivation ends portal access without deleting the person or audit history, and restoring an inactive membership requires a fresh invitation. Phaeno administrators handle global account disablement and organization status. Every user should have their own account. Do not share sign-in credentials or use a shared mailbox as a substitute for an accountable user.

sections.heading: Manage delivery locations
sections.text: From Departments, open Delivery locations for the relevant Department. Organization administrators can manage all their Departments' locations; Department administrators manage only their assigned Departments. Use Add delivery location for a new address. Open an existing location to review its address, contact and delivery instructions, then use Actions → Edit location in the page header to make changes or select a default. These addresses are for kits Phaeno sends to your organization. They are separate from the laboratory destinations used when you return samples. A confirmed transportation-kit order keeps the delivery address shown at confirmation; later edits or deactivation do not rewrite that saved address. See Prepare and ship samples for ordering, tracking and receipt acknowledgment. Open a location's Transportation kits area to review containers on the way, available containers, and containers assigned to or in use by a Job. Administrators can confirm receipt of arrived kits here even when the Job that originally requested them has been cancelled. Unused received containers remain available for eligible Jobs at that location. During preparation, scanning and confirming a container's permanent barcode assigns it to a shipment; entering a stock quantity does not create or transfer physical inventory. Safety and withdrawal instructions about previously supplied data continue to go to current organization administrators during an organization suspension. These notices do not restore Portal access. Contact Phaeno if you cannot record a required response in the portal.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.summary: Find Customer Jobs, samples, results, curated data, and retained Trials in the selected Department.

sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: Portal keeps your organization’s laboratory requests, sample progress, released results, commercial documents, curated data, and user access in one place.

sections.heading: Navigate the help center
sections.text: Open the user dropdown menu in the toolbar and choose Documentation under Resources. This entry is available on both wide and narrow screens. On smaller screens, the Documentation tab sits below the toolbar and organization details. Guide navigation opens beneath the toolbar from the far-left edge of the screen. Its header identifies Documentation and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the tab. Choosing a guide closes an unpinned sidebar and displays the article.

sections.heading: Confirm the current organization
sections.text: The header shows the organization active in your current session. That organization controls which records and actions you can see. Customer information never carries across organizations. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is active, or your account belongs to more than one external organization, contact Phaeno before continuing.

sections.heading: Know your access level
sections.text: Customer organization administrators and department administrators can create and submit laboratory requests, accept quotes, and request cancellations within their operational Department. Organization administrators manage organization-wide invitations and roles. Other active members can review their organization’s jobs, follow progress, and download results that have been released. If an expected action is missing, first confirm the organization shown in the header. Your organization administrator can then check your membership.

sections.heading: Find your work
sections.text: Dashboard summarizes laboratory Jobs, assigned data, and any retained Trial history for the selected Department. Follow its links to the owning records; administrators also have a User management starting point. Lab services contains each job from request and pricing through sample preparation, shipping, laboratory progress, and results. Data Library contains Phaeno-curated packages assigned to your organization or Department. Each lab Job owns its Files and results section. For organization administrators, User management manages durable invitations, Member or Organization administrator roles, and membership deactivation. Documentation in the user dropdown menu opens these guides.

sections.heading: Keep submissions safe
sections.text: The initial laboratory request workflow is not a protected-health-information intake workflow. Do not enter patient names, dates of birth, medical record numbers, or other direct identifiers in request fields, notes, file names, or uploads. Use your organization’s own reference values and follow the instructions attached to the selected analysis.

sections.heading: Get help
sections.text: When contacting Phaeno, provide the portal request or sample reference and a description of the step you were performing. Do not send credentials, authentication tokens, or sensitive sample content in a support message.

sections.heading: Earlier Trial Projects
sections.text: If your organization converted from Prospect, Trial Projects retains the approved Trial history and available results in their original department. Conversion preserves existing download deadlines. See Trial history.

sections.heading: Search and browse guides
sections.text: Use Search documentation at the top of Documentation to find a guide or a matching section. Results update after a short pause; use at least two characters. Try “sample shipping” or “results and billing”. Choose Filters to narrow results by Topic, Workflow, or Guide type. Clear filters removes those selections. Browse by topic opens guides for a topic without requiring search words. Workflow links and Related guides at the end of an article provide other ways to find relevant instructions. Select a result title to open its matching section. Your browser’s Back action restores the search and filters. Search uses the guides for your current organization; it does not include the public Website or operational records. A guide’s instructions do not change your account permissions. If no guides match, try fewer words or clear the filters. If search is temporarily unavailable, use Try again or Browse all guides. A documentation update may require Refresh page; guide browsing remains available while the update finishes.

guides.title: Request laboratory services
guides.summary: Complete ordering and shipping on the Job, then follow receipt, laboratory progress and results.

sections.heading: Request laboratory services
sections.text: Use Lab services within the selected Department to describe and price a Job before entering its exact sample list. Organization and Department administrators may prepare a Job. An organization administrator or an administrator of the selected Department may place a configured standard order or accept an applicable manual quote.

sections.heading: Additional samples after acceptance
sections.text: Phaeno can issue a separate Change quote for additional samples on an active accepted Job. Review the added source counts, incremental charge, tax status and expiry. An organization or assigned-Department administrator can Review and accept addition, enter a required purchase order number and affirm the exact scope and price, or Decline addition. The original agreement and existing laboratory work remain in effect. Expired or superseded proposals cannot be accepted. Acceptance opens sample entry for the additional counts. Previously authorized samples remain locked. Add the new samples individually, then review and finalize the full list; only new samples receive additional laboratory and shipping authorization. If laboratory review is required, no partial authorization is saved. Completion bills the original accepted quote plus accepted additions; declining a proposal does not cancel the Job.

sections.heading: Follow the Job workspace
sections.text: The Job has two areas. Ordering and shipping shows six horizontal icons: Pricing review (or Confirm pricing when a quote is ready), Sample identification, Container supply, Assign containers, Match samples to tubes, and Send samples. Checkmarks show completed work, the current step is highlighted, and future steps are muted. On a narrow screen, move along the step strip to review the remaining steps. Once transportation kits are ordered and compatible containers are still needed, Your next step reads Wait for containers to arrive. View kit delivery opens the shipping area; the message distinguishes Phaeno preparing the containers from containers in transit. Confirm receipt only after the kits physically arrive. Assign shipping containers appears when compatible received containers are available at the selected container location; previously received stock can be used without waiting for a new delivery. Container location appears with container selection: one active location is shown as plain text, while multiple locations offer a selector. The selector remains available when the selected location has no stock so you can check another location. The kit-order modal separately uses Kit receiving location for the address where new kits should arrive. Hover over an icon, focus it with the keyboard, or tap it to read its detailed explanation and status, including who must act when work remains. Press Escape, move keyboard focus away or tap outside to close the information. Icons provide information; selecting one does not open work or change the Job. This also applies to completed and future steps. Your next step below the icons explains the required task, any prerequisite, and whether it is with you, your administrator, Phaeno or the carrier. Use its action button for the required work on the same Job. The steps reflect saved records; they are not checkboxes to mark yourself. Waiting for pricing or delivery is not a task you must complete personally. Send includes reviewing and confirming the shipping insert, printing its current revision, following the packing instructions, putting the insert inside the correct container, handing the package to the carrier and recording the shipment. Repeat for each required container. Confirming an insert records its revision; opening a print dialog does not prove that it was printed or packed. Send is complete only when every required active shipment has been recorded as sent. The Job's Actions menu gathers eligible commands under This order and Selected shipment, with the selected shipment reference shown when shipping commands apply. One available command may appear directly. Permissions and the current stage determine which commands are available; Members retain review and permitted downloads without administrator actions. Cancellation remains available under its existing rules. After you send shows recorded shipments and tracking, actual receipt, the latest laboratory progress, timing, and released results. Each recorded shipment can move into this area while another container is still being prepared. All required dispatches must be recorded before the shipping steps are complete. A later request for clarification or replacement material remains visible above the work areas; follow the permitted response without reopening a dispatched shipment's tube assignments.

sections.heading: Review a Job initiated by Phaeno
sections.text: Phaeno may initiate a Customer-owned Job when your organization has already discussed the work with Phaeno. It appears in Lab services as Quote in preparation while Phaeno prices it. You do not need to submit that Job for pricing. Open the Job and review its committed sample count, biological-source composition, storage requirements, safety declaration, and notes. When Phaeno issues the quote and it becomes Quote issued, an organization or department administrator can review it in Quote and billing and select Accept quote beside Order details and billing. Phaeno cannot accept it for your organization. If the scope is incorrect, do not accept the quote; contact Phaeno so the Job can be returned for a corrected revision. For a manually quoted Job, individual sample entry remains unavailable until your organization accepts the quote.

sections.heading: Submit a lab service request
sections.text: Request lab service is available only while your organization has current ordering authorization and PSeq Lab Service is offered. If new Jobs are unavailable, the page explains whether Phaeno must enable ordering authorization or the service is temporarily unavailable. Existing accepted Jobs remain available and follow their normal hold or cancellation workflow. Open Lab services and select Request lab service. In Submit lab service request, enter a unique Job name and each Biological source with its sample count. The Portal calculates the Job's total sample count from those source groups. Enter the Storage requirements and Safety declaration shared by every sample, and any optional Job notes. Do not enter a patient name or identifier. Select Submit request. The portal assigns an immutable eight-character Job number using unambiguous uppercase letters and numbers. The request opens on its detail page at Pricing review, with Waiting for pricing as its next step. Phaeno prepares pricing for you to accept or decline. Submission does not authorize work; individual sample entry remains unavailable until you accept. Members can review work in their assigned Department. Organization and Department administrators may create, edit, submit and accept applicable manual quotes in that Department. Organization and assigned-Department administrators may also place configured standard orders. Department authority does not grant access to other Departments. If an older draft still contains sample rows from the former workflow, the Job identifies them as legacy rows. Clear each row’s details before submitting for pricing; enter the current sample roster again only after accepting the price.

sections.heading: Existing configured standard drafts
sections.text: For an existing unsubmitted draft with a configured standard offering, in Standard PSeq Lab Service, choose an available Offering. Review its allowed material types and biological sources, included scientific outputs, published turnaround range, sample count, purchased sample-sequencing runs, and price per run. The bundle includes laboratory processing and data assembly; it does not require a separate assembly purchase. Choose Review standard order. The review shows the current subtotal, approved tax, and final total. An organization or assigned-Department administrator supplies a PO when required, confirms the scope and prohibited-data statement, and selects Place standard order. The offering, scope, price and approved tax are retained with the Job. Detailed samples are entered afterward. If a readiness or billing requirement is incomplete, the displayed blockers explain why placement is unavailable. Phaeno must resolve the relevant service, shipping, billing or tax setup. A standard order cannot be committed with an unknown final total. If the offering, scientific definitions, price or organization settings change while reviewing, select Refresh terms and review again and affirm the new terms before placing. Describe any required sources, outputs or timing in the lab service request and its Job notes. There is no separate custom-work inquiry to submit for this Job.

sections.heading: Submit for review
sections.text: New requests are submitted for pricing when you select Submit request. Older unsubmitted drafts can use Actions → Submit for pricing. Do not include patient identifiers, PHI, or unnecessary personal data. No individual sample list is required or permitted at this stage. Submission preserves a pricing-profile revision. Phaeno can prepare pricing, request specific corrections, or reject work that cannot be performed. While Pricing review is pending, use Actions → Edit request to change the scope and select Submit changes, or Actions → Withdraw request to stop the request. Each submitted change preserves the earlier revision and returns the latest scope to Phaeno for pricing. When pricing is issued, the first step changes to Confirm pricing; review the quote and accept or decline it. Direct scope edits are unavailable once pricing is issued. When corrections are requested, create and submit a new revision. The prior revision remains in the job history; it is not silently overwritten.

sections.heading: Review and accept a quote
sections.text: From the Job's Actions, select Download quote PDF to save a Phaeno-branded copy of the displayed quote. It includes the Job, quote revision and dates, itemized prices, the biological sources and sample counts recorded for that quote, and any billing details and payment terms saved with that quote. Older quotes without a recorded source breakdown omit that table. Members can download quotes for their assigned Department; downloading does not accept a quote. If the download fails, select Download quote PDF again to retry. Laboratory services are priced per job. Phaeno issues an itemized, immutable Portal quote for the accepted scope. When your approved billing and tax information is available, the quote includes calculated tax and freezes those commercial terms. Otherwise the quote is labeled Pre-tax total, and applicable tax is calculated when the invoice is issued. A zero tax amount is valid for an exempt, non-taxable, or zero-rate determination. The quote is available after all non-billing readiness items are complete and a Customer administrator is active; billing must be complete before invoicing. Before accepting, confirm the committed sample count, biological-source composition, standard service scope, price, currency, expiration date, and whether the displayed amount includes tax or is pre-tax. A Customer organization administrator or an administrator of the selected Department can accept the current unexpired quote. If the scope changes after acceptance, Phaeno issues a separate change quote. Added work does not begin until the applicable change is accepted. Use Accept quote and Decline quote beside Order details and billing. Use the Job's Actions for Download quote PDF under This order. Declining a quote closes the entire request; the confirmation explains this before you proceed. Before a quote is available, use Withdraw request to close your request. After acceptance, use Request cancellation for Phaeno review. When declining, choose a reason: Our needs changed, Cost is too high, Selected another vendor, Prefer not to say, or Other. Only Other requires an explanation in the multiline Please explain field. The selected reason is recorded with the request closure. If accepting, declining, withdrawing, or requesting cancellation fails, review the message in the open dialog. Your entries remain available to correct and retry. Closing the dialog does not confirm the action. You are asked before discarding changed entries. While saving, the dialog stays open and its entries and actions are unavailable until the save finishes.

sections.heading: Expired quotes and extension requests
sections.text: An unaccepted quote shows Expired and its expiration date once its deadline passes. Accept quote appears beside Order details and billing for organization and department administrators; it is disabled with an explanation when acceptance is unavailable. Members can review and download the quote, and should ask an administrator to accept it. For the current expired quote, an organization or department administrator can select Request quote extension, optionally explain why more time is needed, and submit the request. Extension requested confirms that Phaeno has the request; another request for the same quote is unnecessary. If saving fails, the dialog keeps the entered reason so you can retry. If Phaeno issues a new revision, review its price, terms and new expiration date before accepting. An extension request does not accept a quote or automatically extend its deadline. The original revision remains in the history, and its PDF stays available. An accepted quote remains Accepted when its former expiration date passes.

sections.heading: Ship and track samples
sections.text: After placing the standard order or accepting the manual quote, open Sample identification in Samples and shipping. A blank row is provided for each remaining accepted sample, grouped under its biological source. Enter a unique Sample ID in each row; Tubes starts at 1 and can be changed if that sample includes reserves. Select Save sample IDs for the group. You can save part of a group and return to the remaining blank rows. The counts show saved samples; blank rows are not saved records. If a save is interrupted, confirmed saves remain and unconfirmed entries stay available for review and retry. Use Actions at the right of the Samples and shipping heading for list options. For CSV entry, select Actions → Download CSV template and Actions → Import sample list. Import is available only while there are no saved samples or unsaved entries; discard unsaved entries and clear saved sample details first to start again with a CSV. Once all required sample IDs and tube counts are saved, the menu is replaced by Review and finalize list, and CSV options are hidden. The CSV accepts exactly customer_sample_id, biological_source, and tube_count; it does not accept barcodes. Previewing a CSV does not change the Job. Confirming a valid preview saves the complete list as one operation. Samples are grouped by Biological source. Each heading shows saved and accepted sample counts, including sources with no saved entries yet. These counts measure samples, not tubes. All expected rows are visible during identification. Once the list is complete, saved samples are shown 10 per page with Previous samples, Next samples, and a range such as Samples 1–10 of 18. A group spanning pages repeats its heading and full count. Each saved sample’s Actions menu shows its sample ID in the header. Use Actions → Edit sample or Actions → Clear sample details. The Clear sample details? modal offers Cancel and Clear sample details. Confirming clears the saved ID and tube count while preserving the accepted source and required sample count. A blank required row returns with one tube as its default; complete it again before finalizing. Use Edit sample for simple corrections. Finalized samples retain their existing editing restrictions. The routine Expected lab status is hidden while preparing the list; other statuses remain visible. After finalization, each sample's Matched count shows saved tube matches across its active shipments. Expand the sample to review its tubes and their containers. Once a shipment is sent, tubes are received, or laboratory progress is recorded, the row also shows relevant Receipt and laboratory details. Receipt means actual tubes recorded as received, such as 1 of 4 tubes received; matching barcodes does not establish receipt. These counts cover the whole sample even when its tubes are split across containers. Accession details and review reasons remain visible when present. Checking... means information is loading; Not available means it cannot currently be shown, not that the count is zero. Sample IDs must be unique within the Job, and tube counts must be positive whole numbers. Do not enter patient names or direct identifiers. The biological source is already supplied by the group. To correct a saved sample, use Actions → Edit sample and choose another accepted source with room only when it accurately describes the sample. Save or discard unsaved IDs before editing saved samples, importing, or finalizing. Leaving with unsaved entries requires confirmation. If an existing group exceeds its accepted count, such as 2 of 1, it shows a red warning. Its samples remain available to review and correct. Edit a sample's source only when another accepted source accurately describes it and has room, or clear an extra entry’s details with confirmation. Samples with a source outside the accepted list are also shown for correction. The list cannot be finalized until its total and every source count match the accepted scope. Do not ship physical samples before the order is commercially committed and the exact roster is finalized. An early or unmatched package is quarantined and escalated by Phaeno; it is not accessioned or attached to active Job work. The final list must contain exactly the accepted number of unique non-PHI sample IDs, match every accepted source-group count, and give each sample a positive whole-number tube count. A green check beside the overall counter means the total and source counts are complete; it does not finalize the list. After saving every required sample ID and matching the accepted source counts, select Review and finalize list at the right of the Samples and shipping heading or in Your next step. Both buttons open the same review. Clearing sample details returns the card to its incomplete-list controls and hides the finalization shortcut until the required details are saved again. The review follows the same biological-source grouping as the sample area. Both views sort sample IDs in natural numeric order within each group, such as TEST-2 before TEST-10. The review shows source counts and the overall sample, allocated run and tube totals. Review every sample and affirm the no-PHI confirmation before selecting Finalize sample list. Finalization authorizes the specimen-specific Lab work and opens shipment preparation. Use Prepare containers from the Job's Actions, or use the container preparation area in Samples and shipping, and select the location you will ship from. Use compatible received containers available there, including unused kits originally requested for another Job. Order additional transportation kits when needed; kits and outbound delivery are included. Confirm physical arrivals from the location inventory or the Job's kit-delivery area. Links to delivery-location management retain Return to Lab Job with your selected container. Scan each physical container's permanent barcode, review tube allocations, and confirm to assign those containers to this Job's shipments. Each nonempty container becomes a separate shipment, and a sample's tubes may be split across them. With multiple choices, select the Shipping container deliberately before a shipment command; a single available choice is selected directly. Its reference remains visible. Container, kit and receipt details expands the supporting information without narrowing the scanner. Use Match tubes in Samples and shipping or the Job's Actions to match registered tubes in the selected container. One scan field opens inside the active tube row in the expanded sample. Container identity and overall progress stay above the list. For the displayed sample and tube number, scan its permanent barcode and press Enter or Save scan. Each match is saved separately before the next sample and tube are revealed. A successful save updates the barcode and progress, expands the next unmatched tube’s sample, scrolls its row into view and focuses its inline field. Failed, unknown, ineligible, duplicate and already-used scans retain the entered barcode and current target for review and retry. The first saved match locks container reset. Expand a sample to review its individual tubes and container identities. The same list keeps 10 samples per page throughout matching. Reviewing another page does not change the entered barcode or target; Return to active tube restores its sample. Done scanning appears at the right of the Samples and shipping heading only after every tube in the selected container has a saved match. The last saved match closes the field and leaves the list open for review. As part of Send, review and confirm each shipping insert from the Job's Actions. When the selected shipment's current insert is ready, Your next step offers Print shipping insert directly and prints in place. Follow its packing instructions and put that current insert inside its container. After the print dialog returns, confirm that printing and packing are complete only when you have done both. Cancelling printing, dismissing the confirmation or a print error does not acknowledge the work. The Job, selected container and saved matches remain intact. After that explicit confirmation, the next-step button becomes Record shipment. Your confirmation is remembered in this browser tab for this shipment's current insert. A corrected insert must be printed and confirmed again. You must still hand the package to the carrier before recording its carrier, tracking number and shipment time. With several shipments, deliberately select the container you are working on; each keeps its own reminder. A sole available container remains selected directly. Reprint the current insert from Actions. Samples returns to the grouped overview without opening another page. Existing standalone shipment bookmarks remain available, and Trial shipping keeps its existing entry point. See Prepare and ship samples for the complete inventory, receipt, packing and scanning steps. After you send shows the latest recorded laboratory milestone, timing, holds and released results. This is current progress, not a checked history of every scientific stage. A Job can remain in progress while different samples move through laboratory work. When Phaeno records the first container's arrival, the Job shows Received. Individual sample receipt follows verification of actual tubes. A sample shows Accessioned after all its expected tubes across shipments have been accessioned. Partial receipt remains visible while other tubes are outstanding. Receipt does not mean scientific acceptance or analysis has begun. The Job list and header show recorded laboratory progress: Received → Library Prep → Sequencing → Data Assembly → Quality Review → Results Available. In After you send, each stage shows the number of samples currently at that stage. Choose View sample stages to review individual samples. These are current counts, not completion checkmarks; a partial release does not make the whole Job complete. When activity is recorded for the whole Job before individual samples are updated, the page explains that distinction. The Order status filter continues to find commercial stages such as In Progress, On Hold, or Completed. Sequencing requires recorded sequencing activity; shipping to the sequencing provider alone is insufficient. Quality Review includes scientific review and approved results awaiting release. Results Available requires an actual release. Holds, cancellation requests, and completed or cancelled orders retain their visible status. If Phaeno needs replacement material or clarification, the job shows a Customer-safe action and the current schedule health. Internal scientific investigation details are not shown. Ready for release means Phaeno's scientific review is complete and the final deliverable package is complete, checksummed, and malware-clean. It does not mean a file is downloadable until an authorized Result Release Manager publishes that sample. Invoice balance and credit status never gate PSeq result release.

sections.heading: Understand turnaround
sections.text: In After you send, Turnaround and progress shows first receipt, scientific acceptance, the original processing target, current expected completion, laboratory completion, delivery due date, original delivery target, and retained full Portal-delivery time. The published turnaround starts at scientific acceptance, not the day the package first arrives. Receipt-to-acceptance elapsed time remains visible separately. Phaeno may update the expected completion with a recorded reason. The original target remains visible. A later expected date queues a notice; an earlier date updates the Portal. Read the customer-safe explanation and current dates on the Job rather than treating an earlier message as the current schedule.

sections.heading: Cancel work
sections.text: A draft can be discarded before submission. Before Phaeno accepts work, an administrator can cancel eligible scope. After acceptance, submit a cancellation request. Phaeno records whether the request is approved, partially approved, or declined. Any correction to an issued PSeq invoice is retained as an append-only credit, debit, or write-off adjustment rather than editing the invoice.

sections.heading: Find and resume work
sections.text: Search and filter by status, dates, or Submitted by me. Previous and Next show the complete matching result set. From a Job, select Back to lab services to return with the filters and page retained. Clear all removes them. An empty filtered result is distinct from a failed load; use Retry records when loading fails.

sections.heading: What appears at each stage
sections.text: While reviewing an order or quote, Order details and billing stays open. Its heading row shows Accept quote and Decline quote when your permissions and the current order allow those actions. Review the total sample count and the biological-source counts in Quote and billing, alongside the price and expiry. Accepting still opens the confirmation dialog and any required purchase-order entry; selecting the first button alone does not place the order. Expired quotes cannot be accepted, and Members retain their existing review-only permissions. Sample submission and Samples and shipping appear after the order is placed or accepted and sample work becomes relevant. Existing sample records remain available for review. Order details may then be collapsed unless a quote decision is pending. After you send appears when there is recorded shipment, receipt, laboratory progress or released results to track. It stays hidden while you review a quote or prepare unsent samples. For split shipments, tracking can appear for a sent container while the remaining containers still need preparation. Any request for your attention remains visible above the work areas.

sections.heading: Multiple tubes for one sample
sections.text: Pricing counts sample-sequencing runs. Twenty samples sequenced once and one sample sequenced twenty times both count as 20. In the Job profile, leave Sample-sequencing runs blank for one run per sample, or enter the total requested runs. A machine batch is not the pricing unit. After accepting pricing, enter each sample once and allocate its Runs independently of Tubes. Use Edit sample to correct an allocation. The total must equal the purchased run count before Review and finalize list becomes available. The CSV template includes sequencing_runs; an older three-column CSV defaults each sample to one run. Submitted tube counts control shipping, not the price. Extra tubes alone do not authorize extra runs. Existing accepted prices and previously recorded scope are preserved. Phaeno reviews each received tube independently and selects one suitable source. A reserve is used only after the preceding processing attempt is explicitly closed as failed. If no material remains for further permitted analysis, the sample can have a failed processing outcome even though a tube passed receipt checks. Follow the Job's customer-facing progress and any request for additional information.

sections.heading: Delivery due date
sections.text: The delivery due date is separate from the current expected completion. Phaeno may adjust it with a recorded customer-safe reason; the original delivery target remains visible, and the change queues a notice. A forecast change alone does not move the delivery due date. Results are delivered when data for every in-scope sample has been made available through the Portal; you do not have to download or acknowledge them. Partial results and laboratory completion do not by themselves complete delivery. Standard turnaround remains an operating target unless your agreement explicitly provides a guarantee.

sections.heading: Requesting a specimen pause or resumption
sections.text: An organization administrator or administrator of the assigned Department can open a Lab Job and use Specimen holds. Choose Request pause for the affected sample and enter a reason. Other samples are unaffected. The request immediately blocks new preparation, new sequencing handoffs, new analysis and result release for that sample. Pause requested does not mean an ongoing physical procedure has stopped. Phaeno must confirm a safe pause, including any work already with an external provider. If that procedure cannot pause, its facts can still be recorded; new work and release remain blocked. Use Request resumption when ready. Work remains blocked until Phaeno approves resumption. Other authorization, material, quality and workflow requirements still apply, and approval does not automatically start work. Read Hold history for the recorded reasons and decisions. A hold does not automatically change charges, deadlines or retention dates, and results already delivered remain available. Contact Phaeno directly for an urgent request or a separate commercial or retention adjustment.

guides.title: Results and billing
guides.summary: Download scientifically released PSeq results, review retention, and find invoices independently of result access.

sections.heading: Results and billing
sections.text: Scientific readiness and Customer release are separate. The portal shows whether each sample is still being produced, scientifically approved, withdrawn, or available to download.

sections.heading: Follow sample progress
sections.text: Open a laboratory job to see each sample’s current state. Receipt, accessioning, laboratory work, data processing, result readiness, and completion are recorded independently so one delayed sample does not hide progress on the others.

sections.heading: Understand the release rule
sections.text: A PSeq result may be released after its final output package is complete, checksummed, malware-clean, and scientifically approved. An authorized Phaeno Result Release Manager publishes the selected sample; other samples can remain in progress. Payment balance, payment terms, tax state, and Customer credit do not gate release.

sections.heading: Download released results
sections.text: Open the laboratory Job and find Files and results. Review the package for the intended sample. Confirm that the result package is marked available rather than still under review or withdrawn. Review the release details and download the available files. Each release is immutable and linked to its scientific approval, package version, checksums, and quality facts. A corrected result is delivered as a new version; it does not replace the audit history of an earlier release. Download and retention events are audited. If a file passes its retention cutoff, contact Phaeno for an authorized reissue. For a newly released result, the job's Files and results section shows the retention schedule frozen at release. Standard deletion is the normal deletion time. Conditional grace through is used only when at least one file in that release remains undownloaded at the standard deadline; in that case the whole release receives the stated grace period. The displayed date and time include your browser's local time-zone label. Earlier releases created before retention snapshots were introduced do not show a schedule; contact Phaeno before relying on a deletion date for one of those releases. For governed PSeq packages, download status counts a file only after its complete response finishes successfully. A partial or interrupted transfer does not count. Completion must be saved successfully before the standard deadline to avoid grace. If availability changes while a download is being prepared, refresh the package before trying again. If the Portal cannot verify download timing, contact Phaeno; the dates already assigned to your package remain unchanged. One successful download by an authorized member satisfies that file for the organization. If any file was still undownloaded at the standard deadline, Grace period active keeps the whole package available through the final date. Completing the remaining files during grace does not shorten that period. Downloads closed removes new download access at the applicable deadline; it does not by itself mean that stored bytes have been deleted. Policy changes affect future releases and do not change dates already assigned to a package. A retention reminder, when enabled for the workflow, is addressed to active Organization admins and links to the normal Portal result page. The page shows current availability even if the email is older. Access withdrawal or deactivation can stop an in-progress transfer; restoring access requires a fresh download while the package is still available.

sections.heading: Review invoices
sections.text: At Job completion, Phaeno issues one numbered invoice. If the accepted quote included tax, the invoice preserves that frozen determination. If the quote was labeled Pre-tax total, the Portal calculates applicable tax from the approved billing profile at invoicing. The invoice freezes its billing, tax, currency, and payment terms; its due date is the completion date plus those terms. The immutable invoice PDF is available to your organization. The Portal does not collect payment-card information or provide online payment processing in this release. Receipts may be partially or fully applied to the invoice. Overpayments remain visible as unapplied cash until Finance explicitly allocates or resolves them. Corrections appear as retained credits, debits, or write-offs; an issued invoice is never silently rewritten.

sections.heading: Download other laboratory result releases
sections.text: Other managed laboratory files appear under their result release with the retention schedule assigned at release. Use Download package for its ZIP or Download for an individual file. Where retention enforcement is enabled, new file and ZIP requests close together at the applicable deadline. An incomplete release receives its stated grace period; completing it during grace does not shorten that period. The Portal refreshes availability after an unsuccessful attempt. Closed downloads do not mean bytes have been deleted. A file or package withdrawal, failed scan, or access removal can stop an active transfer. A failed ZIP does not count any file from that attempt; prior successful downloads remain counted. Earlier releases without a schedule keep their existing contract; contact Phaeno for guidance instead of inferring a date. Where scheduled retention notices are enabled for Lab releases, active Organization admins receive one download reminder if the release is incomplete at its warning checkpoint, and one grace notice if grace applies. A delayed reminder is skipped if every file has completed or the standard deadline has passed. There are no daily reminders. Notices contain the release reference, deadline, and a sign-in link to the laboratory job; open the job for current availability. Delivery problems do not extend retention dates. Contact Phaeno if a notice needs support.

sections.heading: Keep a release receipt
sections.text: Open View retained package receipt beside a release's retention schedule, then choose Print / save PDF. The receipt retains the complete file manifest, byte sizes, checksums, original deadlines, recorded completion and deletion facts, and any reissue links. It contains metadata, not copies of the scientific files. Times include your display time zone and their UTC value. For newly captured Lab releases, the receipt also retains the sample identifier, recorded supplier tube barcodes, and Phaeno accession as they stood at release. Historical releases may show that lineage was not recorded. Organization admins can also review the organization's downloader history; other members see the release facts available within their Department. A quarantined package cannot be downloaded. A preservation hold protects retained files without extending their download window. Contact Phaeno about either state. After deletion, an authorized reissue requires a newly prepared and approved package; the original receipt and dates remain unchanged.

guides.title: Prepare and ship samples
guides.summary: Use the Job workspace to receive kits, assign containers, scan tubes, print inserts and record dispatch.

sections.heading: Prepare and ship samples
sections.text: For a normal Lab Service Job, sample entry begins after the price is accepted. Shipping and laboratory authorization begin after the exact sample list is finalized. Open the owning Job under Lab services, then use Samples and shipping within Ordering and shipping. Container preparation, tube matching, shipping inserts and dispatch stay on this Job. An organization administrator or an administrator of the selected Department performs these actions. Members can review their Department's shipments and use permitted print and download actions. The six horizontal icons above the work area are Confirm order, Samples, Kits, Containers, Match tubes, and Send. Checkmarks show completed work, the current step is highlighted, and future steps are muted. Hover over an icon, focus it with the keyboard, or tap it to read its detailed explanation and status, including who must act when work remains. Press Escape, move keyboard focus away or tap outside to close the information. Icons provide information without opening work, including completed and future steps. Your next step below them explains the required task and who must act; use its action button for the required work. After you send separately tracks dispatched containers, receipt, laboratory progress and results. Partial sends can appear there while preparation continues for other containers. Send includes shipping insert review and confirmation, printing the current revision, packing it inside the correct container, handing the package to the carrier and recording dispatch. It completes only when every required active shipment is recorded as sent. Confirming or printing an insert alone does not complete Send.

sections.heading: Order and receive transportation kits
sections.text: Transportation kits belong to your Customer/Department delivery location. Received, unused containers can be used for an eligible Job at that location, including containers originally requested while preparing a different Job. The originating Job remains part of the delivery history; cancelling it does not consume unused containers. Use Prepare containers from the Job's Actions, or use the preparation area for tubes awaiting containers, and use Container location to choose where the received containers are stored. It appears beside container selection, with a plain location name when only one active location is available. Review available containers and kits still on the way. If more are needed, use Order transportation kits at the right of the Transportation kits heading, review the Recommended kit configuration for this shipment and Kit receiving location, and select Confirm kit order. You can adjust compatible sizes before confirming. Transportation kits and outbound delivery are included with the accepted laboratory order at no additional charge. Existing compatible received stock can satisfy the need without another order. Use Add a delivery location or Manage delivery locations when an address needs setup or correction. Delivery locations belong to your organization and Department. Administrators can maintain them from the Department workspace. The confirmed order retains the address shown at confirmation even if the saved location changes later. When you open address setup from kit ordering, Return to Lab Job restores the Job and selected container and reopens the unsubmitted kit review. A default address is selected; otherwise choose an address explicitly. Returning from ordinary location inventory restores the Job without reopening kit review. No return action places an order. Kits ordered means Phaeno has received the order for fulfillment. Reopening the page or repeating the same confirmation does not place a second order. Before any kits are dispatched, use Cancel kit order at the right of the Transportation kits heading to review the cancellation. Once dispatched, the kit number, carrier and tracking appear as On the way. This is provisional inventory and is not yet available for preparing samples. When the kits arrive, select Confirm kits received at the right of the Transportation kits heading and acknowledge only those you have actually received. Each acknowledged container becomes Available at its delivery location. If delivery is partial, prepare only with the received containers while the remaining kits stay outstanding. Once receipt is complete, the delivery area shows Kits received without asking you to confirm arrival again. An organization or Department administrator records receipt; ordinary members can review the status. Select View shipping and receiving location to open the selected location and review its Transportation kits inventory, tracking and receipt actions. Use this location view when the Job that originally requested the kits has been cancelled. Inventory distinguishes containers On the way, Available, Assigned to a Job, and In use. Refresh to see changes recorded by another user. Preparation requires registered, received containers at the selected location. A container at another Customer, Department or location, an unreceived container, or one already assigned or in use cannot be claimed. Contact Phaeno if physical stock and its recorded location or receipt do not agree; entering a quantity does not register stock or transfer it between locations.

sections.heading: Configure the supplied containers
sections.text: Assign shipping containers recommends compatible available stock at the selected location, using the fewest containers and then the least spare capacity. Each size shows its common name, SKU number and usable tube capacity. A catalog size alone does not establish that a physical container is available. Open Assign containers at the right of the Assign shipping containers heading and scan the permanent barcode on each physical container you intend to use. Review its size, SKU, capacity and tube allocation. Each container has a numbered card (Container 1, Container 2, and so on), with Container, Tubes, and Scan or enter container barcode fields. The recommendation is labeled Recommended containers — not yet assigned; receiving a container makes it available but does not assign it to this Job. Barcode entry and preview do not reserve stock until you confirm. A row's Remove action removes that selection from the draft. It is hidden when the single selected container is the only compatible container available. Use compatible sizes you actually have available. For example, 30 tubes can use a 20 and a 10, or six 5s. Smart choices avoid redundant containers; spare slots are allowed when needed for the available sizes. Three remaining tubes should use an available 5 rather than adding an available 10 or 20. The Portal checks recorded stock automatically, without manual availability quantities. The preview shows tubes, containers, usable capacity, spare slots and unallocated tubes. Confirm assignment reserves the exact scanned containers and creates a shipment for each nonempty container. If another user has claimed a selected container, the save fails with an explanation and preserves your draft for correction. Partial preparation leaves the remaining tubes awaiting containers. Spare slots are empty capacity, not missing samples. A sample's tubes may be split among shipments. Container choices do not change accepted sample counts or pricing. Assigned tubes and confirmed shipping inserts are not silently rearranged if configuration changes. Contact Phaeno when existing assignments or a dispatched shipment need reconciliation. Adjust each row's tube count as needed. Counts must be whole numbers, fit each container and together equal the tubes allocated in the preview. The Summary stays visible while updating; confirmation becomes available when the current allocation has been checked.

sections.heading: Scan and retain tube identities
sections.text: Use Shipping container in the Job's Samples and shipping area to choose a container or remaining tubes awaiting containers. With several choices, select deliberately before using a shipment command; a single available choice is selected directly. The selected shipment reference remains visible. Switching container or returning to Samples asks before discarding an unsaved scan and is unavailable while saving. Open Container, kit and receipt details for supporting information without narrowing the scan area. Before scanning starts, an organization or Department administrator can use Reset container configuration in Container, kit and receipt details. Review the confirmation: it returns all containers and tubes for the Job to container selection, not just the shipment you opened. Your finalized sample list stays intact, and the previous configurations remain in the records and audit history for support. Retired configurations stay out of normal container choices; an older direct link identifies them as history. Cancelling the confirmation changes nothing. Reset container configuration is also unavailable while a barcode entry is unsaved or saving. Discard an unsaved entry before revising the plan; saving the first scan locks the plan as described below. Before any tube is scanned, a successful reset releases the selected containers back to available inventory at their locations and returns the Job's tubes to preparation. Previous configurations remain in history. The action is locked once any container for the Job has a saved tube scan, bound tube roster, shipping insert, sample-return dispatch or sample receipt. Clearing a scan does not restore it. If another user starts work while your confirmation is open, refresh and review the current state. The finalized sample list, quote, original kit deliveries and their receipts remain intact. Use a stable Customer sample ID that your organization can connect to its own sample record. Do not enter patient names, medical-record numbers, dates of birth or other direct identifiers. Use Match tubes in Samples and shipping or the Job's Actions to match registered tubes in the selected container. One scan field opens inside the active tube row in the expanded sample. Container identity and overall progress stay above the list. For the displayed sample and tube number, scan its permanent barcode and press Enter or Save scan. Each match is saved separately before the next sample and tube are revealed. A successful save updates the barcode and progress, expands the next unmatched tube’s sample, scrolls its row into view and focuses its inline scan field. Failed, unknown, ineligible, duplicate and already-used scans retain the entered barcode and current target for review and retry. The first saved match locks container reset. Expand a sample to review its individual tubes, saved barcodes and container identities. The list keeps 10 samples per page; there is no separate Scan tubes view. While matching, saving reveals the next unmatched tube's sample and page. Reviewing another page or expanding a different sample does not change the active scan target or entered barcode. Return to active tube restores its sample and inline scan field, including the unfinished barcode. No barcode field is shown while the active sample is collapsed or on another page. The scan progress applies to the selected container; each sample's matched count covers all its active containers. Done scanning appears at the right of the Samples and shipping heading only after every tube in the selected container has a saved match. Leaving or changing containers preserves the existing unsaved-scan warning. Paging and dismissal are unavailable while saving. After the last match, the field closes and the same list remains open for review. Use registered tubes belonging to the physical container assigned during preparation. The first successful tube scan changes that container from assigned to in use and locks reset; it does not choose a different container implicitly. A tube from another container, an unknown or duplicate barcode, or an already-used tube cannot advance the step. A failed scan keeps the entered value and current sample available for correction and retry. Do not cover, alter or remove permanent container or tube barcodes. If the wrong tube was assigned, use Change tube or Correct tube and record why the assignment changed. The earlier association remains in history. A correction after shipping insert confirmation, but before dispatch, voids that shipping insert and issues a corrected revision. Destroy unused copies of the old shipping insert and print the replacement.

sections.heading: Confirm each shipment and print its shipping insert
sections.text: Use the Job's Actions menu for Selected shipment commands, including Review and confirm shipping insert, Review packing instructions, Print shipping insert, Download tube list (CSV) and Record shipment when permitted. The shipment reference identifies the container affected; This order holds applicable order commands. If only one command is available, it appears directly. Your permissions and the complete shipment's stage determine availability. Completing one visible tube page does not complete the container. Authorized readers retain print and download access. Use Print shipping insert again for another copy of the current revision. Within Send, review every physical tube in the container, then select Review and confirm shipping insert. Confirmation shows separate sample and tube counts and freezes the destination, instructions, manifest and crosswalk for that revision. A container can be partly filled when all its declared tubes are matched; spare capacity does not require extra tubes. Print one receiving sheet for each physical container and place it inside that container. It shows the Customer, Job/Trial and shipment references, sample and tube totals, essential handling notes and two widely separated scan targets: the large Scan to receive this shipment PH-P- insert barcode and, when assigned, the physical container barcode. Follow the full preparation and packing instructions in the Portal before shipping. Follow the approved temperature-control method, amount and packing steps for the actual container. Instructions may call for regular ice, dry ice, cold packs, another method or no cooling. Do not substitute methods or multiply the amount by the number of samples. Contact Phaeno if the instructions are missing or conflict. Full packing instructions and sample / tube list on the insert page retains the confirmed manifest, every sample and tube barcode, and split-sample references; these details do not print with the receiving sheet. Use Previous samples and Next samples to review long manifests. Receiving-sheet totals always cover the complete container. Use Download tube list (CSV) to retain the complete crosswalk. Laboratory staff acknowledge container arrival in Receive shipments; the tubes are then accessioned individually. Customer barcode lookup alone does not record laboratory receipt. When Send is current and the selected shipment's insert is ready, Your next step offers Review packing and print. It checks the current revision and displays the saved destination, common steps, sample requirements and actual container’s packing instructions. Review the cooling method and amount, then select Print shipping insert. The browser print dialog opens while keeping the Job page, selected container and saved tube matches intact. After the print dialog returns, explicitly confirm that the current insert was successfully printed and placed inside its correct container only when you have done both. Opening, closing or cancelling printing never makes that confirmation for you. If you cancelled printing, dismiss the follow-up and print again when ready. Print or revision-check errors also leave the work unacknowledged. After your explicit printing-and-packing confirmation, Your next step changes to Record shipment. Your confirmation is remembered in this browser tab for this shipment's current insert. A corrected insert must be printed and confirmed again. You must still record the shipment after carrier handoff. Send stays unfinished until every required dispatch is recorded. With several shipments, deliberately select the current container before printing or recording it; each has its own insert and confirmation. A sole available container remains selected directly. Reopen Actions → Review packing instructions at any time. Reprint the current insert through Actions for another copy; this does not issue a new revision. If the insert cannot be checked, review the message on the Job, reconnect if needed and select Try again. If insert confirmation fails, the message appears in the open dialog and your entries remain available. Retain the shipping insert or use Download tube list (CSV) so your organization can connect its own identifiers to the permanent tubes. The shipping insert does not buy postage or replace the carrier label.

sections.heading: Record dispatch and follow receipt
sections.text: After handing each package to the carrier, use Record shipment for its carrier, tracking number and shipment time. Repeat for each physical shipment. After you send shows recorded dispatches, tracking and actual receipt; Ordering and shipping remains active for containers still being prepared. All required active shipments must have recorded dispatch before the customer shipping steps are complete. A later clarification or replacement request can still require your attention. For each finalized sample, use the Matched and Receipt counts in Samples. Saved matches cover that sample's active shipments, while receipt is the actual recorded tube count. Checking… or Not available must not be read as zero. Per-container and Job-wide totals remain explicitly scoped in the scan and receipt details. A sample split across containers remains partly received until all its expected tubes have been recorded; receiving the first package does not mark the entire sample received. Use Samples to return to the grouped Job overview or Shipping container to choose another container without leaving the Job. Existing standalone shipment bookmarks remain available, and Trial shipping keeps its existing entry point. If a tube cannot be matched confidently, a printed barcode cannot be read, or there is no compatible container, contact Phaeno with the Job and shipment references instead of guessing. After a shipment is sent, select its Shipping container in Samples and shipping, then choose Reprint shipping insert. When several containers are available and none is selected, Actions → Select container to reprint insert takes you to the container selector. Reprinting opens the browser print dialog for the current insert without issuing a new revision or recording another shipment or receipt. Portal-generated identifiers now render as QR codes, with the exact identifier printed underneath. Shipping inserts, container labels, kit records and displayed sample/tube identifiers use the same format. Use a QR-capable 2D scanner. Existing manufacturer labels and older printed barcodes remain valid; do not relabel a tube or change its saved identity merely to match the new display. A scan still requires the correct workflow and does not by itself confirm receipt or accession. With one container, the tube count is assigned automatically up to its capacity and shown in a read-only text box. Any remaining tubes stay unallocated. With multiple containers, edit the tube counts to split the allocation. Returning to one container restores its automatic allocation. Samples are ordered by ID alphabetically and digit by digit, rather than by numeric value. In the Job, biological-source groups stay together. Tube matching follows that sample order, with each sample’s tubes in tube-number order. Saving a match advances to the next unmatched tube. Sample rows show matching progress as 1 of 1 tube matched or 2 of 2 tubes matched. This includes the tube total, so the row does not repeat a separate quantity while matching status is shown. Long sample IDs wrap; they are not shortened or changed.

guides.title: Statuses and troubleshooting
guides.summary: Interpret Job, sample, quote, invoice, scan, and release states; recover roster, access, and download problems.

sections.heading: Statuses and troubleshooting
sections.text: A laboratory Job, each sample, its quote, invoice, and released result package have separate statuses. One sample can have released results while others are still processing. PSeq result access is independent of payment and Customer credit.

sections.heading: Laboratory Job statuses
