sections.text: Awaiting shipment becomes Awaiting submission when the kit ships. Preparing inputs identifies an existing saved input request. In progress follows submitted work; Results released, Expired, and Cancelled are case outcomes. Open the request or Prepare inputs from the owning Kit order. Corrections stay with the same case.

sections.heading: Commercial and file states
sections.text: Superseded or Expired quotes cannot be accepted; review the current quote or request a new one. Credit-approved Partner assembly work uses Net 30 release. Otherwise output remains on Payment hold; the current portal does not provide payment confirmation, so contact Phaeno about the request. Assembly inputs and outputs must complete validation and a clean scan. Rejected, Failed, or Unavailable scan states prevent submission. An authorized administrator can remove an incorrect input from an editable draft and provide a valid replacement; contact Phaeno when a valid input continues to fail. A file is downloadable only when its release status is Released. Ready does not bypass a payment gate, and Withdrawn files remain unavailable. PSeq Kit orders use the negotiated bundle price and included profile captured at placement. Included Assembly proceeds through input validation without another quote or sale. Historical standalone Assembly retains its accepted per-job quote. Phaeno Finance uses manual accounting source records outside the Partner workspace to prepare invoices and journal entries; the portal does not collect payment-card information.

sections.heading: Troubleshoot common problems
sections.text: Cannot place a PSeq Kit order: confirm the Partner organization, organization-administrator role, active offering, quantity rules, shipping address, and purchase-order number. Cannot accept a quote: confirm it is the current issued, unexpired quote and that you are a Partner administrator. Upload rejected: compare the file name, type, size, and metadata with the assembly profile. Remove an incorrect saved input through Edit request → Input files before adding a replacement. Do not repeatedly upload a file rejected by scanning. Output missing: check output review, scan, release, and payment states separately. Order changed while open: refresh and review the latest version before attempting the action again. Shipment incomplete: review shipped and remaining quantities; a partial shipment can leave backordered units open. For support, provide the portal order or assembly reference, visible status, and last-action time. Do not send credentials, tokens, confidential data files, or customer information in a support message.

guides.title: Trial history
guides.summary: Find preserved Trial scope, results, and retention receipts after conversion.

sections.heading: Trial history after Partner conversion
sections.text: If your organization previously had a Prospect Trial Project, Trial projects preserves the approved scope, samples, customer-safe progress, releases, and history in the original department. Active authorized members may view that history under the same organization identity. For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures. Keep PHI and sample identity mappings outside the Portal. A Trial release archive includes its approved scope/file manifest. Partner conversion does not reopen a Trial or authorize new Trial samples. Partner reagent orders and data-assembly requests use their own workflows and permissions. Trial results are not subject to Partner pricing or payment gates. Open Retention and receipt for the original release policy and download history. Conversion does not extend file retention or grace dates. After complete release, earlier partial archives direct you to the complete package. Download controls show progress and explain unavailable files, including closed retention access; the workspace refreshes after a transfer. Download available files before the displayed deadline. Withdrawn, held, or deleted files remain unavailable; retained history does not restore deleted bytes. Contact Phaeno with the Trial number if a reissue is needed.

guides.title: Configuration and file retention
guides.summary: Maintain reusable defaults, services, analyses, Partner rules, shipping container sizes and compatibility, and released-file retention.

sections.heading: Configuration and file retention
sections.text: Open the user dropdown menu, then choose Administration → Order settings. Order settings controls the active scientific, Partner, commercial, release, and integration rules used by new work. Changes must be audited and should not rewrite immutable order snapshots. The separate File retention policies page, after Order settings, Lab settings, CRM settings, and Samples & shipping settings in the user menu, controls the retention policy used by future released result and output packages. Only a Phaeno platform administrator can change these settings. Use the far-left Order settings sidebar to move among Quote & workflow, Service catalog, Analyses, PSeq kits, Assembly, and Legacy links. Scientific service definitions are managed inside their catalog item. On wider screens the sidebar can remain pinned; when it is unpinned or the screen is narrow, open the same non-modal navigation from the edge tab. The selected subject appears in the main pane without duplicating the navigation above the configuration form.

sections.heading: Maintain commercial configuration
sections.text: Maintain active billable items under Service catalog. Open an item's name, select Edit item, set Status to Active or Inactive, and select Save item. Active items are available for new pricing; existing orders retain their saved details. You can also change the name, description, base price, and currency. Use Add item and choose Item type. PSeq Lab Service supplies its required permanent reference and fixes Sales unit to Per specimen. If that item already exists, edit it rather than creating another. Other catalog item receives an automatic permanent reference; choose Per specimen, Per kit, Per item, Per service, or an existing catalog unit to identify what one unit of its base price covers. References remain unchanged when items are renamed and can be viewed under Reference details on the item page. Link these Phaeno-owned items to analyses, Partner reagent offerings, or assembly profiles. The designated laboratory-service item must use the permanent code pseq-lab-service, the sales unit specimen, and an active state. The catalog identifies it as PSeq Lab Service. POMS blocks laboratory quote issuance when this exact item is missing, inactive, or uses another unit; an unrelated specimen fee cannot replace it. Configure Partner PSeq Kit availability, negotiated bundle price, currency, effective period, whole-unit quantity rules and shipping restrictions. Bind each active Kit offering to an active, validated included Assembly profile. Each unit creates one included case at purchase; existing orders keep their frozen profile and outputs. Overlapping active price periods for the same Partner and item are not allowed. Historical credit and accounting links are retained under Legacy links. Partner Assembly payment gates remain in its owning workflow. PSeq Customer result release depends on scientific approval and the Result Release Manager; invoice balance and credit do not gate it. Customer billing, tax, invoices and cash are maintained in Order Ops → Finance. Open Quote & workflow → Edit settings to maintain quote validity and review the supported sample and result workflows. The initial quote validity is 30 days, and an issued quote snapshots its own expiration. The supported sample workflow uses an exact roster after quote acceptance; the supported result destination is governed Portal delivery. Free-form configuration text no longer establishes readiness. Review and save older workflow settings once, then maintain shared definitions in Samples & shipping settings → Sample types and destinations and rules in Samples & shipping settings. Each order and shipment still checks its specific requirements.

sections.heading: Maintain a service's scientific definition
sections.text: Open Service catalog → PSeq Lab Service and review Scientific definition beneath the commercial details. This defines the included analyses, supported sample-type revisions, biological sources, outputs, published minimum and maximum turnaround, availability dates, and active state. The price comes from the parent catalog item. Use Add definition when none exists; otherwise use a version's Actions → Create new version. New definitions and versions start inactive. Activate only approved, complete definitions. Synthetic definitions cannot be purchased. Select the supported sample types. New shipment preparation and service availability follow their latest active, effective revisions; existing commitments retain the sample identity and accepted commercial terms. Samples & shipping settings → Sample types maintains reusable definitions; a globally active type or matching shipping rule does not automatically make it supported by a service. Materials follow the selected types. Current configured PSeq ordering requires exactly one supported extracted-RNA tube type; assigning other types does not enable a new intake workflow. Kit and Assembly configuration remain in their own settings pages. Each item has one current scientific definition, with prior versions retained. A scientific version cannot move to another catalog item. Actions → Edit availability changes when an existing version can be selected. Publishing a new active version closes overlapping prior availability for that item; editing availability cannot introduce an overlap. Older definitions without explicit sample assignments show Review required and cannot be selected for new configured orders. Create a new version, review the supported sample types, and activate the approved definition. Existing accepted orders retain their saved version, scope, price, tax, and shipment instructions. New configured commitments also freeze supported sample-type revision IDs. If that revision becomes unavailable before a new shipment is authorized, staff must review the shipping configuration; POMS will not silently substitute an unrelated type. Legacy and manually quoted commitments keep their existing shipping checks. After a concurrent configuration change, a failed save retains your edits and refreshes saved values where available. Review the latest terms before retrying. Closing an editor with unsaved changes asks whether to discard them.

sections.heading: Maintain scientific configuration
sections.text: Analysis definitions describe required Customer sample fields, instructions, expected outputs, and linked quoteable items. Assembly profiles describe Partner metadata, allowed files, validation, expected output contract, availability, and linked quoteable items. Deactivate configuration that must not be used for new work. Existing orders keep their accepted definitions, profile versions, prices, currency, and commercial snapshots.

sections.heading: Maintain sample-shipping configuration
sections.text: The ship-to destinations in this configuration are laboratory receiving locations for samples sent to Phaeno. Customer delivery addresses for outbound kits are maintained separately under the Customer's Departments → Delivery locations. Confirmed kit orders retain their saved address even when a delivery-location record changes later. Open Administration → Samples & shipping settings, after CRM settings in the user dropdown menu. Its sidebar opens separate pages for Sample types, Ship-to destinations, Shipping procedures, Shipping assignments, Container sizes, and Order submission guidance. List titles, descriptions, create actions, and available filters sit in shaded headers. The settings maintain these controlled record sets: ship-to destinations with the full address, receiving team, receiving hours and time zone, closure guidance, delivery directions, and carrier restrictions; sample types with material, quantity, primary-container, preservation, customer-label, prohibited-identifier, safety and transit requirements; reusable Shipping procedures with common packing, transit, carrier, dispatch, required-document, exception and optional customs steps; Shipping assignments linking a sample type and exact destination revision to an approved procedure revision, plus compatibility grouping and optional destination-specific additions; and container sizes with a fixed SKU, name, usable tube capacity and approved sample/assignment combinations. Each combination has its own temperature-control instructions and packing steps. Follow the Setup guide: where each instruction belongs when configuring a new sample. Add a sample type and destination, approve the common procedure, create their shipping assignment, then configure the container combinations. Missing prerequisites link directly to the relevant screen. Manage assignments from a sample detail keeps that sample selected. Create a named procedure once, review it, and mark its revision approved before selecting it in an assignment. Assignments keep that exact revision. To adopt a later procedure, create a new assignment revision and review the container combinations that use it. Existing standalone instructions remain available for reviewed conversion; the Portal does not automatically combine scientific text. Temperature control is flexible. Specify the approved method, amount, units and preparation for each sample/container combination: regular ice, dry ice, cold packs, another method, or explicitly no cooling. Amounts can differ by container size. New procedure-based combinations require temperature-control and packing instructions before activation and packet issuance. Mixed samples must share one approved temperature-control instruction for that container; the Portal never sums amounts per sample or calculates them from tube capacity. Use separate containers if the requirements conflict. Specify the amount for one complete container, not an amount to add for every sample. Destination codes are generated automatically when you add a ship-to destination. Enter its display name; the permanent reference is retained if you rename it or create a revision. New records default to inactive. Activate a revision only after the address and scientific and operational instructions are approved. Selecting Create revision copies the current content into a new record; it does not rewrite history or any packet snapshot already issued. A new active revision replaces its predecessor when it becomes effective. Use Add sample type and enter its Name and approved handling requirements. Its permanent reference is generated automatically; you do not enter a sample-type code. Select Total RNA or Enriched RNA under Material type to match the submitted material. Revisions retain previously saved material values unless you explicitly change them. The compact Quantity card describes submitted items. Use Units beneath Submission unit to insert µL or mL at the cursor, preserving the surrounding text. For example, insert mL between 20 and tube to make 20 mL tube. You can also type a submission description directly. Min defaults to 1; Max is optional. Enter positive whole-number counts, and leave Max blank for no upper limit. Max cannot be below Min. The size in “20 mL tube” describes the container; the count describes how many are submitted. The helper is limited to these two size units and contains no symbol-insertion options. Renaming a sample type in a new revision preserves the reference, and existing references are retained. Each sample-type instruction field has a Units and symbols helper: primary-container, preservation, stabilizer, customer label, prohibited identifiers and safety. Earlier packaging and carrier text is retained when revising existing samples. Choose from volume, mass, concentration, length, temperature, time, percentage, centrifugation and pressure units, or scientific symbols such as ±, ≤, ≥ and µ. A selection inserts at the cursor or replaces only highlighted text, then returns focus to the instruction. Existing surrounding text is preserved. Saving a sample-type definition does not by itself enable it for a service or change ordering and pricing. Current configured PSeq intake uses its supported registered tubes. Submission quantities describe the physical material; ordering and pricing count sample-sequencing runs. In Samples & shipping settings → Sample types, open a sample type's name to see its dedicated detail page. It shows the scientific requirements, quantity and transit limits, availability and revision history. Shipping & packing shows current destination assignments, linked shared procedures and approved containers with their specific packing and temperature-control details. Earlier shipping text remains available for review. Copy the page address to share a link with another authorized Phaeno administrator; the link always opens that exact revision. Select a revision in the history to review it, or use View latest revision from an older page. Actions → Create revision on the latest page opens the revision editor. Saving opens the new revision's details; Back to sample types returns to the list. For Sample types, Ship-to destinations, and Shipping assignments, use Actions → Activate or Deactivate to change availability. Confirm the selected revision; its revision number and content remain unchanged, and the status change is recorded in the audit history. Create revision is for changed requirements, addresses or instructions. New content revisions start inactive. An earlier active revision stays available until you activate its successor or explicitly deactivate it. When a newer draft exists, its Actions menu also offers Deactivate revision N for an earlier approved revision. Activation is available on the latest revision that has not ended. A future start remains scheduled; activating a draft whose start is in the past takes effect now. Deactivation stops new use without restoring an older revision. Existing issued packets keep their recorded information. Before activating a shipping assignment, its exact destination revision, a current sample-type revision and its selected shipping procedure must be active at activation time. The confirmation explains missing prerequisites and links to the relevant setup. For example, activate an inactive destination under Ship-to destinations, then return to activate the saved assignment. An ended destination requires a new assignment linked to a current destination revision. If a status change fails because another administrator changed the record, refresh the configuration and review the latest values before retrying. The Container sizes list supports search and status filtering. Open a common name to review its details and revision history. Use Add container size or Create revision for bounded changes. The SKU stays fixed across revisions, including leading zeros and separators. Saving an inactive container revision creates a draft and leaves the preceding active revision available. To stop an active revision from future selection, open its detail page and choose Actions → Deactivate revision. Existing kits and manifests retain the container facts recorded when they were prepared. In the size editor, select the approved sample/assignment combinations and enter each combination's temperature-control and packing instructions. Expand Supplier details to optionally select a supplier and its product number from the catalog. Choices include active suppliers and their active shipping-container products with active product types. Changing or clearing the supplier clears the product selection. Manage these choices in Lab Operations → Suppliers & products. An older reference that is no longer an active catalog choice stays visible as a saved reference; keep it unchanged, or clear it and choose a replacement. Earlier container notes appears only when previous notes exist; review and clear any text that duplicates the combination instructions. New containers do not ask for a second general packing instruction. Existing details and validation errors open that section automatically. Availability groups the effective dates and activation setting. Use Preview recommendation to enter a tube count, select the exact sample and destination assignment, and optionally enter available quantities. Blank quantities mean availability is unknown; zero excludes that size. The result favors fewer containers, then less unused capacity, and shows any unallocated tubes. A preview from a container detail page can include that draft revision. Previewing does not reserve stock, create a shipment, or estimate shipping cost. When adding a shipping assignment, select Sample type by name. Beneath the selector, Currently using revision N · Active identifies the version used now. Inactive, ended and future-dated versions are excluded. If no revision is currently active, shipping instructions cannot be issued. Saving an inactive sample-type revision leaves the existing active revision available. When an approved successor becomes effective, rules and container compatibility follow it automatically for new shipment preparation; quantity and unit requirements are checked again at packet issuance. Already-issued packets retain their recorded sample revision and instructions. The destination remains tied to an exact revision, so a changed destination still requires a rule for that destination revision. Compatibility group is a shared handling label, such as FROZEN_RNA for frozen RNA. Reuse a group only for sample types approved to share a shipment. Different groups cannot be combined, and This sample type must have a separate shipment packet prevents combination even when the groups match. Choose an existing suggestion or enter the approved label; it is not a unique generated reference. On Shipping assignments, choose a rule's Actions → Preview shared steps. The read-only preview opens automatically for that destination and sample type, using the current time or the rule's exact start time if it starts in the future. Inactive or ended rules cannot resolve a preview. Expand Add sample types to check a combined shipment; the original sample type stays included. POMS displays the shared ship-to and preparation requirements. Review container-specific details through the sample's Shipping & packing section. An issued packet combines and freezes those details for its actual container. If a required combination rule is missing, compatibility groups differ, or a type requires its own package, POMS blocks a combined preview so the work can be corrected or split. Use Actions → Create revision to revise an instruction rule. This configuration is shared infrastructure only. It does not create a Prospect Trial Project, grant a Customer promotion, place an order, or activate any real destination or sample type on its own. Prepare and register standard kits in Lab operations → Receipt & accession → Prepare kits before supplying them to Customer locations. Staff choose a configured container size, record the actual tube and shipper products, register the full configured tube capacity, print the permanent container barcode, and record outbound dispatch against the delivery request. The Customer confirms arrival into location inventory and assigns each physical container to a Job during preparation. Previously prepared shipment-specific kits remain in Kits sent. These records retain product and lot facts, permanent tube identities, and outbound tracking. Qualify the physical tubes, container fit, seals, temperature handling, and readable barcodes before using a container size operationally. Order submission guidance are general guidance copied to new lab orders when customer-specific instructions are not configured. Maintain them in Samples & shipping settings → Order submission guidance → Edit instructions. They are still required for order readiness. Existing orders keep their saved text. Use it to explain sample entry and where to find shipment instructions. Keep scientific requirements, receiving details and packing steps in their owning records instead of copying them here. Saving guidance preserves quote and workflow settings.

sections.heading: Maintain released-deliverable retention
sections.text: Open Administration → File retention policies to review or edit the global released-deliverable policy. The starting values are 30 days of standard retention, one undownloaded-package warning 5 days before the standard deadline, and a conditional 5-day grace period when any released file remains undownloaded at that deadline. Every value is a positive whole number of exact 24-hour days, and the warning lead must be shorter than standard retention. Enter a reason for every change. A new revision applies only to packages released afterward; it never changes a deadline already communicated for an existing release. Prior revisions remain visible in policy history. To configure a Company-specific policy, open the Customer, Partner, or Prospect in CRM Companies, open Services, select Retention, and add an override. Leave any value blank to inherit that value from the current global policy. The page shows the effective value and source for each field. Removing an override restores global inheritance for future releases and also requires a reason. Retention editors retain the policy revision and inherited values shown when you opened them. A background refresh does not replace the values you are reviewing. If another administrator changes the policy before you save, the save is rejected; close the editor, reload the policy, and review the current values before editing again. Unsaved edits require confirmation before closing or leaving. While a save is underway, editing and dismissal pause. A failed save keeps your entries and shows the error in the dialog; Retry reloads a failed policy view. Customer laboratory-result and Partner data-assembly output releases freeze the effective policy version and exact UTC warning, standard-deletion, and potential final-deletion times in the same transaction as release. Their authorized external detail views show the standard deadline and label the later date as conditional until grace is actually activated. Repeated payment events preserve the first release time. An older release without captured retention dates shows no automated schedule; do not infer a deadline from today's policy. Released-file and full-package ZIP downloads retain their attempt and outcome. Only a complete successful transfer counts toward the retention condition. Partial downloads, failures, cancellations, and timeouts do not count. Older download records without verified completion remain in history and do not become successful downloads merely because the record exists. Governed PSeq packages use the same frozen policy and verified-download rules. Downloads obey their deadline independently of cleanup, and existing schedules retain their original dates. Automated notices and physical file deletion depend on the enabled retention services. Check the receipt for their recorded outcomes; a closed download window does not prove that files were deleted.

sections.heading: Accounting and recovery
sections.text: Use Order Ops → Finance for native PSeq invoices, receipts, allocations, imports, aging and reconciliation. Export reports from the owning Finance view. An export does not record payment or mark an invoice as posted elsewhere. Historical connector mappings and explicit QuickBooks catalog recovery remain in Legacy links. A queued recovery request does not prove that the connector is configured or that the catalog synchronized. An unconfigured connector reports unavailable and Needs attention; it records no invoice, payment, or successful balance. The active Service catalog can be maintained directly. Consult the owning integration recovery status before retrying a historical connector operation.

sections.heading: Activate production dependencies
sections.text: Before production use, confirm approved storage and malware scanning, notification delivery, active catalog and scientific profiles, Partner offerings and prices, applicable Partner credit decisions, quote validity, Finance responsibility, and operational ownership. Laboratory activation also requires approved bench workflows, label/printer/scanner and degraded-mode procedures, external NGS provider operating details, and approved operating procedures. Use only the equipment, destinations, and procedures authorized for real work.

sections.heading: Recover a retention notice
sections.text: Filter Owned attention queues to Retention notices. An urgent item identifies the package, deadline, and notification requiring recovery. Confirm active Organization administrators, correct the delivery issue, and retry the existing notification. A later grace notice uses the original final date. Resolution does not extend retention or confirm physical deletion; a persisting delivery failure can reopen the item.

sections.heading: Preserve a release or record a reissue
sections.text: A Phaeno platform administrator can open File retention policies → Review released packages, find the organization, and open a package's retained receipt. The detail page shows its full manifest, checksums, original retention dates, download evidence, cleanup outcome and reissue history. Use Print / save PDF for a metadata copy. A historical release may lack captured sample lineage; do not infer missing facts. Choose Place hold, select the hold type, and record the reason. Preserve bytes blocks physical cleanup. Quarantine and suspend access also stops current transfers and blocks new downloads; it is available only where download monitoring is active. Neither action resets retention. Hold reasons remain in the Phaeno management view rather than the external receipt. Use Release hold with a reason when preservation is no longer needed. If the original deadline has passed, cleanup may proceed once every hold is released and active transfer leases have ended. A stale-record error refreshes the details and preserves your entered reason; review the current state before retrying. After deletion, first regenerate and approve a new package through the owning scientific workflow. Then open the old receipt and choose Link reissued package, select the eligible new release, and record the authorization reason. POMS requires the same organization, workflow and sample where applicable, new file objects, and a release created after the original deletion. Linking never restores deleted bytes or changes the original release dates. Cleanup can remain pending for active transfers, preservation, shared source files, an incomplete package, or provider failure. Provider failures are retried against the same objects. Files deleted records successful physical cleanup; Downloads closed alone does not. Escalate repeated failures with the package reference and safe status, without copying credentials or scientific files.

guides.title: Customer relationship management
guides.summary: Manage canonical Companies, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, Portal access, Tasks, reporting, and data quality.

sections.heading: Customer relationship management
sections.text: The POMS CRM is Phaeno's first-party commercial and customer system of record. It runs without HubSpot or another external CRM and retains Companies, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, Activities, Tasks, pipeline history, reporting, Portal access, and reviewed handoffs in POMS. CRM records are internal Phaeno records. The Company is the canonical Customer, Partner, or Prospect identity. Creating it does not grant membership, activate a service, authorize ordering, start laboratory work, or expose scientific data.

sections.heading: Access CRM
sections.text: Open CRM from the Phaeno toolbar while working in the Phaeno organization. An active Phaeno account with the Commercial operator role or platform-administrator access can use CRM. External organization users cannot see CRM navigation or CRM data. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move among the CRM sections available to your role. Relationships contains Companies and People; Sales contains Leads and Opportunities; Follow-up contains Tasks and, for administrators, Requests; Insights contains Reports. Administrators open Administration → CRM settings from the user dropdown, immediately below Lab settings, for CRM configuration. Home remains the starting summary. The sidebar header identifies CRM and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar from the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar.

sections.heading: Start from Home
sections.text: Home separates follow-up checks from your next Tasks and recently changed Opportunities. When all visible counts are zero, it says No items need attention. Categories with matching records are highlighted and offer Review to open their queue; zero-count categories remain neutral. Each category explains its rule: unfinished overdue or due-soon Tasks, active Leads without a next action, and open Opportunities unchanged for more than 30 days. Administrators also see possible duplicates and missing required custom-field values under Data warnings. Recently changed Opportunities are shown separately for reference. A missing Opportunity amount alone does not trigger an attention warning. Use Find anything to search active Companies, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, and Tasks. Enter at least two characters, then choose a result to open its owning workspace. Search does not cross into Portal users, specimens, files, or laboratory records. Commercial staff can maintain Companies, Contacts, relationships, Leads, Opportunities, Tasks, ordinary Internal Activities, personal saved views, and Internal custom values, and read Reports. A platform administrator manages Company and Contact deactivation/reactivation and merges, Portal identity and access, Company Requests, pipelines and field definitions, imports, exports, shared-view publication, and Restricted Activities and custom values. Administrative sections and actions are shown only to administrators.

sections.heading: Keep the domain boundaries clear
sections.text: CRM owns the canonical Company, commercial relationship facts, qualification, pursuits, follow-up, sales history, and the central Requests review queue. Company detail presents the internal tenant scope, memberships, invitations, readiness, and service entitlements after Portal access is enabled. That scope is not a second customer record. Order operations owns commercial orders, quotes, cancellation and hold decisions, Finance, and governed result publication. Lab operations owns physical fulfillment, laboratory execution, and scientific approval. Lab operations owns physical specimens, accession, controlled execution, materials, equipment, libraries, batches, sendouts, exceptions, and scientific approval. Use a reviewed CRM handoff when relationship context should enable or change Portal access or enter Order operations. Never copy patient information, sample identifiers, scientific results, credentials, confidential file contents, or internal laboratory investigation notes into CRM. Use the CRM subtopics in this guide for complete field, status, workflow, administration, handoff, and recovery instructions.

guides.title: Activities and Tasks
guides.summary: Record commercial interactions and manage owned, recurring follow-up in record context.

sections.heading: Activities and Tasks
sections.text: Company, Contact, Lead, and Opportunity workspaces contain one commercial activity timeline and a linked Task list. Record work in the owning record so its context remains visible.

sections.heading: Log an Activity
sections.text: Select Log activity from the record workspace. Choose Note, Call, Meeting, Email, or Status change; enter the required subject and optional details. POMS records the current time and signed-in actor. Choose visibility deliberately: Internal is ordinary Phaeno commercial context. Restricted is available only to platform administrators. Commercial staff cannot read, create, edit, or deactivate Restricted Activities. Keep confidential procedures and scientific evidence in their authorized owning system. Manually logged Email means a user recorded that an email occurred. It does not send or retrieve email. Connected email and calendar capture are deferred. System, Portal, and Task events may also appear in the timeline. They are written by POMS and cannot be edited as ordinary notes. Never place patient information, sample identifiers, credentials, scientific results, file contents, or laboratory investigation detail in an Activity.

sections.heading: Create a Task
sections.text: Select New task from the owning record. A title is required. Add a description, active Phaeno owner, priority, due date and time, reminder, and optional daily, weekly, or monthly recurrence. Priorities are Low, Normal, High, and Urgent. Use them to communicate commercial urgency, not scientific or patient severity. A Task must be linked to a Company, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity; the standalone Tasks workspace intentionally does not create context-free Tasks.

sections.heading: Manage the Task queue
sections.text: Open Tasks from the CRM sidebar to search by title or description, filter by status, overdue state, or due within seven days, page through results, and apply saved views. Administrators can also export the current view. Search and filters remain when you return from a record. Statuses are: Open: not started. In progress: actively owned. Blocked: unable to proceed; a reason is required. Completed: finished. Cancelled: intentionally stopped. Use Actions > Edit task in the queue or a related record's Task list to change the title, description, owner, priority, due date, or reminder. Commercial staff and administrators can edit Open, In progress, and Blocked Tasks. Dates and times use the time zone shown in the editor. Review the reminder when moving the due date: it stays at its existing time unless you change it, and cannot be later than the due date. Select Save changes to apply the edit. Rescheduling keeps the current status and related record, and updates overdue and due-soon views. The linked record's Activity timeline records who edited the Task and when, including the previous and new due date, reminder, owner, and priority when those values change. If another user changes the Task while you are editing, POMS refreshes its saved values and retains your edited fields. Review the latest values before saving again. If the Task was completed or cancelled, it can no longer be edited. Use Actions > Update status to change status. A blocked Task requires the blocking reason. Completed and Cancelled Tasks retain their history and cannot be edited, rescheduled, or reopened. Create a new follow-up Task when more work is needed. Completing a recurring Task creates its next occurrence from the current due date using the same daily, weekly, or monthly interval, reminder offset, details, and owner. Rescheduling therefore shifts the next occurrence too; it is not an exception to a separate fixed schedule. Keep a due date on recurring Tasks. The edit dialog preserves the existing recurrence interval. Confirm the new occurrence and due date rather than changing the completed historical Task.

sections.heading: Use Home attention safely
sections.text: CRM Home shows overdue Tasks, Tasks due within seven days, and your next assigned Tasks. Completing a Task from Home uses the same durable status transition as the record workspace. If the Task has changed since Home loaded, refresh before retrying so a newer owner's work is not overwritten. Selecting an attention card opens its matching filtered list. Overdue Tasks are unfinished Tasks due before now; Due in 7 days includes unfinished Tasks due from now through the next seven days. Leads needing a next action excludes Converted and Disqualified Leads. Stale Opportunities are active, open Opportunities unchanged for more than 30 days, across all pipelines. The list shows these filters and lets you clear or save them. A failed Home search offers Retry CRM search results; no matches is shown only after a successful search.

guides.title: Companies and Contacts
guides.summary: Maintain Company identity, contextual People, relationships, invitations, and Portal access in one workspace.

sections.heading: Companies and People
sections.text: Companies and Contacts are durable relationship records. The Company is also the canonical Customer, Partner, or Prospect identity. A Company does not become accessible to external users until Portal access is reviewed and enabled; a Contact never becomes a Portal user automatically. Commercial staff can maintain identity, ownership, Company relationships, Sales, and ordinary Activity. Company People shows Contact relationships for Commercial staff. Portal identities, invitations, memberships, Departments, Services, Requests, merge, and Company/Contact deactivation or reactivation are administrator-only.

sections.heading: Create and find a Company
sections.text: Open Companies from the CRM sidebar. Search by the known organization identity and review possible duplicates before selecting New company at the right end of the Company directory header. Creating a Company alone does not grant access or start work. Company name is required; Website and relationship stage remain visible for quick entry. Open Additional details only when you need to record: an explicit normalized domain; when left blank, POMS derives it from Website source, industry, employee count, phone, and postal address tags and a relationship summary Company, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and Task lists show total counts and pages. Searches update after a short pause; Clear all resets active filters. Opening a record and using its Back link retains the list search, filters, and page. Company sections remain in the URL. POMS assigns the creator as owner unless another supported owner is selected later. The Company name opens a stable, view-first workspace. Its header Actions menu contains Change owner, Edit, and, for administrators, Merge and Deactivate or Reactivate. Each opens the existing review or editing dialog. Use Overview for the Company profile and custom data, People for Contacts and Portal identity/access state, Sales for Opportunities, Departments for department settings, membership and delivery locations, Services for readiness, entitlements and retention, Requests for request creation and history, and Activity for the commercial timeline and Tasks. Use CRM's central Requests queue for approve, decline, recovery, application, and completion decisions. Changing a CRM lifecycle to Active customer or Partner is descriptive only. It does not enable or reclassify Portal access, grant membership, activate services, or authorize orders. Company and Contact editors keep your entered details when the record refreshes in the background. Company ownership and deactivate/reactivate confirmations also retain the record you reviewed. If saving reports that the record changed, your entries remain available; review the current record before making another attempt. Closing and reopening an editor starts from the latest loaded details. For a Company edit conflict, POMS loads the current Company and shows changed details. If that read fails, select Retry current record. Compare the current values with your retained entries, then select Use reviewed record before deliberately saving again. This does not save automatically. While saving, the editor protects against repeated submission, dismissal and navigation. Cancelling an edited draft asks before discarding it. If the response was interrupted, refresh and inspect the saved Company before repeating the change.

sections.heading: Create and manage a Contact
sections.text: From a Company’s People section, select New person to create the Contact and its Company association together. The global Contacts directory also provides New contact when no Company context is available. First name and last name are required. Record email, phone, Phaeno owner, and tags. Sales and marketing outreach shows a separate decision: Not established means staff have not recorded a supported outreach decision. Allowed means staff have recorded the supporting source, evidence date, and explanation of the outreach covered for this email address. Suppressed records an unsubscribe, direct request to stop, or internal restriction. Select Record or update outreach decision only when making that decision. Choose its status and supporting source, enter the evidence date and an explanation of its scope, and give a reason for suppression. Saving an email or other profile detail does not establish permission. Changing an Allowed email resets the decision to Not established unless you explicitly record a new decision for the replacement address. Cancelling an edited draft asks whether to discard it; a failed save retains your entries. The Contact workspace and directory show the current outreach status. The Activity timeline retains each changed decision, its previous and new evidence, and the staff member and time. System history cannot be edited or deactivated. Contact exports include the status and evidence. Earlier Opted out and Do not contact values appear as Suppressed. Earlier Permitted values need evidence review before appearing as Allowed; historical values and contact-basis text remain retained. These decisions are recorded for staff reference. CRM does not currently send sales or marketing outreach, and this setting does not automatically block messages sent through other tools. Staff must check the current decision before using an external sending tool. Requested Portal invitations, order updates, results, and security messages are managed separately. Requesting a Portal invitation does not grant sales or marketing permission. A Contact is not a Portal user. Email equality does not link identities, issue an invitation, or grant access. From a Company’s People section, use Invite to Portal for a reviewed Contact and choose Organization-administrator or explicit Department access. The Actions menu for each person separates these tasks: Manage access changes active membership and Department roles; pending or expired invitations have separate Edit invited access, Resend invite, and Revoke invite dialogs. Successful acceptance creates the Portal membership and the explicit Contact/User identity link. If POMS finds an existing Portal user with the same email, it shows Identity review; select Review and link, verify that both records identify the same person, and record the reason. Never treat the suggestion as proof. Unlinked Portal users and invitations remain visible until staff intentionally resolve them. The Invite to Portal dialog shows the reviewed Contact and Company as a recipient summary. Under Access after acceptance, review the role descriptions and selected Departments; the indented administrator option applies only to its Department. Send invitation sends the email invitation. It does not immediately grant Portal access. For a Member, selecting no Department disables Send invitation and immediately explains that at least one Department is required.

sections.heading: Associate Contacts and Companies
sections.text: Open either record workspace to create the association: use Add existing person in the Company's People section to search incrementally for an existing Contact, or use Associate in the Contact's Company relationships area to search incrementally for an existing Company. Record the Contact's free-form job title at that Company and choose the relationship role—Decision maker, Scientific lead, Procurement, Executive sponsor, Champion, Influencer, Technical evaluator, or Other—then record whether this is the Contact's primary Company and the effective-from date. A Contact may be associated with more than one Company, with a different title and relationship role at each. In Add existing person, Escape first closes open search choices and keeps your draft. Dismissing an edited form, or leaving the page, asks whether to discard unsaved changes. Decline to keep the draft; a discarded form opens fresh next time. Job title and relationship role are intentionally different. Job title is the person's organization-specific position, such as Director of Genomics, and remains free-form. Relationship role describes how the person participates in the commercial relationship and uses the controlled choices above. The Contacts directory displays the title and Company from the active primary relationship. Each relationship remains visible from the Company's People section and the Contact's Company relationships card. When a title, role, primary designation, or effective date changes, edit the Company relationship rather than the Contact's identity. When a relationship ends, record an effective-to date. Do not delete the Contact or overwrite the former Company simply to hide historical employment. POMS retains the effective-dated relationship and marks ended rows consistently in both workspaces.

sections.heading: Deactivate, reactivate, and merge
sections.text: Deactivate a Company or Contact when it should leave active directories while its history remains available. Reactivation restores the same CRM identity. Deactivating a Company suspends its attached Portal access scope; reactivating restores it. Contact lifecycle actions do not change Portal users. On the Contact workspace, Deactivate or Reactivate opens a confirmation naming the Contact. Review it before confirming; Cancel leaves the Contact unchanged. If the change fails, the dialog shows the error. Manage this person's Portal membership and invitations separately from Company People. Use Merge only for a confirmed duplicate: Open the duplicate record that should be retired. Search the active Company or Contact directory and choose the record that should remain authoritative. The duplicate you opened is excluded from the choices. Record a required merge reason. Review the consequence and confirm. The merge dialog names the record being retired. A failed search offers Retry; a failed merge keeps the selected target and reason for review. Leaving an edited merge draft asks whether to discard the choices, and the dialog stays open while a merge is being processed. If another user changes the source record, reload and review the current version before submitting again. POMS retains the source as an inactive alias, moves supported relationships and history, and writes a permanent merge record. If only one Company has Portal access, that access scope follows the surviving Company. POMS blocks a merge when both Companies have Portal access because choosing the surviving tenant requires an explicit data decision. Ordinary CRM UI does not undo a merge. If the records describe different legal entities or people, do not merge them; correct their fields or effective-dated relationships instead. Contact merging preserves suppression if either record is suppressed. It does not transfer an Allowed decision from the retired Contact to a different surviving email address.

sections.heading: Complete required custom data
sections.text: Active custom fields configured for Company or Contact appear in the record workspace; Company custom fields are under Overview. Option fields accept only configured choices. A missing required value is shown on the record and contributes to CRM Home data-quality warnings. Complete the value on the authoritative record rather than suppressing the warning with unrelated text.

sections.heading: Create an Opportunity from its Company
sections.text: Open Sales and select New opportunity. The shared Opportunity form retains this Company, so you can capture the pursuit without leaving its workspace. The resulting record appears in Company Sales and the global Opportunity list.

guides.title: Leads and conversion
guides.summary: Capture signals, record qualification decisions, and convert without granting Portal access.

sections.heading: Leads and conversion
sections.text: Use a Lead for an unqualified commercial signal that is not yet ready to become a durable Company, Contact, or Opportunity.

sections.heading: Capture the Lead
sections.text: Open Leads and select New lead. Choose Individual or Company and enter the required display name. A Company Lead also requires a company name. Add contact facts, source, owner, next action, and tags when known. Do not create a Contact merely because an email address arrived, and do not create a Company merely because a web domain was observed. The Lead preserves the original signal while qualification is incomplete. Lead statuses are: New: captured but not yet worked. Working: active follow-up has begun. Qualified: the signal is suitable for conversion. Disqualified: the signal will not proceed; the reason is retained. Converted: the selected CRM records were created or linked and the original Lead is immutable history. Use status and search filters to find the relevant queue. All statuses includes converted history; select Converted to reopen a completed Lead and its recorded results. Save a view when the same filter supports recurring work.

sections.heading: Qualify or disqualify
sections.text: Open the Lead and use its Actions menu to edit it or change its status. Select Start working before active follow-up when it is still New. Qualification and disqualification require an explanation so another Phaeno user can understand the decision. The full-width Qualification record shows only the applicable decision: qualification notes for Qualified or Converted Leads, the disqualification reason for Disqualified Leads, or a concise pending state while no decision exists. Qualify only when the organization or person, commercial fit, and next action are understood well enough to avoid speculative records. Disqualify when follow-up should stop; record the actual commercial reason without protected scientific or patient information.

sections.heading: Convert a qualified Lead
sections.text: Select Actions > Convert lead from a Qualified Lead. Review each requested result: choose an existing Company or Create company in the Company dropdown; No company supports a Contact-only conversion optionally create a Contact optionally create an Opportunity in an active pipeline If an existing Company is chosen, POMS links conversion to that CRM identity. Create company uses the Lead's recorded company name when available. If the Lead has no company name, enter the required Company name in the conversion modal. This names the new Company without changing the original Lead's captured details. Opportunity creation requires an existing or new Company and uses the selected or default active pipeline. Likely Company or Contact duplicates stop unsafe creation or are returned as warnings. Review the suggested records and retry with an existing authoritative identity when appropriate. Do not alter spelling or identifying data merely to bypass duplicate detection. Conversion records the resulting Company, Contact, and Opportunity identifiers on the original Lead. It never enables Portal access or creates a user, entitlement, order, shipment, or Lab work order.

sections.heading: Correct mistakes safely
sections.text: Converted and Disqualified Leads are terminal for ordinary editing. Preserve them as decision history. If commercial work later resumes, use the resulting records or create a new Lead that represents the genuinely new signal; do not rewrite the old decision. If a save reports stale data, reload the Lead, review the newer change, and submit a deliberate update. If conversion partially appears to have succeeded, refresh the Lead and open its recorded conversion results before retrying.

guides.title: Opportunities and pipelines
guides.summary: Run commercial pursuits through controlled stages, immutable history, and currency-safe reporting.

sections.heading: Opportunities and pipelines
sections.text: An Opportunity represents one commercial pursuit for one CRM Company. It is not an order, quote, entitlement, or promise that Phaeno will perform work.

sections.heading: Create an Opportunity
sections.text: Open Opportunities and select New opportunity. Record the required Opportunity name, Company, and active pipeline. POMS assigns a unique, read-only Opportunity Number when the record is created, starts the Opportunity in the selected initial stage, and records the first stage-history entry. Use the Opportunity Number when referring to the pursuit outside its detail workspace. Product interest is optional and uses the defined PSeq Lab Service or PSeq Kit product domain rather than free text. You may also record: Phaeno owner and product or service interest amount and three-letter currency expected close date, next step, competitors, description, and tags Amount remains in its recorded currency. POMS does not silently convert it. Keep the next step current so Home and reporting can distinguish active work from stale work.

sections.heading: Work the pipeline
sections.text: For a selected pipeline, the Pipeline summary shows each stage's configured probability beside its name, a numeric count and recorded value across all matching Opportunities, including records beyond the current queue page. Values remain separate by currency; unpriced means no amount has been recorded, while zero is a recorded value. Search, pipeline and the stale-work filter affect the summary. Selecting a stage filters the queue while keeping the full stage summary visible; choose All stages to clear the stage filter. Clear filter stays at the end of the filter row, after the Pipeline dropdown when shown, and is disabled when no other filters or later queue page need clearing; selecting a stage alone does not enable it. When enabled, it also clears the selected stage while keeping the pipeline. Use the single Opportunity queue to compare Company, stage, amount, expected close, owner and next action. It pages through 25 records at a time and uses compact rows on phones. Search applies automatically as you type; Enter applies the current text immediately. Use the summary buttons to select a stage. The Pipeline dropdown, including All pipelines, appears only when multiple active pipelines are available. With one available pipeline, it is selected automatically and the dropdown remains hidden even with the 30-day filter enabled. All pipelines replaces stage cards with one All opportunities count across every matching queue page; search and the 30-day filter still apply. The combined queue shows each Opportunity's pipeline and stage. Choosing a specific pipeline restores its selectable stage cards. Saved views retain the filters; old saved board/table preferences now open the same queue. Export current view uses those same filters. Open the Opportunity name for its view-first workspace. Use Edit for commercial facts. Associate buying-team Contacts with an optional role and one primary Contact when that reflects the pursuit. In Opportunity contacts, select Associate and search the Contact directory by name or email. Choose a result, optionally record the person's role, and select Associate contact. Contacts already actively associated with this Opportunity are excluded from the choices. If the section or directory search fails, use its Retry action before continuing; a failed load is not an empty buying team. Use the association's Manage action to change its role or primary designation. Remove association asks for confirmation and retains the Contact and prior association in history. Keep association returns to the editor. Failed saves retain your entries; leaving an edited draft asks whether to discard the unsaved changes.

sections.heading: Move stages deliberately
sections.text: Use Move stage from the Opportunity workspace. Select another active stage from the same pipeline and record the required reason or useful context. Stages are categorized as Open, Won, Lost, or Abandoned and carry the configured probability. A configured stage may require a reason. Lost and Abandoned stages in the default pipeline require outcome context. POMS rejects a move to a stage from another pipeline or an invalid terminal transition. Every accepted transition writes immutable history containing the prior stage, new stage, actor, time, and reason. Moving a closed Opportunity back to an Open stage clears the current closed outcome while retaining earlier history. Do not edit pipeline configuration to falsify one Opportunity's outcome. Correct the Opportunity through a valid stage transition and leave the historical transition visible.

sections.heading: Interpret values and reports
sections.text: Counts include Opportunities in every currency. Aggregate amount and weighted-forecast figures are USD-only; a non-USD Opportunity is counted but its amount is not treated as converted USD. Probability is taken from the active stage for reporting. An Opportunity marked Won is still only commercial evidence. Use a reviewed CRM handoff for Portal onboarding, evaluation, Trial Project, custom work, service change, relationship change, or offboarding. Orders and Lab work retain their separate authorization gates.

guides.title: Company requests and approvals
guides.summary: Create Company requests, decide them centrally, complete approved work, and apply reviewed Prospect conversions.

sections.heading: Company requests and approvals
sections.text: A Company request carries commercial context into an audited review queue. It can propose online access, products and services, a relationship change, or reviewed work without creating another customer identity. Company Requests, approval/completion, and Portal-access changes are available to platform administrators. Commercial staff should keep the Company and Opportunity context current and ask an administrator to prepare or complete the reviewed handoff.

sections.heading: Create a Company request
sections.text: Open the CRM Company, select Requests, and then select Create request. Start with What does this Company need?: Online access: onboarding, evaluation, or offboarding Products and services: service change Work: Trial Project or custom work Relationship: relationship change The form asks for a more specific request type only when the selected outcome has more than one. It then shows only fields relevant to that request. For new online access, choose Prospect, Customer, or Partner. Requests for an existing relationship show its current kind. An existing Prospect can use Change the relationship to request Customer or Partner; the selected target is preserved for review. Link an Opportunity when evaluation or work arose from a specific commercial pursuit; Customer order handoffs still begin from the Opportunity workspace. An Online access request never asks for a product or service. It creates or changes the Company's sign-in scope, and users can reach only the products and services the Company is separately entitled to use. Choose Products and services and Service change when product or ordering eligibility must change. Add a relationship summary suitable for the affected Company only when the reviewer needs more context; POMS supplies a short request label when the summary is blank. Do not include patient information, sample identifiers, scientific results, credentials, confidential file contents, or laboratory investigation detail. The handoff summary is relationship context for review, not an unrestricted notes field.

sections.heading: Understand what is created
sections.text: Submitting creates one pending Company request with a retained operation identity. It appears in CRM's Requests review queue and, when applicable, Order operations intake. The Company workspace shows the request number, type, status, and creation time. The handoff does not by itself: enable or reclassify Portal access invite or activate a user mark the Company Ready activate a service entitlement or ordering authorization create a quote, order, sample roster, shipment, or Lab work order approve offboarding or revoke existing access An authorized reviewer owns those consequences in the destination workflow. Online access is one possible request outcome, not the parent of every request. When onboarding or evaluation is approved, POMS attaches one internal tenant scope to the existing Company. That access scope keeps the Company's records and sign-in rights separate; it is not another Company or customer identity and does not add or remove any product or service entitlement.

sections.heading: Review and follow up
sections.text: The Requests queue stays within CRM, with CRM selected in the main navigation and Requests selected in the sidebar. Older saved Requests links open the same queue and retain the selected request and queue tab. Open CRM's central Requests section to review onboarding, evaluation, products and services, relationship, work, or offboarding requests. Use Needs decision for pending review, Approved / needs work for fulfillment and access recovery, and Completed / history for finished decisions. The Company's Requests tab keeps history and links both pending and approved items to the same queue. Access-only onboarding and Portal evaluation complete automatically once Company access is active and an organization administrator or an administrator of an active Department has accepted access. For requests with additional work, perform that work, then select Complete request and record what was completed. For an approved relationship change, Apply Customer relationship or Apply Partner relationship performs the Prospect conversion and completes the request in one action. Open Order operations for custom-work or order-intake review when the request is applicable there. Keep CRM Activities and Tasks focused on commercial follow-up; record each decision in its owning workflow.

sections.heading: Follow the work checklist
sections.text: Every approved request shows Work needed, with Done, Needs attention, Waiting, or Needs review beside each step. Progress comes from saved Company and workflow records; it updates every 15 seconds while the page is visible and when you return. A pending invitation shows Waiting for acceptance until an organization or active-Department administrator accepts and gains active access. Expired or revoked invitations return to Needs attention. A progress-loading failure disables completion and offers Retry progress. Each work item has an expandable Instructions, Waiting details, or Completion details section. Select its chevron or label to expand or collapse it. Several items can stay open together. Instructions identify who handles the work, where to go, which fields to complete, how to save, and what clears the requirement. For a service step marked Needs attention, expand Instructions and follow the numbered steps. Open the Company, then Services → Entitlements → Add entitlement. If the approved service permission already exists for the same department, Edit it instead. Review Applies to, Service, Effective from, and Effective to. Set Service configuration to Ready when the permission is ready to use, and select the displayed request number under Approved source request. Save with Add entitlement or Save entitlement. The checklist verifies that saved permission; a future start date remains Waiting. Enabling a service does not create an order or remove other operational-readiness requirements. Operational-readiness instructions distinguish shared Phaeno configuration from Company setup: Order settings, in the user menu, contains Service catalog and Quote & workflow. A Phaeno platform administrator maintains these shared definitions. Samples & shipping settings, in the user menu, contains Sample types, Ship-to destinations, Shipping procedures, Shipping assignments, Container sizes, and Order submission guidance. Shipping readiness requires a currently effective active rule whose selected destination and sample-type revisions are also active and effective. Order operations → Finance → Customer billing contains this Company's billing contact, address, payment terms, and tax decision. Open the Company and select Edit billing and tax. Save required fields, then have Finance enter Finance approval notes and select Approve current tax decision. Any later billing or tax edit requires fresh approval. The message below the checklist points back to the remaining Work needed items instead of repeating the requirements. Follow the expanded instructions for the specific missing requirement. After saving, return to Work needed for the next progress refresh. Resolved readiness blockers leave the list; when readiness passes, Complete Customer operational readiness shows Done. Use the request's Actions menu to open the owning workspace, apply a relationship change, complete access enablement, record completion where needed, or cancel. Access-only onboarding and ordinary Portal evaluation have no Complete request action: acceptance records completion automatically and moves the request to Completed / history. If active administrator access already exists, approval completes the request immediately. Trial Projects retain their separate scope and acceptance requirements. For other requests, Complete request is disabled until the displayed minimum requirements pass. The server checks them again when you submit, so a previously open page cannot rely on outdated approval, access, or entitlement state. | Request | Work to perform and verify | | --- | --- | | Onboarding or Portal evaluation | Enable Company access; invite an organization or Department administrator from Company People; have that administrator accept and gain active access. The request then completes automatically, with the reason and time retained in history. Services and orders are separate requests. | | Trial Project | Start the Trial from this exact request; submit the current scope; obtain Commercial and Scientific Operations approvals; have the Prospect accept that revision. Continue laboratory execution in the Trial workspace. | | Products and services | Apply the approved entitlement in Company Services → Entitlements, link this request as its source, and complete configuration and effective dates. A future start date remains Waiting. Customer PSeq requests also show the existing operational-readiness blockers. | | Relationship change | Review the requested Customer or Partner relationship, then use the corresponding Apply action. It performs the supported Prospect conversion and records completion together. | | Customer order handoff | Resolve the displayed order-start blockers, then start the Customer order from this handoff in Order operations Intake. Creating the linked order completes the request. | | Other custom work | Review the Company and Opportunity, document the agreed scope and commercial decision, and carry out the approved work in its owning workflow. Record the outcome in completion notes. | | Offboarding | Review active work, billing, files and retention obligations with their owners, then disable Company access. Existing work and historical records are retained for their own controlled workflows. | Items marked Needs review cannot be verified automatically. Complete those reviews and record their outcome in the required completion notes. The minimum-requirements check does not attest that a person reviewed operational, billing, or retention obligations. For requests requiring manual closeout, after all work is done, use Actions → Complete request; completion does not send invitations or configure services. For Customer PSeq Lab Service, a Won Opportunity can create a dedicated Customer order handoff from its detail page. After Company request review approves the request and confirms the active Company operational scope, Ready ordering entitlement, available service offering, and no manual operational block, Start Customer order appears in both the Opportunity and Order intake. An online Customer administrator is not required to begin pricing, but every non-billing readiness item and an active administrator are required before the quote can be issued. Billing readiness may be completed after acceptance and must be complete before invoicing. Starting the order creates one order, marks the request Applied in the same transaction, and links both records. Open the resulting order from either surface. Create a separate reviewed handoff when the same Opportunity legitimately produces another order; never retry by creating a duplicate handoff. Trial Project and Portal Evaluation handoffs do not start Customer orders. Company-level Customer order handoffs may start an order without an Opportunity, but they follow the same approval and eligibility checks. If the Company already has active online access, choose the appropriate change or offboarding request instead of creating a second onboarding request. If a submission outcome is uncertain, check Company request history before creating another request. A repeated operation key is rejected as an existing handoff. CRM lifecycle labels and Opportunity Won status never substitute for this reviewed boundary.

sections.heading: Trial Project handoff
sections.text: Create a Trial Project request from an active Company Opportunity. Its request carries commercial context; scientific analyses and deliverables are selected in the Trial workspace. Start Trial on the Company request opens creation with that exact request selected and retains a link back to the Company. If the request already created a Trial, open that existing Trial instead of creating another request. The general Trial creation flow also supports searching and paging through available requests. Commercial and Scientific Operations independently approve a frozen scope, then a Prospect organization administrator or an administrator of the assigned Department accepts it. The CRM request review does not replace either Trial approval. See Trial Projects. Trial milestones appear on the Company and Opportunity activity history. A pending CRM publication does not block laboratory work. The Trial shows pending milestones and provides Retry CRM publication; retries preserve the original event identity. Sales updates the Opportunity stage separately from Trial scientific completion.

guides.title: Reports and administration
guides.summary: Interpret commercial reports and manage pipelines, fields, views, duplicates, imports, and exports.

sections.heading: Reports and administration
sections.text: Reports explain current commercial state. CRM settings controls pipelines, stages, custom fields, saved views, duplicate review, imports, and audited exports. Commercial staff and administrators can read Reports and save personal views. Administration, imports, exports, shared-view publication, and Restricted custom fields are administrator-only. Commercial staff see and maintain Internal custom values in the owning record.

sections.heading: Read Reports
sections.text: Open Reports to review: open Opportunity count, USD open amount, USD weighted forecast, and win rate stage-level counts, USD values, weighted values, and average age owner workload across open Tasks, overdue Tasks, Leads, and Opportunities Lead-source qualification and conversion performance Activities recorded in the last 30 days Opportunity counts include every currency. Amount and weighted-forecast totals include USD records only and never imply conversion from another currency. Reports contain commercial relationship facts and must not be interpreted as scientific throughput, recognized accounting revenue, or laboratory capacity.

sections.heading: Configure pipelines and stages
sections.text: Open Administration → CRM settings from the user dropdown. Create a pipeline for a distinct commercial process, then add ordered stages. Each stage has a name, position, category, probability, and a choice requiring transition reason. Each pipeline and stage has an Actions menu for editing and deactivation or reactivation. The pipeline menu also contains Add stage and, when eligible, Delete. Only one active default pipeline supplies default conversion behavior. Deactivating a pipeline or stage removes it from new selections without erasing Opportunity or stage history. Before deactivation, review active Opportunities that still depend on it and move them through valid business transitions. An administrator can select Actions > Delete for a pipeline with no stages and no Opportunity history, whether active or inactive. Confirm the pipeline name before permanently deleting it. Inactive stages also prevent deletion. Choose another default pipeline before deleting the current default; use Deactivate for pipelines that contain stages or history.

sections.heading: Configure custom fields
sections.text: Custom fields are additive CRM metadata for Company, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, or Task. Choose Text, Number, Date, Boolean, or Option; choose Internal or Restricted sensitivity; and decide whether the field is required. Option fields accept only configured choices. Required active fields appear as incomplete-data warnings until the matching record has a valid value. Deactivation stops active collection but preserves stored history. Do not create custom fields for samples, patient data, scientific results, credentials, or file contents.

sections.heading: Save and export views
sections.text: Company, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and Task directories can save the current filters as a personal view. Administrators can also publish a shared view; Commercial staff can apply existing shared views. Applying a saved view replaces the current supported filters. Export current view uses the same filters and creates an audited export record. CRM settings lists saved views and supports full audited exports for Company, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and Task. Treat every downloaded CSV according to Phaeno's commercial-data handling rules.

sections.heading: Review possible duplicates
sections.text: CRM settings groups likely duplicate Companies and Contacts by the detected matching value. A warning never merges records automatically. Open every candidate, confirm that it represents the same legal entity or person, choose the authoritative record, and use the controlled merge action with a reason.

sections.heading: Import CSV data
sections.text: Select Preview CSV import, choose Company, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity, and select a CSV file. Imports support at most 5,000 rows and only these columns: Company: name, domain, phone, industry, source Contact: first_name, last_name, email, phone Job titles belong to Company relationships and are not accepted as standalone Contact import fields. Associate the imported Contact with a Company, then record the title on that relationship. Contact exports include primary_company and primary_company_title as derived reference columns. Lead: display_name, company_name, first_name, last_name, email, phone, source Opportunity: name, company_name, product_interest, amount, currency, next_step. When supplied, product_interest must be PSeqLabService or PSeqKit. Preview shows valid, duplicate, and invalid counts. Duplicate rows are skipped. Any invalid row blocks the commit so the source can be corrected as one controlled batch.
