An imported Opportunity's company_name must exactly match an active CRM Company; it starts in the first active stage of the default active pipeline. The batch identity is derived from record type and file facts so an unchanged retry is idempotent. Do not rename or alter a file merely to force a second commit. Tasks are excluded from import because every Task requires an explicit owning CRM record.

guides.title: Troubleshooting and recovery
guides.summary: Resolve access, duplicate, stale-update, conversion, stage, import, Task, and handoff problems safely.

sections.heading: CRM troubleshooting and recovery
sections.text: CRM preserves optimistic concurrency and consequential history. Recover by refreshing and using the owning workflow; do not repair failures with duplicate records or rewritten history.

sections.heading: CRM is unavailable
sections.text: CRM requires an active Phaeno account with Commercial operator or platform-administrator access in the Phaeno organization context. If the toolbar item is absent, confirm the selected organization and your account role. If the page reports that CRM access is required, ask a platform administrator to review your authorization rather than sharing credentials or using another person's session.

sections.heading: A list is empty or will not load
sections.text: Clear search and saved-view filters, confirm active/inactive filtering, and refresh once. An empty result differs from a failed request; retain the displayed error when escalating. Do not create a replacement record until search and duplicate review confirm that the record does not exist. The Company's People, Sales, and Requests tabs show a loading message or a specific failure with Retry for the affected records. A refresh failure may leave previously loaded records visible with a warning; it does not mean the Company has no records. Retry the affected section before associating a Contact, preparing an invitation, or choosing an Opportunity for a request. The same distinction applies to a Contact's Company relationships and an Opportunity's Opportunity contacts. Retry a failed collection before adding or changing an association. Contact and Company search controls have their own retry action if the directory search is unavailable. Search the directory rather than creating a replacement Contact simply because it is absent from the initial choices.

sections.heading: A record may be duplicated
sections.text: Open Administration → CRM settings from the user dropdown and review the possible-duplicate group. Compare identity, domains, email, associations, activity, Tasks, Opportunities, and Portal-access status. Merge only a confirmed duplicate and record the reason. A merge is not the repair for a changed employer, renamed organization, or distinct legal entity.

sections.heading: An update is stale
sections.text: Another user changed the record after your page loaded. Reload, review the newer version and history, and re-enter only the change that is still correct. Do not repeatedly submit the stale form or ask for concurrency protection to be bypassed. Company edits provide Use reviewed record after loading and displaying the changed details. Your entered values stay in the form. Review them against the current Company, select that action, and save only if the change is still correct. Retry current record reloads a failed review. After an interrupted save response, inspect the refreshed Company first: the change may already have saved. If so, discard the retained draft instead of saving it again.

sections.heading: A Lead will not convert
sections.text: Confirm the Lead is Qualified, required Company choices are complete, the selected pipeline is active, and duplicate warnings have been resolved. If conversion may already have completed, refresh the Lead and open its recorded Company, Contact, or Opportunity results before retrying.

sections.heading: An Opportunity will not move
sections.text: Confirm the destination stage belongs to the Opportunity's pipeline and remains active. Enter a reason when the stage requires one, especially Lost or Abandoned outcomes. Reload stale Opportunities before retrying. Do not edit pipeline configuration to force one transition.

sections.heading: A Task status will not change
sections.text: Blocked requires a reason. Completed and Cancelled Tasks do not offer Update; create a new follow-up Task when more work is needed. For a recurring Task, verify whether completing it already created the next occurrence.

sections.heading: An import cannot commit
sections.text: Preview must contain no invalid rows. Correct unsupported headers, missing required values, malformed currency or amount values, unmatched Opportunity company names, and row-count limits in the source CSV, then preview again. Duplicate rows are skipped; do not modify identifying data merely to force them through. If the same file may already have committed, review the batch result and affected records. The idempotency boundary is designed to make an unchanged retry safe.

sections.heading: A Company request appears missing or repeated
sections.text: Refresh the Company workspace and open Requests to find the displayed request number. A repeated operation key is rejected as an existing handoff; inspect the original request before submitting anything new. Use the central Requests queue to follow it through Needs decision, Approved / needs work, and Completed / history. Never create a second CRM Company or change the request identity merely to make another request appear.

sections.heading: Protected or scientific information was entered
sections.text: Stop adding or copying the information. Preserve the record and contact the appropriate Phaeno privacy or security owner for controlled remediation. Do not duplicate the content in a support message, Activity, Task, export, or replacement CRM record.

guides.title: Curated catalog and publishing
guides.summary: Snapshot ready sources, validate complete packages, publish immutable versions, and retire safely.

sections.heading: Curated catalog and publishing
sections.text: A curated package is a Portal-facing, immutable version built from one exact ready source revision. Publication creates a stable package identity and manifest; it does not grant the package to an organization.

sections.heading: Create the curated draft
sections.text: Select the ready source revision and review the source identity, revision, ownership and de-identification evidence, files, checksums, and snapshot time. The draft captures that source state so later source changes cannot alter it. Add the Portal-facing title, summary, release notes, scientific context, and dataset-specific metadata required for users to understand the package. Do not copy internal investigation notes or storage keys into the visible description.

sections.heading: Validate the complete package
sections.text: Before publication, confirm: every required record and file is included; the manifest is complete and checksummed; ownership and de-identification evidence is present; every file passed managed-storage and malware checks; source lineage points to the exact ready revision; and policy and audience-eligibility requirements are satisfied. Publication is atomic. A failed validation leaves an editable draft and exposes no partial version.

sections.heading: Publish and manage eligibility
sections.text: Publishing creates an immutable version. Marking it eligible makes the version available to authorized Phaeno grant workflows; eligibility itself grants no tenant access. A later version has its own identity, review, manifest, and release notes. Existing organization grants remain pinned to their current version until explicitly upgraded.

sections.heading: Retire a version
sections.text: Retirement permanently prevents new grants while preserving existing grants, files, manifests, and download history. Confirm the affected active grants and provide a retained reason. Do not use retirement when the intent is immediate safety blocking; use quarantine instead.

guides.title: Governance and recovery
guides.summary: Quarantine unsafe content, investigate with purpose, close out incidents, and retry safely.

sections.heading: Governance and recovery
sections.text: Governance actions protect every organization using a curated package while preserving evidence, immutable versions, grants, and download history.

sections.heading: Quarantine immediately
sections.text: Use quarantine when ownership, de-identification, source safety, or published content becomes uncertain. Confirm the affected source, package versions, organizations, and active grants. Record the high-level concern category, internal investigation reason, and tenant-safe instructions. Quarantine overrides all grants derived from the affected source and immediately blocks tenant viewing and downloading. It suspends grants; it does not revoke them or delete content.

sections.heading: Investigate with purpose
sections.text: Quarantined content remains available only through the Phaeno investigation path. Every investigation view or download requires a recorded purpose. Keep internal evidence restricted and do not use the tenant download route.

sections.heading: Clear or withdraw
sections.text: Clear quarantine only after recording the investigation outcome and why the unchanged immutable version is safe. The confirmation should show which still-active grants will resume and which revoked or inactive grants will remain unavailable. If the content is confirmed unsafe, preserve the version as evidence and withdraw it from future use. Track one administrator attestation per affected organization, its due date, reminders, and completion evidence. Phaeno may record an externally received attestation, but the record must identify the organization contact, evidence source, and that it was Recorded by Phaeno.

sections.heading: Review notice delivery
sections.text: Grant notices use current active organization and department access when dispatched. A revoked or superseded grant may still require a notice. Deactivated users, memberships, and department-admin assignments are excluded. Organization-wide notices go to organization administrators. Quarantine, clearance, withdrawal, and attestation reminders continue to reach current active organization administrators for affected organizations during suspension, because instructions may apply to copies already held. This does not restore Portal or download access. If no eligible administrator remains, arrange follow-up and record any externally received attestation with its evidence source. A notice with no eligible recipients or an unconfigured email sender remains failed and eligible for retry under the normal retry limits. Review current administrator assignments, the applicable organization or department status, and sender configuration before retrying. A successful delivery state records sender acceptance; confirm the recipient's response separately.

sections.heading: Recover failed operations
sections.text: Publication, grants, upgrades, revocations, quarantine, and clearance use version-aware, idempotent commands. Refresh before retrying a failed operation. Retry the existing provisioning or governance run rather than creating a duplicate grant or package version. Never clear a quarantine, restore access, or change an immutable version merely to resolve an integration or UI error.

guides.title: Organization grants
guides.summary: Grant, upgrade, and revoke exact package versions without implicit access changes.

sections.heading: Organization grants
sections.text: An organization grant gives one Prospect, Customer, or Partner organization access to one exact immutable curated-package version. Organization kind, relationship stage, eligibility, or publication never creates access automatically.

sections.heading: Create the grant
sections.text: Confirm the active target Company access scope and package identity. If access has not been approved, use Open Company access setup, create or open the CRM Company, and complete its reviewed online-access request. Return to the pending data assignment; its selected version and access scope remain in the browser session. Select a published, eligible, non-quarantined, non-retired version and review the complete package contents before confirmation. The grant operation should show: target organization and organization kind; package and exact version; current grant state and any superseded version; files and manifest included in the package; and the access consequence for active organization members. Company access approval and data assignment are separate actions. A failed grant never recreates the Company or its access scope.

sections.heading: Understand access
sections.text: An organization-wide grant is visible to authorized active members throughout that organization. A Department grant is visible only in that Department under the current role rules. Access is package-wide, not file-by-file. Downloads remain authorized at request time against membership, grant, version, package, and governance state.

sections.heading: Upgrade explicitly
sections.text: Publishing a newer version never moves an existing grant. An upgrade atomically supersedes the prior active grant with the selected new version and preserves the earlier grant, version, downloads, and audit history.

sections.heading: Revoke access
sections.text: Revocation immediately blocks future viewing and downloads but cannot recall files already downloaded. Require confirmation and a retained reason. Organization deactivation suspends access without revoking the grant; reactivation restores access only when the grant remains active and eligible. Prospect conversion preserves every existing grant and pinned version. Handle any desired package change as a separate grant, upgrade, or revocation action.

guides.title: Data provisioning
guides.summary: Manage Phaeno-owned sources, immutable packages, exact-version grants, and governance events.

sections.heading: Data provisioning
sections.text: Phaeno controls organization access and the lifecycle of Phaeno-owned source samples and curated package versions. Customer and Partner operational data is a separate access class and is never automatically reused for curated packages. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move among Source registry, Curated catalog, Organization grants, and Governance. The sidebar header identifies Data provisioning and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar. The selected section remains in the page address, so refresh keeps it open and browser Back returns to the previous section. From a source sample workspace, Back to Source registry returns to its owning list.

sections.heading: Understand the lifecycle
sections.text: Register Phaeno-owned source material and its ownership and de-identification evidence. Complete the editable source revision and mark it ready. Snapshot one exact ready revision into a curated draft. Validate and publish an immutable package version. Mark the version eligible for the intended external audience when appropriate. Explicitly grant one exact version to an organization or one of its Departments. Preserve publication, grant, download, revocation, retirement, and governance history. Each step is explicit. Source readiness does not publish a package. Publication does not grant access. Eligibility does not grant access. A later version does not upgrade an existing grant. When creating a dataset, editing its details, deactivating it, or retiring an exact version, POMS asks before discarding an edited draft. The dialog stays open while the change is being processed. If saving fails, the error appears at the top and your entries remain available for review. Discarding a draft clears those unsaved entries before the next action.

sections.heading: Use the correct access
sections.text: Only authorized Phaeno users register sources, publish versions, manage eligibility, create or upgrade grants, revoke access, or open and resolve governance incidents. When assigning a package, choose All departments (organization-wide) or one active Department. Prospect, Customer, and Partner users can view only exact active versions granted organization-wide or to their currently selected Department. Department administrators see download history for that same scope; organization administrators retain access across Departments and are the only external users who can submit an organization-wide governance attestation. Company identity, relationship, membership, and lifecycle are managed in CRM → Companies. In Organization grants, Open Company access setup takes you there; Return to pending data assignment returns to the grant screen with its draft selections retained in this browser session. Data provisioning assigns packages to existing access scopes and does not create a separate tenant. A Prospect-to-Customer or Prospect-to-Partner conversion preserves the organization identity, memberships, grants, pinned versions, and audit history. Conversion never creates, replaces, upgrades, or revokes a curated-data grant. For a Customer using PSeq Lab Service, Company Services → Overview shows derived, Department-specific readiness. Resolve account, administrator, entitlement, offering, order/sample/shipping/result-destination/instruction, and manual blockers before quote issuance or Customer commitment. Billing, terms, tax, and Finance approval remain visible but may be completed after acceptance; they must be complete before invoicing. Beginning pricing needs the active Customer, the selected Department's effective Ready PSeq service entitlement, active offering, and no operational block. Historical Portal readiness text is informational and does not authorize a transaction. Invitation access and email delivery are separate. Review the delivery state, sends, error, and expiry before retrying. A hard bounce requires revoking the invitation and issuing a new one to the corrected address; never copy or bypass an invitation token.

sections.heading: Protect the boundary
sections.text: Operational Customer or Partner files do not enter the source pool automatically. Every curated package is derived from an approved Phaeno-owned source revision. Keep storage keys, internal evidence, another organization’s grant state, and governance investigation detail out of tenant-facing content.

guides.title: Source registry
guides.summary: Register Phaeno-owned sources, managed files, evidence, and immutable ready revisions.

sections.heading: Source registry
sections.text: The source registry is the Phaeno-only intake for material approved for curation. It establishes ownership, de-identification, evidence, managed files, and revision lineage before any curated package can be created.

sections.heading: Register the source
sections.text: Create the source shell with the stable Phaeno identifier and the minimum descriptive context needed to distinguish it. Confirm that Phaeno owns or is authorized to use the material for the intended curated package. Customer and Partner operational data must not be reused merely because Phaeno processed it.

sections.heading: Build the draft revision
sections.text: Add required metadata, ownership and de-identification evidence, and approved files. Upload files through managed portal storage so the system records size, content type, checksum, scan state, and storage identity. The draft remains editable while validation is incomplete. Review every required field and file, then resolve validation or malware-scan failures before readiness. If a file's scan is Unavailable or Pending, restore the scanner and choose Retry scan on that draft file. Retry scans the same saved bytes and updates their scan state; it does not upload a replacement or grant access. A rejected file cannot be cleared by this action, and ready or archived sources cannot be rescanned here. Scan refresh preserves unsaved metadata. If your metadata save reports a changed revision, reload and review the current source before saving again.

sections.heading: Mark the revision ready
sections.text: Save your draft changes before choosing Mark ready. Readiness uses the saved revision; the action stays unavailable while metadata is unsaved or a save, upload or scan retry is in progress. Ready is an irreversible revision boundary. A ready revision is immutable and can be selected for a curated snapshot. Later corrections require a new source record for a new curated package version; they never mutate the source already used by a package.

sections.heading: Discard or archive safely
sections.text: An authorized Phaeno user may discard only an unreferenced draft. Discard requires confirmation and a retained reason. A ready, archived, or curated-snapshot revision cannot be deleted through the normal workflow. Archive a ready source when it must no longer be used for new curated snapshots. Archiving does not alter packages or grants already derived from that source. If ownership, de-identification, or safety becomes uncertain after publication, use the Governance workflow. Do not edit the source evidence or silently replace files.

guides.title: Phaeno operations guide
guides.summary: Find each workflow, its owning workspace, reusable configuration, and the roles needed to act.

sections.heading: Phaeno operations guide
sections.text: The Phaeno organization workspace is the operating surface for first-party customer relationship management, organization administration, data provisioning, Customer and Partner order work, laboratory execution, public Website intake, commercial configuration, and integration recovery.

sections.heading: Navigate workspaces and guides
sections.text: Open the user dropdown menu in the toolbar and choose Documentation under Resources. This entry is available on both wide and narrow screens. On smaller screens, the Documentation tab sits below the toolbar and organization details. The POMS dashboard, CRM, Lab operations, Order operations, Data provisioning, and Documentation use a shared sidebar anchored beneath the toolbar at the far-left edge of the screen. Its header identifies the current workspace and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. The sidebar is pinned by default, leaves a centered page in place when the left margin has room, and reflows the page only to prevent overlap. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the edge; keyboard and touch users open the same non-modal rail from the tab. Documentation automatically lists only the guides for the current organization, with an icon identifying each topic. CRM, Data provisioning, Order operations, and Laboratory operations expand to show an overview and detailed workflow guides. The group containing the current guide opens automatically; use its disclosure button to expand or collapse it.

sections.heading: Work in the Phaeno context
sections.text: Phaeno users enter the Phaeno organization context through their authenticated session. The user menu does not provide an act-as control for switching into Prospect, Customer, or Partner organizations. Manage those Companies and their access through CRM. Available workspaces and actions depend on your active Phaeno membership and assigned roles. Platform administration, order pricing, Finance, laboratory execution, scientific approval, and result release have separate responsibilities; a visible guide does not grant any of them. Ask a platform administrator to review missing access.

sections.heading: Protect your account
sections.text: After your first sign-in step, connect an authenticator app and confirm the code it displays. Store the one-time backup codes separately from the authenticator device. Never send an authenticator or backup code in email, chat, support notes, or an audit description. If both the authenticator and all backup codes are lost, contact an authorized Phaeno platform administrator. The administrator verifies your identity, resets the MFA enrollment, and revokes active sessions. You must connect a new authenticator before Portal access resumes. Email can initiate recovery but does not automatically bypass MFA.

sections.heading: Find platform work
sections.text: Dashboard uses the sidebar to show one Order Operations, Lab Operations, Customer access, or Web Operations panel at a time. The selected panel stays in the page address, so refresh and browser Back retain your place. Counts summarize the work or intake represented by each panel. CRM opens the complete first-party relationship, sales, and customer-access workspace. Its sidebar groups Companies and Contacts under Relationships; Leads and Opportunities under Sales; Tasks and Requests under Follow-up; Reports under Insights. CRM configuration is available from Administration → CRM settings in the user dropdown, immediately below Lab settings. The Company is the canonical Customer, Partner, or Prospect record. Its workspace separates Overview, People, Sales, Departments, Services, Requests, and Activity so you can focus on one kind of work at a time. Creating a Company does not grant access. Use the central Requests queue to review Needs decision, carry out Approved / needs work, and review Completed / history; use People for Company contacts, Portal identities, invitations, and reviewed access, Departments for department settings and delivery locations, and Services for readiness, service entitlements, and retention. Online-access approval creates only the internal tenant scope required for sign-in; product and service entitlements are managed separately, and approval never creates another customer record or a user. Web Operations is a Phaeno-administrator view of active public Website intake. Use Mailing List, Demo Requests, or Email delivery to select one panel at a time. Mailing List shows the newest active signups and identifies technical-brief requests; use Unsubscribe and confirm to remove a contact from that active list. Demo Requests shows the inquiry contact, organization, email, and submitted description; use Mark complete and confirm after the inquiry has been handled. Completed or unsubscribed items leave their active list immediately, but the original Website intake and action audit remain in POMS. Each panel paginates independently in groups of 10; its footer paginator appears only when the list has more than one page. These actions preserve Website intake history; create a CRM Company or Company request separately when commercial follow-up requires one. User management is the durable employee-access workspace. Invite a named Phaeno user with their intended Platform administrator and additive laboratory roles, edit accepted users and their roles, deactivate or reactivate accounts, and manage pending invitations there. Data provisioning manages source samples, curated packages, grants, and governance. Order operations contains Order intake, Trial projects, PSeq kits, Assembly, Attention, Result release, Finance, and Legacy integrations. Start each Customer Job from Order intake → New Order. Company request decisions remain in CRM; receipt and laboratory execution remain in Lab operations. Lab operations contains Phaeno-only work orders for receipt, accession, protocol execution, materials and equipment, libraries and batches, outsourced sequencing, exceptions, and scientific approval. Its sidebar contains operational work rather than role administration. Access requires an effective Lab role or platform-administrator bootstrap access. Order settings under Administration in the user dropdown menu maintains Quote & workflow settings, the Service catalog, Analyses, PSeq kits, Assembly, and Legacy links. The next menu item, Lab settings, opens laboratory configuration with its own sidebar. CRM settings follows Lab settings, then Samples & shipping settings and provides sample types, shared shipping procedures, container-specific packing, destinations, order submission guidance and shipping assignments, with preview available from each rule's Actions menu. File retention policies follows as a separate page for future-release policies. Menu items follow your access permissions. Trial configuration is reached from Trial projects and owns Trial approvers and deliverable definitions. Documentation in the user dropdown menu opens the guide set for the current organization.

sections.heading: Recover Website email
sections.text: Within Web Operations, select Email delivery to inspect queued messages, provider acceptance, and failures. View attempts shows the retained attempt history and refreshes while open. Temporary failures retry automatically up to five attempts. Accepted by email provider confirms the provider accepted the message; it does not confirm inbox delivery. The queue summary shows queued, sending, and failed messages, the oldest queued message, and interrupted attempts. Needs attention shows failed messages and interrupted attempts awaiting recovery. An interrupted attempt may have reached the recipient; review its history before taking action. Use Pause email delivery during an investigation and enter a reason. The pause persists until a platform administrator selects Resume email delivery and records a reason. Your identity, time, and reason are retained in the change history. Public Website intake and manual recovery continue to queue messages while paused; attempts already in progress may finish. Resuming processes queued messages and eligible retries, without automatically resending messages already accepted by the provider. If the delivery setting changes during review, use Reload delivery status; keep reason. Editing and dismissal are temporarily blocked while saving or reloading. Review the refreshed state before submitting your preserved reason. The queue summary refreshes automatically; a loading error identifies counts that may be out of date. For an eligible active intake record, choose Queue resend, review the specific contact and recipient, and confirm. Resending can produce a duplicate if an interrupted attempt already sent the message. A five-minute wait and a current record are required; Refresh delivery status helps recover a changed record. Each staff request is audited. An older active Mailing List signup that requested a brief may show Queue technical brief when no delivery record exists. Its original delivery status is unknown. Review and confirm the recipient before queuing it. Unsubscribed contacts and completed demo requests are not eligible for recovery.

sections.heading: Separate safe and internal information
sections.text: Tenant timelines and messages must contain only tenant-safe reasons and actions. Internal notes, scientific investigation evidence, credentials, retry details, and other restricted facts stay in authorized Phaeno surfaces. Never place passwords, OAuth credentials, webhook secrets, connection strings, protected health information, or customer file contents in notes, audit descriptions, notification messages, or accounting memo fields.

sections.heading: Support users safely
sections.text: Confirm the selected organization, user membership, capability, record reference, and visible status before changing data. Ask the caller which action and status their own audience guide and workspace show. Phaeno Documentation remains in the Phaeno audience; it does not offer an external-audience selector or impersonation. Do not ask users to share credentials or authentication tokens.

sections.heading: Search and browse guides
sections.text: Use Search documentation at the top of Documentation to find a guide or a matching section. Results update after a short pause; use at least two characters. Try “scientific approval” or “Department administrator”. Choose Filters to narrow results by Topic, Workflow, or Guide type. Clear filters removes those selections. Browse by topic opens guides for a topic without requiring search words. Workflow links and Related guides at the end of an article provide other ways to find relevant instructions. Select a result title to open its matching section. Your browser’s Back action restores the search and filters. Search uses the guides for your current organization; it does not include the public Website or operational records. A guide’s instructions do not change your account permissions. If no guides match, try fewer words or clear the filters. If search is temporarily unavailable, use Try again or Browse all guides. A documentation update may require Refresh page; guide browsing remains available while the update finishes.

guides.title: Exceptions, rework, and cancellation
guides.summary: Classify exceptions, preserve rework history, and respond safely to cancellation requests.

sections.heading: Exceptions, rework, and cancellation
sections.text: Exceptions preserve unexpected scientific or operational facts without exposing internal investigation detail to a Customer. Rework and cancellation decisions must retain the original work and its history.

sections.heading: Classify the exception
sections.text: Choose Internal when the issue can be resolved without Customer action. Choose Customer action required only when Commercial should present a safe request to the Customer. Record the internal description, severity, blocking state, responsible role, and required next action. For Customer-action exceptions, add a separate safe summary that states what is needed without disclosing internal scientific hypotheses, other organizations, or confidential operational detail.

sections.heading: Resolve or rework
sections.text: A blocking open exception prevents scientific approval. A Lab Supervisor records the durable resolution, decision, and any authorized rework. Rework remains under the same Commercial order unless the approved Commercial process creates a new authorization. Do not delete a failed execution, consumed material, rejected library, or prior QC result. Link the rework to the original facts and record why it was required.

sections.heading: Handle cancellation requests
sections.text: The Customer request remains in Commercial review. For unreceived work, Lab Ops can report that cancellation is safe. Started work requires a bounded work-order or specimen-level decision based on receipt, consumption, execution, and sendout state. Do not force Lab work to cancelled merely because Commercial received a request. Return the Lab decision so Order Ops can approve, partially approve, or decline the Commercial cancellation and preserve any financial adjustment for PSeq Finance or the applicable Partner accounting handoff.

sections.heading: Recover projections
sections.text: Commercial receives only safe action counts, summaries, milestones, schedule health, and timing projections. If a projection is delayed, refresh and retry the durable event. Never copy internal exception data into Commercial tables or create a duplicate work order.

sections.heading: Customer-requested specimen holds
sections.text: Open the Lab Job's Specimen holds card. A customer request immediately blocks new attempts, new protocol executions, new sequencing handoffs, new analysis and result release for the selected sample. Jobs with an outstanding request appear blocked in the Jobs queue. Other samples can continue. A Lab Supervisor or Operations Administrator records the decision. Use Confirm safe pause only after checking the physical procedure and any external provider. Record what already happened before confirming a pause. Use Cannot pause ongoing work when necessary; this preserves the difference between a request and a physical stop, while continuing to block new work and release. Reasons are visible to the customer. After the customer requests resumption, choose Approve resumption or Keep paused, with a reason and confirmation of the safe operational boundary. Resolve a separate Job hold or cancellation before approving resumption. Clearing this customer hold does not clear other restrictions: the normal authorization, material, protocol and quality gates are checked when work actually starts. No work starts automatically. Hold history retains requests and decisions. Holds do not rewrite prior evidence, revoke results already delivered, extend retention or change prices or deadlines. Handle those decisions through their separate approved workflows.

guides.title: Libraries, batches, and sequencing
guides.summary: Reuse preparation QC, hand passing libraries to sequencing batches, and track sendout manifests and custody.

sections.heading: Libraries, batches, and sequencing
sections.text: Library and batch records preserve the physical lineage from submitted specimen through prepared library and outsourced sequencing custody.

sections.heading: Record sequencing and analysis evidence
sections.text: Open a job, select its specimen, and go to Sample history. Operators and Supervisors can choose Record sequencing output or Record analysis run. Reviewers can open the saved records without changing them. Each file or run name links to its own detail page. For sequencing, select the recorded Library / tube and Sequencing submission. The submission must contain the exact library and barcode in its saved manifest. Enter the actual sequencing run reference, sample/index/lane mapping, exact external file version, SHA-256 checksum and byte size. Record the actual run start and completion times, plus a QC summary and named measurements or a supporting document with role qc. The library must have completed the required preparation and QC before the record can be saved. For analysis, select every exact sequencing input and describe each input's role. Inputs must come from the same source-tube attempt and purchased sequencing run. Each purchased run has its own result, even when runs reuse one prepared library. Record the actual analysis run, start/completion times, software and reference versions, and settings checksum. Every new staff-recorded analysis pins the scientific evidence requirements in effect for this screen. Where inapplicable, QC, software, settings or reference evidence may use Not applicable with an explanation; source identity, times and file attribution cannot be waived. Times use your browser's local timezone, displayed above the fields. If a clock change repeats a time, choose its occurrence. Additional run details includes instrument, flowcell, lane, pool, index mapping, workflow version and optional submission/receipt times. Supporting documents require an exact external version, checksum and byte size. These references do not upload the underlying files or confirm their availability. Use Record correction from a sequencing record or Record reanalysis from an analysis record to create a linked replacement with a reason. Review the prefilled facts against the actual work before saving. Earlier records remain unchanged and can be opened through View preceding record. Failed saves retain your entries; retrying unchanged evidence does not create a duplicate record. Where the legacy manual-upload workflow is still enabled, authorized platform administrators can choose Upload result from an analysis record. The selected analysis is carried into the upload. Identify the exact row, entry or range for this sample, or confirm that the entire file belongs to it. Upload does not approve or release the result. This action is unavailable when governed result delivery has retired manual uploads.

sections.heading: Track sequencing assembly
sections.text: Open Lab operations > Data assembly > Sequencing runs, or the Sequencing assembly section on a sample. Select a sample/run in the list to open its assembly attempt. Assembly cases contains the existing Partner manufacturing work. The processing connection is not yet configured. POMS displays Assembly setup required, and Start assembly remains unavailable until the external service is connected. This notice does not mean a job failed. For a connected service, Start assembly selects the registered inputs for one sample/run and a configured processing recipe. The server verifies the inputs before accepting the request. Processing continues after the browser closes. Percentage progress is live display information; individual updates are not retained. After a connection interruption, the percentage may be unavailable until a fresh update arrives. Each attempt retains actual start and stop times and its final disposition: succeeded, failed or terminated. These times are displayed in the browser's local time zone. Elapsed duration is calculated from the recorded start and stop. A request cancelled before execution has no fabricated execution times. Job history contains meaningful lifecycle events, not a percentage-update feed. Repeating an ended attempt requires a reason and keeps it linked to the earlier attempt for the same purchased run. Request cancellation is available only when the job can still be stopped; a request does not confirm termination. The external service may complete the job before cancellation takes effect. Successful execution does not approve or publish results. Record the completed analysis and scientific evidence through the existing capture workflow. When the matching analysis is available, Link completed analysis checks its provider execution, inputs and actual start/stop times. Result files still require verification and scientific QC before the separate customer-release workflow.

sections.heading: Prepare a library
sections.text: For tray-based preparation, open Library prep and the preparation batch. From a tube's actions choose Create library output, record the actual quantity, unit and storage location, then label the output and Confirm output identity by scanning its barcode. The job, specimen, source and preparation attempt are carried forward. Completing the final preparation stage creates the library and reuses its recorded QC evidence; do not enter the same measurements or disposition again. Complete the preparation batch before adding its eligible libraries to a sequencing batch. For historical individual work outside preparation batches, the existing library form still links source and library containers to the specimen and completed preparation execution, followed by its separate library QC entry. POMS uses the library container's barcode as the immutable library key in both paths. Only a library with passed QC can enter a sequencing batch. If QC fails, preserve the failed library and use the documented rework or replacement path.

sections.heading: Build a batch
sections.text: A preparation batch is a tray of source tubes that stays together through library preparation. A sequencing batch groups completed, eligible libraries for sequencing. These are separate records. The preparation workspace shows each library's current sequencing membership and offers Add to sequencing batch for eligible, unassigned libraries after the preparation batch is complete. Duplicate membership within a batch is rejected. A library may supply another sequencing batch when its previous batches and sendouts are complete and purchased runs remain outstanding. A batch may contain libraries from different organizations and Commercial orders. Give it a human-friendly name and optional notes. POMS assigns the current External sequencing type and a date-stamped, scanner-safe batch number when the batch is created. The name helps operators recognize the run; the batch number remains the immutable identifier. Add only the required library identifiers and operational facts. Do not copy Customer names, prices, order notes, or other confidential Commercial details into the batch manifest. For scan-first entry, open Sequencing batches, expand Scan libraries in the list header, select a draft batch, and scan each physical library container. The scan section starts collapsed and retains your entries when collapsed again. POMS accepts a container linked to a library with passed QC. A previously sequenced library can be reused while purchased runs remain, provided its material is available and its earlier batches and sendouts are complete. An unknown barcode, non-library container, failed QC, active earlier assignment, or duplicate membership is rejected without changing the batch. Open the library record to review its sequencing history. A successful scan clears and refocuses the field for the next container. Confirm membership before starting the batch. Once started, preserve the membership history and use supported add, remove, or exception actions rather than rewriting the original manifest. Scanning proves the container identity used for entry; it does not replace the approved physical manifest and custody checks. When an authorized operator uses Start or Complete batch, POMS opens a confirmation modal with the observed start or completion time prefilled. The operator can correct the time when the bench event happened before it was entered; POMS stores the submitted value as UTC and retains the server audit timestamp. Use the Status filter above the batch list to focus on drafts, in-progress batches, or completed batches without changing which draft batches are available for scanning.

sections.heading: Create an outsourced sendout
sections.text: For outsourced NGS, enter the provider name, optional provider reference, expected completion, and any additional manifest notes. POMS freezes the current batch membership, library identifiers, and library-container barcodes in the sendout manifest. Confirm the physical contents against the batch before saving. Advance it through Shipped, Received by provider, Sequencing, and Complete only when the corresponding operational fact is known. Add custody events whenever responsibility or location changes. Record the event code, location or responsible party, and carrier or tracking reference when used by the approved procedure. An optional custody note captures additional operational facts.

sections.heading: Respect the implementation boundary
sections.text: The sendout tracks material, manifest, timing, provider status, and custody. The assembly workspace tracks requested processing attempts and their outcomes, but the external processing connection and automatic result import still require integration setup. Uploading raw sequencing datasets and preserving externally held files remain responsibilities of their producing system. Scientific approval and customer release remain separate steps.

sections.heading: Record library quality evidence
sections.text: For library QC, select Pass or Fail and record the observations and decision basis. Add named measurements with their values and units as needed. POMS retains those structured observations with the library; operators do not need to prepare JSON. The applicable method still determines the scientific acceptance criteria.

sections.heading: Sequence a sample more than once
sections.text: A purchased sample-sequencing run is one sequencing of one sample. Twenty samples sequenced once and one sample sequenced twenty times both use 20 purchased runs. Tube count and library-preparation count are separate. One prepared library can supply multiple sequencing runs. To use it again, retain the original preparation and QC evidence and select that library when recording sequencing output. If another batch is needed, complete the previous batch and sendout, then use Add to batch in the job's library list or scan the library into a draft sequencing batch. POMS checks for outstanding authorized runs and rejects simultaneous batch assignments. For a fresh preparation, open the specimen and select Prepare a new library. Select and scan an eligible source tube. If using a previously successful source tube, confirm material remains and record the supporting evidence. Complete the new preparation, output identity and QC through the existing workflow. Open the sample's Scientific evidence and select Record sequencing output. Enter the Purchased run number (1 through the sample's authorized total), explicitly choose New preparation for this run or Use an existing prepared library, and select the library and recorded submission actually used. Complete the provider run reference, exact file identity, checksum, sample mapping and scientific evidence. The same machine run can contain several purchased runs of a sample; record their distinct sample mappings and purchased run numbers. Additional files use the same purchased run number. A linked correction or a replacement after failed sequencing retains that number and records its reason. Corrections and reanalysis do not purchase or complete another unit. Each output retains its producing library and preparation attempt. A successful preparation alone does not complete a purchased run: approved results must cover every allocated run, and delivery remains incomplete until the results for all runs are published.

sections.heading: Resuming scientific file uploads
sections.text: The file picker shows the current limit (normally 100 MiB). A 50 MB file is within this limit. POMS transfers the file in portions and verifies its full size, fingerprint and malware-scan result before it can be used as evidence. This does not establish the scientific validity of its contents. If the connection fails, choose Resume upload. In the same browser tab, selecting the same file after returning to the page also resumes confirmed portions for up to 24 hours. Keep the original file unchanged. After expiry, select it again to start a new transfer. A failed replacement preserves the previously selected evidence file. If complete-file scanning is unavailable, retry verification after the service recovers. Abandoned transfer portions expire; admitted scientific files and their receipts remain protected internal evidence. Customer result retention does not delete these internal files. Names, sample and run attribution stay the same when the configured private storage provider changes.

guides.title: Materials and equipment
guides.summary: Qualify lots and equipment, record consumption and use, and preserve dated resource evidence.

sections.heading: Materials and equipment
sections.text: Materials and equipment records show what was used, in what quantity, and whether it was suitable at the time of execution. They support scientific traceability; they are not purchasing or accounts-payable records. New consumption and equipment-use records retain a dated copy of the resource details available when the use is recorded, including lot QC and expiry or equipment calibration. Later resource changes do not replace that saved evidence. Older use records may lack this copy. For late entries, the copy reflects the recording time; it does not prove what the resource record contained on an earlier date.

sections.heading: Receive and qualify material lots
sections.text: In Materials, select a lot's name and lot number to open its details. The page shows material identity, supplier, available quantity and unit, storage, expiration or retest date, and the recorded QC status, date and failure reason. Prepared reagents also show their recorded source lots and quantities; select a source lot to inspect its details. Use Back to Materials to return to the list. Choose the lot kind first: Supplier lot uses a controlled material identity, supplier, catalog product, supplier lot number, and storage location. Select the exact product from the chosen supplier; changing the supplier clears the product selection. Prepared reagent uses a controlled material identity, Phaeno lot number, storage location, and one or more source component lots. It does not use a supplier. Select existing controlled records when available. If a material or storage location is new, choose the corresponding Create a new… option and enter its name in the focused modal. The entered name returns as the selected option in the lot form. The new reference is created with the lot, and POMS assigns an immutable key to a new material. Retired reference records are retained for history but are not available for new lots. Record the available quantity and unit. Use Expiration or retest date when applicable; this is a date-only field and the lot remains valid through the end of that date. Exact time-sensitive use-by control is not represented by this field. New lots show QC: Pending. A laboratory supervisor uses Record QC, confirms the QC date, and selects Pass QC or Fail QC in the modal. A failed outcome requires a reason. Passing QC makes the lot eligible for controlled work when its expiration or retest date, availability, and other rules are also satisfied. Failing QC keeps the lot blocked. POMS also retains the operator and server-recorded audit time. For an older purchased lot without a product, open its details and choose Actions → Assign product. Confirm the product from the recorded supplier against the lot label before saving. The assignment cannot be replaced. Add or activate missing suppliers/products in Suppliers & products first. Historical stock use is retained. A configured product in Library prep offers only eligible lots assigned to that exact product. An internally prepared reagent offers only prepared lots of its configured material definition. Unlinked purchased lots cannot satisfy a product-specific step. If no lots are offered, check the identity assignment, QC, expiry and available stock. Only lots with Passed or Approved exception QC may be consumed in controlled work. An approved exception must retain the decision, reason, approver, and applicable scope. Expired, failed, quarantined, or otherwise unavailable lots remain blocked. When a prepared reagent is created, select each exact source lot and quantity. Every source lot must be QC-approved, unexpired, and available in the entered unit. POMS records the lineage and subtracts the component quantities atomically.

sections.heading: Record consumption
sections.text: Start the assigned execution before recording consumption. Select the exact lot, quantity, and compatible unit required by the protocol. The portal blocks unit mismatches and consumption above the available quantity. Consumption is a durable scientific fact. Do not reduce or delete it to make inventory appear correct. Use an approved correction, adjustment, or exception that preserves the original entry and reason.

sections.heading: Reconcile an uncertain lot quantity
sections.text: When a sample's material amount is recorded as Amount unknown, POMS retains that fact and places the lot's quantity on hold. Known amounts from the same entry are deducted normally. The last recorded balance remains visible, but the lot cannot supply further work, including prepared reagents, until it is reconciled. Passing QC does not clear a quantity hold. A Supervisor or Operations Administrator opens the lot and chooses Reconcile quantity. Verify the physical remaining stock, enter the Counted remaining quantity in the lot's unit, and explain the reconciliation. The balance may be zero and cannot exceed the last recorded balance. Saving retains the before/after quantities, reason, operator and time in Quantity history, then clears the quantity hold. Earlier sample amounts remain unknown; reconciliation does not invent a sample quantity or undo known consumption. If the affected tube is also held, a Supervisor must separately review it and choose Resolve hold from its Library prep actions, with a reason. Reconcile its uncertain lot first. Neither inventory reconciliation nor resolving a hold makes a failed attempt usable again.

sections.heading: Register equipment
sections.text: Enter the equipment name, then select an equipment type and location already used by the laboratory. Protocol equipment requirements also supply type choices, and active material-storage locations are available as location choices. If the required type or location is missing, choose Create a new…, enter its name in the focused modal, and use the returned selection. POMS assigns the immutable asset code when the equipment is created. Record the Last calibration date and Calibration due date when applicable. These are date-only laboratory facts; a time of day is not required. The due date cannot be before the last calibration date, and a last calibration date cannot be in the future. Equipment must be active and calibration-current at the time it is used.

sections.heading: Retire equipment
sections.text: A Lab Supervisor or Operations Administrator can open an asset's Actions → Retire equipment, enter a required retirement reason, and confirm. Retirement prevents new equipment-use records, including backdated entries, while retaining the asset identity, calibration details and existing usage history. POMS records who retired the asset and when. Retirement cannot be undone through this screen. Retired assets are hidden by default. Select Show retired above the Equipment list to include them and read the retirement date and reason. Clear the checkbox to return to current equipment.

sections.heading: Record equipment use
sections.text: Link the exact equipment record to the execution step or run. Confirm that its status and calibration cover the use time. If equipment becomes unavailable or overdue, stop new use, record the issue, and select another qualified item or follow the approved exception path. The accounting system may own a purchase-order reference, but supplier invoices, payment, and procurement approval remain outside Lab Ops.

guides.title: Laboratory operations
guides.summary: Track jobs and specimens, record scientific evidence, investigate result delivery and retention history, and save internal evidence reports.

sections.heading: Laboratory operations
sections.text: The dashboard's Laboratory work card identifies each job by its Commercial order number, submitted reference, or a unique work-order identifier when neither is available. Select a job to open its record, or use Open Lab operations at the top-right of the card. Use Receipt & accession in Lab operations to prepare return kits, identify arriving packages, compare registered tubes, and see authorized work awaiting specimens. Choose Open receipt to record custody, accession, and intake disposition in the linked Lab work order. Customer quote acceptance opens sample-list preparation; finalizing the exact compliant roster records the Commercial authorization and creates the linked Lab work order and shipment together. Do not create Lab work manually to repair an order. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move through Receipt & accession, Jobs, Library prep, Sequencing batches, and Results & review. Separate groups contain PSeq kits and Data assembly, then Suppliers & products, Materials and Equipment. Phaeno platform administrators use Suppliers & products to maintain supplier names, product names, descriptions and product types for reagents and shipping supplies. Within Suppliers & products, use the Suppliers & products tab for vendors and their products, and the Product types tab to manage those categories and their eligibility for transportation kits. Search and Show inactive are in the shaded header of the suppliers, products and product types lists. Open Lab settings from Administration in the user dropdown menu for Lab steps, Protocols, Workflows, Stage durations, Holiday calendar, and Library tray formats in its own sidebar; tray layouts are managed there and selected when assembling work in Library prep. Library prep opens preparation batches, where accepted tubes from compatible jobs are assembled into a tray and processed together. Open Jobs, directly above Library prep in the sidebar, for the job and specimen list. Jobs remain open until results for every in-scope sample have been published to the customer Portal. The Active jobs tab is the default. Closed jobs contains fully delivered and cancelled jobs, including cancellations before shipment. A failed sample does not close its job. Scientific approval and Ready for release do not complete delivery. Expand Filters in the list header to search or narrow either jobs tab. The section starts collapsed, shows how many filters are applied, and summarizes the selected criteria in one sentence while closed; collapsing it keeps those filters in effect. Use Clear filters beside the Filters label to reset only the selected tab’s filters, even when the section is collapsed. Typed dates apply when you leave the date field or press Enter, so you can finish entering the year. Each tab retains its own search, date filters and page when switching tabs, refreshing or returning from a job. Results & review opens the same jobs at scientific review; a listed job is not necessarily ready for approval. Its return link preserves the section you came from. Specimen, execution, library and exception history remain accessible from either entry point. PSeq kits retains its manufacturing workflow. Data assembly has Sequencing runs for sample assembly jobs and Assembly cases for Partner manufacturing. The sequencing connection currently shows a setup notice until the processing service is configured. Each assembly attempt retains actual start/stop times and final disposition; percentage progress is shown live without a saved update history. The sidebar header identifies Lab operations and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar.

sections.heading: Investigation evidence preservation
sections.text: Internal sample history, traceability records, saved investigation reports and uploaded supporting preparation/QC reports are retained indefinitely for now, separately from customer download expiry. Deleting expired customer result files cannot remove a supporting report referenced by internal evidence. External scientific files remain with their producing system; a saved reference or checksum does not mean POMS holds their bytes.

sections.heading: Understand the boundary
sections.text: Lab Ops owns return-kit preparation, physical PSeq kit fulfillment, shipment intake, specimen receipt, accession, container lineage, Data Assembly execution, controlled protocol execution, material and equipment use, libraries, cross-order batches, sequencing sendouts, exceptions, and scientific approval. Commercial owns order intake, the Customer or Partner order, quotes, approval, cancellation review, billing, and accounting source records. Work enters Lab Ops only through an immutable Commercial authorization. Lab Ops publishes safe milestones and action requests back to Commercial; it never exposes internal laboratory tables or investigation notes to a Customer.

sections.heading: Use the correct role
sections.text: Laboratory roles are additive Phaeno-only assignments: Lab Operator records receipt, accession, containers, execution, consumption, equipment use, libraries, batching, sendouts, custody, and exceptions. Lab Supervisor can perform operator work, approve material QC, and resolve exceptions. Protocol Administrator authors, approves, activates, and retires controlled protocol versions. Scientific Reviewer records scientific approval after execution and blocking-exception gates pass. Lab Operations Administrator can perform all Lab actions and assign Lab roles. Platform administrators retain bootstrap access. Only active Phaeno members can receive or use Lab roles; disabling or offboarding a user removes effective Lab access even if an assignment record remains. Assign the narrowest roles needed for a person's work. Separation of operator and reviewer is supported but is not mandatory for every service. Manage these assignments from User management. Select Edit on an active Phaeno user, then change the laboratory roles in that user’s single Roles group and save the record. The Lab operations sidebar contains operational laboratory work only.

sections.heading: Follow the work sequence
sections.text: Open the authorized work order and verify the expected specimens. Record receipt and accession; POMS assigns the authoritative barcode and creates the initial physical container. Apply the intake decision and preserve every derived-container relationship. In Library prep, assemble accepted sources into a preparation tray using an approved workflow for the jobs’ purchased service. Confirm the tray to start. Record ordered steps with their prescribed batch or tube scope, shared resource use and any tube exceptions. Create and identify outputs in the same workspace, reuse preparation QC, and close the tray before adding passing libraries to a sequencing batch. Record sendout custody separately when applicable. Resolve blocking exceptions and complete scientific review. Publish Ready for release back to Commercial. Every transition preserves prior state. Do not repair mistakes by deleting containers, overwriting protocol versions, replacing shipment history, or duplicating work orders.

sections.heading: Investigate a sample or questioned result
sections.text: Open Closed jobs, select the job, and open the specimen. Sample history is also available from an active job. Choose a Result version to see its saved producing analysis, sequencing inputs, result-file attribution and exact source tube. A historical result without those links is shown as unknown; POMS does not infer a tube from the latest attempt. Expand Protocol work to review entries, corrections and actual performers/times separately from the person and time that recorded the entry. Other sections show materials, equipment, libraries, scientific metadata, result files, approvals, exceptions and custody. Event history has Previous and Next controls. Open a protocol execution to review its controlled instructions and detailed work context. Open Supporting reports to download a preparation or QC report attached to a step that covered this sample. Recorded report details shows the retained file identity and checksum. A download checks current access, the saved clean-scan status, file size and checksum before returning the file. A missing file or checksum mismatch appears as Evidence unavailable; investigate the original attachment and retry after the problem is resolved. Downloading does not replace or change the saved evidence. The access record confirms that a verified download was requested, not that the browser finished receiving it. Sequencing outputs and Analysis runs link to individual records. Operators and Supervisors can record new evidence and linked corrections from these sections. See Libraries, batches, and sequencing for the required run, file, QC, software and source information. Delivery and retention history covers all recorded result versions for this sample: delivery events, download attempts, verified download timing, retention schedules and saved policies, preservation holds and reissues. A started or failed download is not a completed transfer, and a completed transfer does not prove that the recipient read the file. Missing completion or commit timestamps remain unrecorded. A shared Trial release describes the package containing this sample; other samples' files and downloads are omitted. Package-wide holds or retention decisions still apply to the shared package. Saving an investigation report also preserves this history as it stood at that time. Find related samples searches an exact tube barcode, material lot number, equipment asset code, sequencing run, library key or preparation-tray barcode within this job’s organization. A shared resource is a starting point for investigation; it does not establish that the samples share a problem. Use Save investigation report to preserve the evidence available at that time. Each saved report’s Actions menu offers a readable report, which can be opened and printed, and a structured evidence manifest. The checksum identifies the exact saved manifest and is checked before download. Later work does not rewrite an earlier report. Customer download expiry does not remove saved investigation reports. These reports capture the sample history; supporting PDF files and external scientific files are not embedded. Review missing or unavailable evidence. Recorded metadata does not certify scientific validity or prove that an external source file is still available. A failed source load appears as Evidence unavailable. Large histories may exceed the supported report size; POMS rejects that report rather than presenting a partial history as complete. Reports are for internal investigation, not automatic customer distribution.

sections.heading: Operational readiness boundary
sections.text: POMS now allocates checksummed Phaeno barcodes, renders QR container labels, records reasoned print and failure history, and adds eligible libraries to a draft batch by scan. These software controls do not prove that a particular printer, stock, scanner, browser, or environment is fit for production. This guide explains the portal workflow; it is not a laboratory SOP or evidence that a production process has been validated. Before production use, Phaeno must approve the actual minimum fields, labels, printers, scanners, reprint and degraded-mode procedures, external NGS provider identifiers and manifest/status exchange, and operational ownership. Use only approved procedures and configuration for real work.

sections.heading: Track delivery deadlines
sections.text: Active jobs prioritizes Overdue, At risk and Due soon work, followed by other open work. Filter by Job or organization, Due date: From / To, Deadline status (All deadlines, Overdue, At risk, Due soon), and Job status. The list includes jobs once at least one specimen shipment has been recorded as shipped, delivered or received. A recorded specimen receipt also qualifies older jobs without shipment records. Jobs still being prepared for shipment are excluded. Matching jobs appear across pages, including sent specimens still awaiting acceptance. Expand Filters to use the Overdue, At risk and Due soon count links. All clears only the deadline status, keeping the other filters. These warning counts cover every page for the current search, due-date range and job status, before the deadline-status selection. Closed jobs provides Job or organization, Order date: From / To, and Outcome (All outcomes, Delivered, Cancelled). Order date is the original order creation date; Trials use their creation date. Older work without its originating record uses the retained work creation date. Closed jobs show their outcome; delivery timing remains available in job details. Either date endpoint may be blank. From and To include the entire selected calendar day in the browser timezone, which is shown below the filters. Job statuses are Awaiting receipt, Awaiting acceptance, Ready for preparation, Library preparation, Sequencing, Data processing, Quality review, Awaiting delivery, and On hold. The overall status follows the earliest outstanding sample stage; an explicit job hold takes precedence. Sequencing includes libraries awaiting sequencing in a batch. Partial publication does not move remaining laboratory work into Awaiting delivery. Sample stages remain available in the job details. No failed-job outcome is defined yet. The due date starts with the service offering’s saved maximum turnaround in calendar days, from scientific acceptance. Future offering changes do not move existing job deadlines. Every accepted job must have a delivery due date. A configured turnaround calculates it on acceptance. If no turnaround is recorded, an operator or supervisor must use Actions → Set due date on the job before accepting samples; acceptance cannot be saved without one. Before acceptance, the job may show Awaiting acceptance. Any historical accepted job missing its required date is flagged At risk for correction. Due soon means a delivery or outstanding sample target is within three calendar days. Holds, blocking exceptions and a forecast later than the due date produce At risk. Passing the job’s due time without complete delivery produces Overdue, even if the forecast has moved later. An earlier outstanding sample target remains visible. Open a job to see the original delivery target, current due date, expected completion, published-sample count and due-date history. Operators and supervisors can choose Actions → Set due date (or Adjust due date when one exists), enter the exact date/time and a customer-safe reason, and save. The original target and forecast are retained. Commercial jobs receive one notice of this deliberate due-date change. Adjust a staff expected-completion estimate separately through the Commercial order when needed; the calculated progress forecast is explained below. Follow any commitments in the governing agreement; the standard TAT alone is not a contractual guarantee. The form identifies the timezone used for entry. Dates retain their exact time cutoff; they do not silently mean end of day. The list refreshes deadline warnings while open. No new periodic email reminder is sent by the Jobs list. Partial publication leaves a job open. Download or acknowledgement is not required for completion. A withdrawal makes the affected sample outstanding again while retaining the original full-delivery event; ordinary expiration of the download period does not undo delivery. Historical published jobs without a retained first full-delivery event show Complete — timing unverified, rather than an invented on-time/late assessment. Failed samples remain outstanding unless an actual customer-visible deliverable is published or the scope is explicitly cancelled through the existing process.

sections.heading: Calculated expected completion
sections.text: Active jobs show Calculated expected completion based on each sample’s recorded progress and configured stage durations. Open a job and expand Sample progress and remaining work to see current stage, entry time, time in stage, remaining calendar days and the stages still needed for Portal delivery. The latest outstanding sample determines the job date; parallel libraries are evaluated separately. A later calculated or explicit staff estimate makes the job At risk when it exceeds the committed due date. The calculation updates when the queue or job is refreshed. An hourly internal refresh also retains forecast history. The calculated forecast, original turnaround baseline, staff estimate and delivery commitment are separate. Automatic calculations do not change a commitment or send a customer message. An unfinished stage whose estimate is exhausted receives one additional stage day from the current evaluation time, followed by its remaining downstream work. A business-day stage uses an eligible business day for that allowance. The original estimate and recorded entry time remain intact. Insufficient information means the calculation needs configuration, a reliable stage timestamp or a required workflow decision. Blocked means a hold, unresolved failure or blocking exception prevents a reliable date. Coverage shows how many outstanding samples can be estimated; a partial estimate is not presented as the whole job’s expected completion. Older library and review records may lack the newly captured transition times.

sections.heading: Configure stage durations and holidays
sections.text: Protocol administrators and supervisors maintain the Stage durations and Holiday calendar sidebar sections under Lab settings. Lab steps remains the default section. Open Holiday calendar and create the calendar first. Enter its confirmed coverage period and the actual observed dates and names of holidays or other laboratory closures. An empty calendar confirms there are no additional exclusions within that period. No jurisdiction’s holidays are assumed automatically. The year filter and revision details appear in the calendar header. Holiday dates display as Sep 18, 2026; the display list and existing entries in the editor are ordered by observed date. Open Stage durations, select the workflow version and choose Configure durations or Actions → Edit durations. Set estimated days and Calendar days or Business days independently for every applicable stage. Include normal waiting time. Blank means not configured; zero means no additional downstream time. Indicate whether the workflow requires library QC and sequencing after its protocol stages. Business days use Monday–Friday in America/Los Angeles and exclude configured closure dates. Calendar-day stages count every day. Fractional business days count time within eligible dates; work starting on a closed date begins counting at the next eligible midnight. Forecasts needing business dates beyond confirmed calendar coverage remain unavailable until coverage is extended. Save with a reason. Saving creates a revision. New jobs use the latest configured revision for their approved or current service workflow; existing workflow assignments retain their revision. If a sample starts an attempt using another workflow version, that version receives its own timing assignment. Each sample is forecast using its actual selected workflow. To change existing jobs, choose Actions → Preview and apply to jobs. Review current and proposed forecasts, select the jobs and provide a reason. Apply the revision only after reviewing that preview. A calendar edit also requires selecting the new calendar in the workflow’s durations and applying the resulting policy revision to existing jobs. Timing settings support operational estimates; they do not establish or change customer delivery commitments. A scientific or operational review is still needed to decide appropriate duration values.

guides.title: Service workflows, protocol control, and execution
guides.summary: Use Lab settings for controlled workflows; record actual performer/time and independently review on-behalf entries or attribution changes.
taskKeywords: Service workflows, protocol control, and execution

sections.heading: Service workflows, protocol control, and execution
sections.text: Lab Ops uses a controlled service workflow to arrange reusable, versioned protocols into the approved production process. Commercial orders and jobs identify the purchased service. Preparation batches and specimen attempts retain the exact workflow, stage, and protocol versions used to deliver it. A job’s historical workflow assignment does not restrict new attempts. Explicitly approved Trial workflow constraints remain part of that Trial’s scope.

sections.heading: Reusable Lab steps
sections.text: Open Administration → Lab settings → Lab steps to find reusable procedures. Open a step name to view its versions and Used by protocols. Protocol Administrators create the identity, then choose New version or Edit draft. The dedicated editor captures instructions, typed values and their scopes, optional PDF attachments, resources, outputs, operator confirmation, roles and QC criteria. New configurations default to batch preparation. New captured values and QC gates default to one batch entry or outcome. Choose individual tube capture or shared values with tube exceptions where the procedure requires it; barcodes remain tube-specific. Recording a step automatically includes every eligible tube; individual tubes cannot be deselected. Existing saved definitions retain their configured scopes. Save the draft, review its configuration preview, and choose Approve version from its Actions menu. A different Protocol Administrator approves it.
