A platform administrator approving their own draft must explicitly record an override reason. Approval locks that version. A new version leaves every earlier approved version and existing protocol snapshot unchanged. Cancelling an approval override with an unsaved reason asks whether to discard it. A rejected save retains the reason for review and retry. In a protocol editor, choose an exact Approved Lab step version and select Add Lab step. Its content is read-only. Set its required, optional or conditional placement and arrange the occurrences in order. Earlier occurrences remain prerequisites. Repeating a step creates a separate occurrence with independent evidence. Existing embedded protocol steps remain supported. When a newer approved Lab step version exists, the pinned occurrence offers Adopt approved v…. Adoption changes only the open protocol draft. Save and independently approve the assembled protocol before using that new version. Workflows and active batches keep their existing protocol versions. Retire Lab step prevents new selection; existing pinned occurrences, versions, usage and history remain available. In the editor, Fields to record defines the information operators enter. Recorded for specifies whether an entry applies to the batch or individual samples. Use Units and symbols beside a unit field to choose a common unit, or type a custom unit. Insert symbol beside text fields inserts µ, Δ, °, ±, ×, ≤, ≥ at the cursor, replacing selected text when present. Selecting a common unit replaces the unit field. These controls preserve the entered symbols without converting measurements. In each step editor, Batch report lets you omit the upload control or include a QC report or preparation worksheet. When a report is included, Report required determines whether a performed step can be saved without its PDF. Required reports show a required marker and validation message in both preview and live recording. Allowed skips do not require a report. New steps start without a report; older definitions retain their existing report behavior until explicitly changed in a draft. Batch only fields apply to every eligible tube without showing a sample-entry list. For Same entry with sample exceptions, select Record exception to reveal the collapsed sample cards. Enter only the overrides that differ from the batch entry and give an exception reason. Turning Record exception off clears those overrides and their reasons. Fields configured for individual samples remain visible even when no shared exception is being recorded. Use Material used, Equipment used, and Output created in Fields to record to collect these entries with the step. In configuration, choose a vendor/product or an Internally prepared reagent under Configured material. For entries without lot tracking, you can instead define the material manually with its name and optional vendor. The saved version retains those details. Set Quantity unit in configuration using free text or Units and symbols. During recording, the material and unit are fixed; the operator enters only the quantity. Enable Include lot number in configuration to request a released inventory lot at run time; only lots linked to the exact configured product, or prepared lots of the exact configured material definition, are offered. Older purchased lots need Assign product in Materials before they can be used in a product-specific step. Manual descriptions do not support lot tracking in new configurations. Saving the step records its stock use. Batch quantities default to an amount per sample; authors can instead specify a total batch amount. Equipment used always requires selecting an eligible registered instrument when recording the step. The selector shows its name and equipment barcode. Equipment fields have no optional barcode or Required setting; free-text equipment names are not accepted. Previously saved equipment records remain unchanged. The configured unit appears in the quantity label, for example Quantity per sample (µL). Tracked lots must use the same unit; units are not converted automatically. Enter the amount in that unit; the batch total appears below. Earlier approved configurations without a unit continue to use the selected lot's unit, or manual entry for untracked materials. When the step includes a QC or preparation report, attach it at the end of the step entries, before the final confirmation. The report applies to the included batch samples. An output field records a separate library container for each included sample. Enter common quantity, unit and storage values once, with individual values where needed. Existing outputs retain their identity. Save step record saves these entries together. A correction retains previous resource use rather than consuming stock again; a repeat records new material/equipment use. Existing resource requirements can be explicitly converted to these fields in a configuration draft using Convert existing requirements to fields.

sections.heading: Configuration preview
sections.text: Use Configuration preview in a Lab step or protocol editor to inspect unsaved configuration, or from a saved Lab step version. It opens the Library prep capture form with clearly fictional example tubes. Preview does not approve a configuration or establish scientific validity. Select any step directly, or use Previous step and Next step. No prior specimen or QC state is needed. Choose performed, repeat (when permitted), or correction presentation; optional and conditional steps also expose the performed/skip decision. These selections inspect form presentation and do not simulate workflow progression. Enter example values and select Validate entry to see missing or invalid fields. Shared and individual fields, units, choices, confirmations, QC criteria, optional attachments and resource controls follow the same form configuration as Library prep. Resource controls show fictional choices; output validation creates no containers or barcodes. File selections remain local and are never uploaded. Reset example values clears the current form. Changing steps or presentation also clears its example values. Return to configuration discards all example entries while preserving your configuration draft. Edit the draft and reopen preview to inspect the updated definition. Nothing entered in preview becomes laboratory evidence, inventory activity, approval, sequencing work or customer status.

sections.heading: Record when a step was performed
sections.text: For both individual execution and library preparation, When the work happened separates the performed time from the time the record is saved. Choose Now only when confirming the work at recording time. Choose Earlier for work already completed, enter its actual date/time in the displayed time zone, and give a Late-entry reason. Earlier entries retain minute precision and the selected UTC offset. A nonexistent daylight-saving time cannot be entered; when the same local time occurs twice, choose the correct occurrence. Future times are rejected. Confirm the actual performer and time before saving. Me — personally performed identifies you as the performer. Alternatively select another staff member as described below. In a shared preparation entry, the same performer and time apply to every included tube; use separate entries when the actual work differs. The configured instruction confirmation still applies where required. Time and confirmation entries in configuration preview remain fictional and are never saved. Execution history and Current sample records show Performed by and Recorded by separately, along with late-entry reasons. The recorded time always comes from POMS. Older entries without separate performance evidence say so; a recording timestamp is not treated as a known performed time. A Repeat records new work and needs a fresh confirmation/time. A Supervisor's Correct action preserves the original performer/time, including any unknowns, and adds the correction and its recorder to history. It currently corrects step values, not performed time or performer attribution. Where both Repeat and Correct are available, open the step's Actions menu. Skips claim no performed work.

sections.heading: Record another person's work or correct performer/time
sections.text: In When the work happened, choose Another staff member under Performed by, select the actual performer, and explain why you are recording their work. Choose Earlier when appropriate. You remain identified as the recorder. The entry is unverified until a different Supervisor reviews it. Open the sample's Sample history → Performer and time reviews to inspect these entries. A Supervisor can choose Propose performer/time change, select the original step, identify the actual performer and time, and give the reason and supporting evidence. Another Supervisor uses Review entry to approve or reject it with an explanation. Authors cannot review their own entries. If someone approves a competing change first, reload and propose against the current evidence. The original record and every proposal/decision remain in history. A rejected correction leaves the original attribution unchanged. A rejected on-behalf entry needs a corrected, approved proposal before it becomes verified evidence. Pending reviews block results using the governed traceability path. Step Correct continues to correct captured values while preserving original performer/time; use this separate proposal workflow for attribution changes.

sections.heading: Preparation batches
sections.text: Open Lab operations → Library prep to create a preparation batch. Choose an active library tray format and an approved workflow whose protocol versions explicitly support preparation batches. POMS generates the batch identifier from the service and creation timestamp in UTC, for example PSeq-20260912-143052. A numeric suffix distinguishes batches created at the same time. You do not enter a batch name; add optional notes for context. The identifier stays with the batch through preparation and sequencing handoff. Existing batches retain their original names. Jobs must request the same service and have a confirmed tube-use instruction. Accepted, available tubes without an existing attempt can join the batch even if the job was created under an older workflow. Adding a tube records this batch’s exact workflow version on its attempt. An existing unstarted attempt must already use that same version; cancel it with a reason before selecting a different procedure. Started attempts cannot be moved to another workflow. In Find eligible tubes, use Freezer box barcode to scan a box or enter part of its recorded barcode. Combine it with the tube barcode or job search to narrow the list further. Each result shows its recorded freezer box. The list shows up to 10 tubes per page, with a total count and Previous/Next controls below it. Changing either filter returns to page 1. Clear filters returns to the first page of all eligible tubes; filtering and paging do not change eligibility or add a tube to the tray. Within the Tray card, beneath the Required legend, select Find eligible tubes to expand or collapse the list. It starts collapsed, and collapsing it preserves your filters and current page. The progress strip shows Prepare tray → Prepare libraries → Complete batch → Sequencing handoff. Prepare tray includes scanning the physical tray, loading tubes and confirming the contents. The Next step panel changes its guidance as you progress through those tasks. When recording protocol evidence, its title shows the protocol number and the step number within that protocol, followed by the step name. Loading tubes alone does not complete Prepare tray: partial trays are allowed, and you choose Confirm tray when ready. Future work stays hidden until relevant; the strip still shows where the journey leads. Hover over a step, focus it with the keyboard, or tap it to see its purpose, completion condition and saved progress. Press Escape or select outside the panel to dismiss it. These panels provide information only; use the visible Next step panel and Tray controls to perform the work. Prepare libraries shows X of Y steps completed and A of B protocols completed across the pinned workflow. Each workflow step and protocol stage counts once, regardless of tube count. A step completes when all continuing tubes have resolved it; partial coverage, unresolved QC and evidence needing review after an earlier step changes keep it incomplete. A protocol completes when its stage has been completed for the continuing tubes. Counts include permitted step and stage skips. Failed tubes remain visible but do not block progress for the remaining tubes; failing a tube does not itself complete a step. Complete batch separately tracks tube outcomes. In the Confirm tray dialog, check I reviewed the tray identities and positions, then choose Confirm tray. The checkbox starts unchecked and is required before confirmation can be saved. Select an occupied tray position to see its tube details, including Specimen type (for example, Human liver) and Declared safety information from the specimen's current saved authorization. Missing declarations appear as Not recorded. These are submitted declarations; a missing safety declaration does not mean that no hazards are present. In the Tray header, scan the label on the physical tray into Scan physical tray barcode, then press Enter or Save tray. This is a one-time assignment. POMS saves that tray identity separately from the batch identifier. The same physical tray cannot belong to two Draft or In progress batches. Completion or cancellation makes it available for another batch while preserving the earlier history. Existing batches without a tray identity require a physical tray scan before adding tubes or confirming the assembly. The saved barcode appears read-only when you return or refresh. Continue loading or confirm the assembled tray without rescanning it. Saving the physical tray identity does not start preparation or approve the contents. The Next step panel gives guidance; use the nearby Tray controls directly. Print tray label reprints the saved physical tray barcode if its label needs replacing; it does not create a new batch identity. An empty, unconfirmed Draft batch can be assigned a different tray using Change tray, scanning the replacement barcode and choosing Save tray. Cancelling a change retains the saved tray. A populated batch must retain its assigned tray; remove the tube assignments before changing trays. Occupied cells show the position and a small QR code. Planned status is summarized at tray level rather than repeated in every cell. Select an occupied cell to show the readable tube barcode, job, specimen, actions and preparation evidence below the grid. Only the selected tube's details appear. The screen QR is a reference; identity confirmation requires scanning the label on the actual tube. Scan an accepted, available tube directly into an empty tray cell. The scanner’s Enter key or the cell’s Save button saves the scan. After a successful save, focus moves left to right, row by row, skipping filled and unavailable cells. If you started partway through the tray, it returns to earlier empty cells after reaching the end. You can select a different empty cell at any time. An invalid or duplicate tube stays in its cell with an error for correction; saving does not start preparation. If another operator has filled the position, review the saved tube and dismiss your unsaved entry before continuing. Tubes may come from different jobs, and positions may remain empty. A specimen can reserve only one source at a time. When the tray is assembled, review the identities and positions and choose Confirm tray in its header. Save or clear unsaved barcode entries first. Confirmation locks tray editing, survives reload, and surfaces Start preparation in the Next step panel. Before starting, Actions → Edit tray reopens it with a reason; confirm it again after making changes. Prepare libraries becomes current once the tray is confirmed. Choose Start preparation in the Next step panel when laboratory work begins. This starts the first workflow stage immediately, records the start time and permanently locks the positions for this batch; there is no additional confirmation dialog. After start, the Tray card collapses to leave room for preparation work. Select its chevron heading to inspect tubes and their details; the scannable tray QR code, its printed identifier and Print tray label remain visible. Review library outputs opens the tray automatically. Reloading a started batch also begins with the tray collapsed. After start, failed tubes remain in its history and reserves must enter a new batch. Supervisors and Protocol Administrators manage library tray formats in Administration → Lab settings → Library tray formats. Choose New library tray format or Edit to set rows, columns, position labels and unavailable positions. Preview the layout before saving. Retiring a format prevents its use for new batches while preserving existing batch layouts. Return to Library prep to select a format when creating a preparation batch. Record steps from the batch in workflow order. The page shows the current stage, with available and already-recorded steps. Later stages and blocked future steps appear as their prerequisites are resolved; recorded evidence remains available through tube details and batch history. Each entry shows Applies to X tubes and an excluded count when relevant. Expand View tube coverage to inspect included tubes and exclusion reasons. Every eligible tube is included automatically, with no tube-selection checkboxes; confirm the coverage before saving. Use an explicit recorded failure action when a tube must stop processing. The approved protocol determines whether a value is one batch entry, an individual tube measurement, or a shared value with identified tube exceptions. Record an exception reason whenever a tube differs from a shared value or QC outcome. Failed tubes cannot inherit later success. A Hold remains unresolved until permitted repeat/correction or explicit attempt failure; it does not automatically start a reserve. When recording a preparation step, each tube shows its Customer sample ID, Specimen type, and linked Accession reference. The accession link opens the specimen in a new tab so the entry remains open. For the standard Specimen reference capture, POMS records the saved accession for each tube automatically; do not copy it into a shared field or supply exception reasons merely because tubes belong to different specimens. Scan the physical source tube barcode and compare its identity with the displayed details. Other observations, dates, confirmations and genuine exceptions still need to be recorded according to the protocol. Enter Identity checked on once in Batch entries; that date is saved with each tube covered by this entry, without a separate per-tube date field. Automatic accession recording does not confirm that a physical identity check was performed. If a tube fails an identity check and its preparation attempt must be disqualified, choose Close attempt as failed in that tube's section of the step-entry modal. The confirmation names the tube and requires a Failure reason and Reason and evidence. Back to step returns without closing the attempt. After a successful failure, the tube remains visible in its original tray position and in the modal, marked Failed, with its identity, failure reason and recorded evidence available as read-only information. It cannot be selected for new step evidence. The shared date and other tubes' values remain in place; review and confirm the remaining tube coverage before saving. You can also access the failure action by selecting the tube in Tray (under Actions when other actions are available). While the failure is saving, wait for confirmation before returning to the step. Failed tubes remain available for inspection even when you choose Skip with reason for an optional step. The active and failed counts distinguish tubes that can continue from those still occupying the tray. Closing an attempt does not record physical removal. Unsaved entries for a newly failed tube may remain visible for reference while the modal stays open; they are not saved as step evidence. Failed tubes remain visible when you reopen the modal. For Review a prior input QC hold in the established test protocol, POMS automatically records a skip when every active sample has resolved prior steps, passing input QC, and no Hold or Fail anywhere in its input QC history. Failed tubes are excluded. The check runs after saving step evidence or a tube failure, and when an authorized user opens an already eligible batch. The existing step role is still required. Batch history identifies the automatic skip, covered tubes and reason, and the Next step panel moves forward. If any active sample has a prior Hold or Fail, even after a passing repeat, the review remains pending. Missing evidence also prevents an automatic skip. Other written conditions still need an explicit assessment. An earlier correction may require fresh downstream evidence; automatic skipping never replaces an existing review or skip. For the conditional review step, enter Review rationale once. When recording the performed review, POMS also saves that text as the condition assessment. Skipping, repeating or correcting the step still requires a separate reason. Under Sample entries and exceptions, each sample card shows its position and barcode, with Close attempt as failed at the right end of the header. All sample cards, including failed tubes, start collapsed when the modal opens. Select the position and barcode to expand or collapse the sample details. The standard identity check omits Tube exception or QC reason when there are no shared-value exceptions or tube QC decisions to explain. Other steps retain this field for non-fatal exceptions and QC holds. Closing an attempt as failed preserves its history and prevents its output from supplying a successful sequencing library. An exception note alone does not fail a tube; excluding it from an entry only leaves that step unrecorded for it. Record failure before continuing the remaining tubes. In preparation QC steps, QC report (optional) appears after the other step-entry fields, before the final configured confirmation. It lets you choose one PDF up to 10 MB for the tubes covered by the entry. The report uploads only when you choose Save step record. You may remove the selection. Saving without a report is permitted only when the step makes it optional. POMS records the report reference, operator and timestamp automatically. After saving, download it from Batch history or the tube's Current sample records. It is internal laboratory evidence. Attaching a report does not select a QC outcome or replace required measurements and confirmations. An unsuccessful upload or file scan leaves the step unsaved so you can retry or remove the file. The test protocols no longer require copying a synthetic QC record reference; earlier saved references remain in history. For library preparation, Preparation report or worksheet (optional) appears after the other step-entry fields, before the final configured confirmation, in place of the manual preparation record reference. Choose one PDF up to 10 MB, or continue without a file. POMS records its reference automatically when you save the step record. Download it later from batch history or current sample records. Preparation mode, protocol-required materials and equipment, and output barcode evidence remain required. In the step modal, record configured material and equipment fields directly in Batch entries or the appropriate sample card. These values save together with Save step record. Resource choices exclude expired material lots and equipment past its calibration due date; POMS rechecks eligibility when you save. Output fields offer common quantity, unit and storage values with individual overrides. Saving creates a separate output barcode for each tube; existing outputs are shown without being recreated. Unavailable tubes cannot receive an output. Output creation does not confirm physical identity; scan each output barcode using Confirm output identity when ready. After all required steps and QC resolve, choose Complete protocol. The confirmation names the batch and protocol and explains what completing it will do; no additional data entry is required. The final stage requires a confirmed output barcode for every successful tube and reuses recorded QC to establish library eligibility. The Next step panel offers Complete preparation batch after every tube has succeeded with a library or explicitly failed. Sequencing handoff appears only after the batch is complete and passing libraries are available. Each passing library has an Add to sequencing batch action and shows its destination after assignment. A batch with no passing libraries retains its outcomes without offering handoff. Scientific result review remains separate. An output from a failed attempt remains visible for traceability but cannot supply a sequencing library; it does not require output confirmation. Existing specimen and execution pages link batch-owned work back to its tray. Historical individual executions retain their original entry workflow and evidence.

sections.heading: Record a material amount exception
sections.text: Configure a material field as Same entry with sample exceptions when the protocol permits recording different actual amounts. This uses Amount per sample; total batch amounts do not have sample overrides. Product, lot and unit stay shared. Existing approved configurations keep their original recording scope. Enter the common quantity and lot in Batch entries. Select Record exception, expand the affected sample, and select Record a different amount for this sample. Enter its actual quantity, including zero if none was added, or select Amount unknown. Record a Material exception reason and choose the Tube outcome: Continue — permitted variation records a known amount and lets the tube continue subject to the protocol and QC requirements. The choice does not approve a scientific deviation. Hold for review prevents further processing until a Supervisor resolves the operational hold. Close attempt as failed closes the attempt while retaining the tube in the tray and preserving its material use. An unknown amount requires hold or failure. Save step record saves the quantities, exception reasons and outcomes together. The common amount applies only to samples without an override; each known override replaces that sample's share. Failed tubes still consume what was actually used. Unknown quantities place the tracked lot on hold for reconciliation in Materials. No amount is guessed or returned to stock. When several material exceptions affect a tube, failure takes precedence over hold. While entering material exceptions, use the outcome field and save the step; the immediate failure button is unavailable to protect unsaved material entries. Clearing Record exception discards unsaved material overrides. Corrections retain previously recorded resource use. To release an operational material hold, a Supervisor reviews the selected tube and chooses Resolve hold, with a reason; any uncertain lot must first be reconciled. Failed attempts cannot be resumed.

sections.heading: Build the service workflow
sections.text: In Administration → Lab settings, Lab steps opens by default. Use the sidebar for Protocols, Workflows, Stage durations, Holiday calendar, and Library tray formats. Each section has its own link, so refreshing or returning from a builder restores the relevant section. Retired protocols are hidden by default; select Show retired to include them. Protocols with only discarded versions are excluded from the working list, including when Show retired is selected. Discarded revisions remain labeled Discarded in the associated protocol's read-only version history, with no editing or creation actions on those revisions. Newly created protocols without a saved version remain visible. In the Workflows tab, create one Controlled service workflow for each active marketed laboratory service. POMS takes the service identity from the active Commercial catalog; do not type or maintain a separate product key. Choose Add version to open the workflow builder. Arrange stages in operating order and select the exact Approved protocol version for each stage. Mark each stage Required, Optional, or Conditional. A Conditional stage requires a plain-language condition. Add handoff criteria when the next stage depends on recorded evidence or a specific state. Save the Draft, then use its Actions menu to continue editing or approve it. Approved versions offer Promote to production and Withdraw approval in Actions; Invalid versions offer Review workflow, Revalidate and approve, and Discard. Promote to production makes the complete workflow the default for new standalone source selections using the exact Approved protocol versions selected in its stages. The previous Production workflow becomes Retired; existing attempts and batches retain their original workflow and protocol versions. A service has only one Production workflow at a time. The workflow and every included protocol must have recorded independent approval or an explicit administrator approval override before promotion. Once those approvals exist, an authorized Protocol Administrator may promote the workflow even if they authored the workflow or one of its protocols. Promotion records the actor and time and preserves the original approvals.

sections.heading: Control protocol versions
sections.text: For a new preparation-compatible version, select Use this version for preparation batches and explicitly choose each capture's evidence scope and each QC gate's scope. Barcode identity captures must use Tube scope. Use individual scope for measurements that must be taken separately; shared entries do not represent individual measurements. Older approved versions do not gain scopes automatically. Follow the approval workflow below before using the new version. A Protocol Administrator creates the protocol by entering its name and optional description, then continues directly to the structured definition builder. POMS derives a readable, immutable protocol key from the name and adds a suffix if that key is already in use. The key remains available in Edit name and description before approval when it is useful for support or integration matching, but the working list does not repeat it as user-facing protocol information. Open the protocol's labeled Actions menu. Choose Edit protocol to change the Draft's ordered steps, captures, resources, or QC gates. Edit name and description is available only until the first approval; after approval, create a new protocol identity if the name no longer represents the controlled method. The system-assigned key never changes. An identity without a saved definition is labeled Setup incomplete. Choose Edit protocol to build its initial Draft; the interface does not present this first definition as a new version. After a version is Approved, choose Create new version. The initial definition starts blank and offers an optional library-preparation example. A later version starts with the Approved definition. Build the procedure in execution order and use Add step, the move controls, duplicate, and remove actions to maintain that order. Replace example or copied content with the intended laboratory procedure before saving. For each step, enter a name and operator instructions, then choose whether the step is required, optional, or conditional. Conditional steps require a plain-language condition. Record whether the step may repeat, whether explicit confirmation is required, and whether a particular laboratory role is required. Confirmation required adds one step-completion attestation as the last field, after the report upload; it applies to every permitted role, including Supervisor. Turning it off removes the instruction-specific attestation; a new performed step still needs confirmation of who did the work and when. There is no separate tube-coverage checkbox: Save step record submits the automatically included eligible tubes, which POMS rechecks. Add captured values only when the approved procedure requires them. Captures may be numbers, text, dates, choices, file references, or barcodes. Number captures may identify a unit, and choice captures require their permitted choices. For a barcode that identifies the original specimen tube, select Must match the selected source tube. POMS then checks it against the attempt source. Existing approved definitions are unchanged; add this setting through a controlled new version when appropriate. Barcodes identifying recorded containers must belong to the current attempt’s lineage. Use Material used, Equipment used, and Output created fields for resource recording. Older comma- or line-separated requirements remain readable and can be converted explicitly in a draft. A QC gate records explicit Pass, Fail, or Hold outcomes and requires acceptance criteria. Use the collapsed JSON preview only to review or copy the portable representation; do not author protocol JSON directly. Create protocol draft validates the complete definition and reserves the next version number. Cancelling after edits warns before discarding the unsaved definition. Each protocol can have only one Draft. While a Draft exists, Edit protocol replaces Create new version. Saving returns to the Protocols list, where the state is shown as Draft vN and the Actions menu exposes Review and approve. Standard approval is a formal, irreversible controlled release. Review and approve shows the exact ordered definition, whether preparation batches are enabled, each capture and QC scope, and source-tube matching requirements. Review these scopes to distinguish a shared observation from evidence recorded for each tube. Approval requires an explicit attestation, requires an independent Protocol Administrator who did not author the version, and records that approver and timestamp. Approval locks the version and makes it the Approved version for future use. If another version was previously Approved, it becomes Superseded; work and service workflows already pinned to it remain unchanged. Before any version has been approved, the Actions menu offers Delete protocol to permanently remove the protocol and all its Draft or previously Discarded versions after confirmation. It does not offer Discard draft at this stage. Once any version has been approved, deletion is unavailable; Discard draft lets you abandon a proposed revision while retaining that version as Discarded in history. Approved, Superseded, and Discarded versions remain immutable and available to explain protocol history. A protocol referenced by a laboratory record cannot be deleted.

sections.heading: Administrator approval override
sections.text: Independent approval remains the normal path. If you authored the version and are an active platform administrator with protocol-management access, its Actions menu also offers Approve with administrator override. Review the exact protocol definition or workflow stages, enter a required Override reason, and explicitly confirm responsibility for bypassing independent review. Choose Approve with override. The saved version shows Administrator override, the reason and approval time; POMS retains your actual identity and the change in its audit history. It never records another person's approval. An override applies only to the selected version. It does not waive valid definitions, preparation evidence/QC scopes, current protocols, permissions or version checks. A workflow still requires separate Promote to production before it becomes the default for new standalone source selections. Recorded overrides satisfy that promotion's approval check; older self-approvals without an override record do not. Withdraw approval removes the current workflow approval and override, while retaining the audit history. Approving again requires a new review and either independent approval or a new explicit override. Scientific review and result-release rules are unchanged.

sections.heading: Select a specimen and source
sections.text: Record actions appear as a named button when only one action is shown, or in Actions when multiple options are shown. Instructions written as Actions → action name refer to the direct button when it is the only option. Use Specimens → Tubes → Execution → Libraries → Exceptions → Review in that order as work progresses. Actions → Manage specimen attempts returns to the specimen list. Each sample opens its own page with recognizable sample ID, received/expected counts, intake decision and separate processing progress. Complete tube intake during accessioning; Tubes shows the recorded decisions. On the specimen page, choose Actions → Select source tube, choose an accepted available tube and scan its exact barcode. For a new standalone attempt, POMS uses the service’s current Production workflow; existing matching Planned execution records retain their recorded procedure. Saving reserves that source and assigns the first workflow stage together. To use an Approved preparation workflow, add the tube directly through that preparation batch instead. It does not start processing. Unreceived, unreviewed, held, rejected, unavailable or previously failed tubes cannot be selected. Extra tubes remain reserves. On an older unstarted job with no recorded tube-use instruction, a Supervisor must first choose Confirm tube-use instruction, review the order and record a reason. Selecting the source adopts a matching existing Planned first-stage execution; it does not duplicate it. Historical started work is never assigned a source retrospectively and is flagged for review. An unstarted attempt can be cancelled with a reason to release its reservation. After start, the source is fixed. Completing one protocol does not release the source: assign the next stage from the same specimen's Actions menu. Complete stages in order within that attempt. Required stages cannot be skipped; Optional and Conditional stages need an explicit decision and reason. A replacement tube begins a new attempt at the first stage of the workflow selected for that attempt; earlier evidence is not reused.

sections.heading: Failure, reserve use and exhaustion
sections.text: A QC Hold or failed repeatable reading keeps the current attempt unresolved; it does not automatically authorize a reserve. Repeat a permitted step or resolve the evidence in that attempt. Hold attempt records a reason and the next action owned by the person recording it. Resolve attempt hold requires a resolution before work resumes. When the attempt cannot continue, choose Close attempt as failed. Select a predefined processing-failure reason, a started execution and the evidence/reference. This closes the attempt while retaining completed work, consumed materials, equipment records and output lineage. It does not dispose of the tube. Failed-attempt outputs cannot proceed into a replacement attempt, batching or release. If another eligible tube remains, choose Use reserve tube and explicitly select/scan it. Review the failed source, failure reason and restart point. A new linked attempt begins at the first workflow stage; earlier completed stages do not count for the replacement. Only one attempt may be active, and a successful attempt prevents further source selection. When no reserve is currently eligible, processing waits On hold with a material-resolution explanation and next action. Expected tubes or potentially usable tubes awaiting review must be resolved first. After terminal failure with no material remaining for further permitted analysis, use Confirm material exhausted, record evidence and confirm the specimen Failed outcome. Its earlier intake acceptance remains intact. Close any resulting follow-up exception separately after review. No receipt, review or exception resolution automatically starts a reserve.

sections.heading: Retire a protocol
sections.text: A Protocol Administrator can choose Actions → Retire protocol after a protocol has been approved. Enter a retirement reason. Discard any open protocol draft first. Retirement is final and preserves identity, definitions, approvals and execution history. Use Show retired to see its reason and date. The dialog checks affected workflows and work before allowing confirmation: If samples are in process, retirement is blocked and the affected jobs are listed. This includes unfinished workflows whose earlier executions have started or completed. If work is assigned but has not started, POMS warns that retirement may strand it. Choose Proceed anyway only after reviewing those jobs. Cancel leaves everything unchanged. If workflows use the protocol, POMS warns that they will become invalid. Confirmation retires the protocol and invalidates affected workflows together. Changes to the displayed impact require a fresh review. POMS creates a new Invalid recovery revision with the retired protocol removed and the remaining stages kept in order. Previous versions, stages and approval records remain historical. Open Review workflow to inspect or modify the remaining procedure. Revalidate and approve checks that at least one stage remains and every stage uses an eligible approved protocol, and applies the normal independent-review rule. Further edits are optional when the remaining procedure is already correct. Explicit Promote to production is still required before the revised workflow governs new work. Queued attempts retain their original assignments and display Execution workflow needs review when their procedure is unavailable. They cannot begin processing under an invalidated version. Cancel an unstarted attempt with a reason before selecting a replacement procedure. A commercial job without an attempt is not tied to the retired workflow. Approving a replacement never changes started work. If retirement removes every stage, open Review workflow and choose Add stage to add an eligible replacement. Save the revision, then have an independent reviewer revalidate it. Saving alone leaves the workflow Invalid.

sections.heading: Record execution
sections.text: On the laboratory job's Execution tab, open the execution link. The dedicated workspace shows its pinned protocol version, specimen, instructions, resource requirements, saved evidence, and remaining completion blockers. For a Planned specimen execution without an accepted available tube, Tube acceptance required explains the prerequisite and Open tubes opens the job's Tubes tab. Start execution also requires an explicitly selected source attempt. Use Open specimen and source if selection is missing; accepting a tube alone does not select it. Return after accessioning to refresh eligibility. Choose Actions → Start execution and scan the selected source barcode again. POMS rechecks current eligibility before recording any start. Choose Record for the next step. Enter the measurements, dates, approved choices, file references, and barcodes required by the procedure. Units appear beside the relevant capture. A file reference records an identifier; it does not upload a file. Confirm performed work when the procedure requires it. POMS checks the saved values against the pinned definition and records your identity and the time. Use Material and Equipment on the job to record consumed lots and quantities, output-container references, and equipment use. Before confirming a step's resources, check the listed inputs, outputs, and equipment against that traceability. Resource descriptions and QC acceptance criteria are controlled instructions assessed by the operator; POMS does not infer scientific thresholds or match free-text resource descriptions automatically. Enter a quantity greater than zero and no more than the lot's available stock. If the quantity is unavailable, correct the entry and save again; the rejected attempt does not deduct stock or add a consumption record. Resolve every optional and conditional step with recorded evidence or an allowed skip. The preparation review described above can record its skip automatically; other conditional steps require an explicit decision. An allowed Skip with reason requires the reason or condition assessment. Required steps cannot be skipped, and previously performed work cannot be changed into a skip. A step with a specified Lab role must be recorded by a user with that effective role. Earlier steps must be resolved before later evidence is recorded. For a QC gate, deliberately choose Pass, Fail, or Hold. Fail and Hold require a reason. They remain visible as saved evidence, mark the execution Blocked, and prevent later steps and completion until resolved through an allowed repeat or correction. Saved progress remains available when you leave and return. When all steps and QC gates are satisfied, choose Actions → Complete execution, add an optional deviation note, and confirm completion. POMS rechecks the persisted evidence and locks the completed execution. A held or finished laboratory job cannot accept new execution evidence.

sections.heading: Recover safely
sections.text: Do not edit an Approved definition to repair an execution. If a protocol is wrong, create and approve a new version; update and approve the service workflow separately when its stage composition must change. If execution data is wrong, use the supported correction or repeat-work path while preserving the original record and reason. Repeat is available only when the pinned procedure allows it. Correct repairs a data-entry error and requires a Supervisor who also has the step's required role. Both require a reason, fresh confirmations, and a new saved record. Expand Step history to review every earlier value, QC outcome, reason, operator, and timestamp. If an earlier step changes, later evidence must be reviewed and recorded again before completion. If another user changes the execution during a save, POMS reloads the current record and preserves your entered values. Review the latest history before saving again. If the original action is no longer available, close the form and use an allowed repeat or correction. Abandon execution remains available for eligible historical, unlinked work and retains its evidence with a reason. For an attempt-linked execution, cancel the unstarted attempt or explicitly close the started attempt as failed from the specimen page; ordinary abandonment cannot authorize reserve use. Historical unstructured definitions or results remain preserved with a recovery message; a Protocol Administrator must prepare a valid new approved version for new work. POMS does not silently rewrite controlled history.

sections.heading: Who can perform work
sections.text: Source and attempt actions require an effective Operator or Supervisor role. Each protocol step additionally checks its required role. POMS retains the actual person recording each action; an earlier assignment never grants permission to perform a step. If you edit an attempt action and then cancel, press Escape, or leave the page, POMS asks before discarding your unsaved details. Declining keeps your entries. While a save is pending, wait for its result before closing or navigating away. If another operator changes the record, your entries remain available; close the action, review the latest specimen state, and reopen the action that is still appropriate.

guides.title: Receipt and accession
guides.summary: Dispatch barcoded containers to Customer locations, track inventory and assignments, and record receipt and accession for each registered tube.

sections.heading: Receipt and accession
sections.text: Receipt and accession connect the Customer’s submitted specimen identity to the physical material handled in the laboratory. Record these steps in sequence and never create an unlinked laboratory specimen. The first recorded shipment arrival moves an awaiting Job into Lab operations → Lab work with the milestone Received. Its commercial order moves to In progress, while the Customer/Partner Job list displays Received. Customer progress uses Received, Library Prep, Sequencing, Data Assembly, Quality Review and Results Available, with current counts and individual sample stages in After you send. Only recorded provider sequencing establishes Sequencing; sendout alone does not. Scientific approval remains distinct from released results. It remains in Lab work while you accession tubes, including when other containers are outstanding. A completed container leaves the accession queue; its tubes and freezer-box values remain in the Job's Tubes tab. Verified tube receipt updates the sample's receipt progress. The commercial sample becomes Accessioned after all its expected tubes across active shipments are accessioned. Order updates can take a few seconds. Container receipt alone does not accept tubes. During tube accession, confirm the receipt checks: Accepted is the normal outcome, with no reason code required. A specimen becomes Accepted when at least one of its tubes is Accepted; its acceptance-based turnaround target starts then. This intake decision is separate from laboratory QC and scientific review. Use the tabs in Lab operations → Receipt & accession to focus on one task: Kit requests: review Customer orders and fulfill requested kits. Prepare kits: prepare stock and review kit inventory and deliveries. Kits sent: finish previously prepared shipment-specific kits and review their recorded fulfillment dates. Dates use your local time zone; a dash means fulfillment has not been recorded. Receive shipments: review expected containers and tracking numbers; scan the PH-P- insert to acknowledge container arrival. Accession samples: open a received container, then scan and accession its individual tubes. Kit requests and Prepare kits require the existing configuration-administrator permission; opening these queues does not require a laboratory execution role. Your selected tab and queue filters stay in the page address; returning from a request or kit reopens its queue. Switching tabs during a visit retains the accession lookup draft and its results. Existing shipment links open the shipment-specific return-kit tab.

sections.heading: Fulfill Customer transportation-kit orders
sections.text: Open Lab operations → Receipt & accession → Kit requests to review Customer transportation-kit orders. New orders notify Phaeno administrators for fulfillment. Open a request to review its Customer, Department, Job, requested sizes and quantities, and the delivery address saved when the Customer confirmed. Transportation kits and outbound delivery are included with the accepted laboratory order; this action creates no additional quote, invoice or payment step. Use Record kit shipment to choose matching, fully registered physical kits and enter the carrier, tracking number and dispatch time, then select Record dispatch. If there is insufficient prepared stock, prepare and register more standard kits before returning to the request. Registration alone does not fulfill the request: it can still show Pending and zero dispatched kits until dispatch is recorded here. A partial dispatch leaves the remaining requested quantities outstanding. The kit order and saved delivery address remain linked to each dispatched kit. Dispatch adds those kits to the Customer delivery location's inventory as On the way. The Customer acknowledges the containers that arrive, moving them to Available. Unused available stock may supply any eligible Job at that Customer/Department/location; the originating Job is delivery history, not a restriction on use. Cancelling the originating Job does not consume delivered unused stock. Customer acknowledgment is separate from the laboratory's later receipt of returned samples. Kits not yet acknowledged remain unavailable, and a partial receipt permits only the received portion. Maintain delivery locations from the Customer's Departments workspace or the Department's delivery-location screen. Open a location and use Actions → Edit location in the page header. These locations belong to the Customer and Department, and are separate from global lab receiving destinations. Changing a saved location does not rewrite a confirmed kit order's delivery address. The Customer location workspace provides inventory and receipt access even if the originating Job has been cancelled. The request shows what to do next. If no matching kits are ready, choose Prepare kits to open preparation for the missing sizes. Prepare each physical kit, register its tube barcodes, then use Back to kit request. Once matching kits are ready, Record kit shipment selects the kits and records the carrier, tracking number and shipment time after handoff. A partially ready request can ship its available kits while the remaining sizes are prepared. Preparation does not reserve stock or record a shipment.

sections.heading: Suppliers and products
sections.text: Phaeno platform administrators manage Suppliers & Products in the Lab operations sidebar, before Materials and Equipment. Choose New supplier, enter its name, and save. Open the supplier name to see its products. Choose New product and enter the Product #, a required Product description, and Product type from the saved active types. Vendors can supply reagents, tubes, shipping containers, and other products from the same supplier record. Product numbers must be unique within each supplier, including inactive products. Each supplier and product row has an Actions menu. Choose Edit to correct details, or Deactivate and review the application confirmation to make the record inactive. Show inactive reveals those records; choose Actions → Activate to restore them. The supplier detail header offers the same actions. Inactivating a supplier prevents selection of all its products for new kits; it does not alter prepared kits. Inactive product types also prevent their products from being selected for new kits. The tube Lot remains specific to each kit preparation and is not stored in the product catalog.

sections.heading: Manage product types
sections.text: Open Lab operations → Suppliers & Products and select the Product types tab to manage the categories offered by your vendors. Tube, Shipping Container, and Reagent are provided initially. Choose New product type and enter a unique name, description, and Use in transportation kits. For reagents and other supplies, choose Not used in transportation kits. A vendor can offer products of several types. Open a type's name to review its description, status, kit use, and product count. Each type has an Actions menu in its list row and detail header. Choose Edit to change its details, or Deactivate to make it inactive after reviewing the confirmation. Use Show inactive, then Actions → Activate, to restore a type. Once products reference a type, its kit use cannot change; create a different type when that classification needs to differ. Existing products retain inactive type references for review and correction, but new products must choose an active type. Inactivating a type preserves kit history. Reagent vendors use the same supplier directory as Materials. Reagent product catalog entries do not create material lots, receive stock, or record QC; those remain separate Materials actions.

sections.heading: Prepare and register standard kits
sections.text: Open Lab operations → Receipt & accession → Prepare kits. Search by kit number, size, SKU, location or Job, or filter by inventory status. Open the kit number to review its products, registered tubes, location, receipt, outbound tracking and any current assignment. Distinguish the originating request's Job from the Job currently using the container. Choose Prepare standard kit, select an active configured container size, and complete the two sections: Tubes contains Supplier, Product name, and optional Lot; Shipping Container contains Supplier and Product name. Select a saved supplier, then choose its product number and description. Only active suppliers and products of the correct type are available. Changing a supplier clears the product selection. The configured size supplies the usable tube capacity and preselects its shipper reference only when it matches an active catalog product. Product details are saved with the kit, so later catalog changes do not rewrite its history. A new kit does not yet belong to a Customer Job. Open the kit and choose Register tubes. Scan each permanent supplier barcode on its own line. A kit must contain exactly its full configured tube capacity before dispatch; duplicate scans and excess tubes are rejected. The kit's own permanent number is its container barcode; print its label and keep the readable number with the barcode. A fully registered kit is ready stock at Phaeno. Return to Kit requests, open the request, and use Record kit shipment to select that kit and record dispatch to its confirmed address. The kit's Record dispatch action also selects a request and displays its frozen delivery address. Both entry points update the same request and stock exactly once. Dispatch supplies the location; the Customer later assigns the container to a Job during preparation by scanning its barcode. On the way means dispatched but not yet acknowledged. Available means received and unassigned at the Customer location. Assigned means the Customer confirmed this container for a Job/shipment; In use means tube scanning has begun. Reset before the first tube scan releases an assignment to available inventory. After scanning, ordinary reset/reassignment remains locked. Needs review identifies incomplete location or receipt history that must be resolved before use. The original request, tracking and receipt remain distinct from the consuming Job. If an older kit is already sent but its request still shows an outstanding quantity, the kit page offers Update kit request when the saved dispatch has one eligible matching request. Review the existing carrier, tracking number and dispatch time, then confirm Update kit request. This links the existing dispatch; it does not send another kit or confirm Customer receipt. A failed update keeps the confirmation available for review and retry. Existing Trial and Partner supply workflows remain unchanged. Use the configuration workflow to qualify or revise container sizes rather than changing a kit's capacity.

sections.heading: Delivery deadline before acceptance
sections.text: Every job must have a delivery due date when its first sample is accepted. The saved standard turnaround calculates the date automatically. When no turnaround is recorded, an operator or supervisor opens the job and chooses Actions → Set due date, enters the delivery date/time and a customer-safe reason, then returns to acceptance. Acceptance cannot be saved until the date is set. Receipt and holding or rejecting a tube do not start the turnaround clock.

sections.heading: Receive a shipment
sections.text: Open Lab operations → Receipt & accession → Receive shipments. Expected shipments lists each expected container separately, including the Customer, Job, carrier, tracking number and expected tube count. Containers still being prepared remain visible with their current status; missing tracking is shown as not recorded. When a container physically arrives, scan the PH-P- barcode under Scan to receive this shipment in the body of its shipping insert in Shipping insert barcode, then submit with Enter or Receive shipment. This action records the container's arrival time and staff audit event. The confirmation identifies the shipment and offers Accession samples at the right of its first row. Repeating the same scan shows the original receipt without creating another event. Invalid, replaced or cancelled inserts cannot receive a container. A failed response leaves receipt unconfirmed in the screen; scanning again safely checks or completes that receipt. This receiving field accepts only the shipping insert's PH-P- code. The SHP… shipment reference, PH-S- shipment barcode, PH-O- Order barcode, PH-M- sample barcode, physical KIT- container barcode and individual tube barcodes do not acknowledge container arrival here. Receipt of a container does not accession its tubes or accept its samples for processing.

sections.heading: Open a received container
sections.text: Choose Accession samples. Received containers awaiting accession shows containers that have arrived and still have tubes to accession. Open the shipment reference or scan its PH-P- insert. This lookup is read-only. Within this tab, a PH-S- barcode opens the shipment's current confirmed insert, and PH-O- or PH-M- lookups let you choose a related manifest. The readable SHP… reference and physical KIT- barcode are not accepted by the lookup field. The shipping insert opens the accession dialog with every expected tube and its saved intake decision. Once the shipment details have loaded, the Supplier tube barcode field receives keyboard focus unless you have already moved to another control. Inspect tubes before storage. Scan each available physical tube in Supplier tube barcode and press Enter or Identify tube. Identification selects the tube for this session; it does not save acceptance or a storage location. Record the exceptions first. Choose Record exception on the expected tube's row. Select Rejected or On hold and a predefined reason. Confirm that the received tube or damaged remains match that shipment row. A broken tube whose barcode cannot be scanned can still be rejected against its expected identity. Missing tubes remain outstanding; do not mark them received merely because they appear on the insert. A broken or destroyed rejected tube requires no freezer location and is unavailable for processing. POMS retains its expected-tube link, rejection reason, notes, actor and time. No remaining quantity is asserted for a non-stored rejection. If rejected material is actually retained, its real storage location may be recorded. An internally held tube must have a real retained-material location. Rejection itself does not record disposal. The modal footer shows X with exceptions | Y to be accepted. Exceptions count tubes on hold or rejected in this shipment; the acceptance count includes only identified tubes with no saved decision. After exceptions are saved, choose Accept (Y). Previously accepted, held, rejected and unidentified tubes are excluded. Review the listed identities, record each actual freezer-box barcode, and confirm inspection. Accept N tubes saves the entire batch together. Routine acceptance needs no reason code. Storage is recorded as entered; POMS does not validate a freezer registry or assign a position within the box. If any selected tube changed, the whole batch is refused. Your entries stay visible; close the acceptance dialog and review the refreshed selection before trying again. For an uncertain connection result, retry the same request. A completed batch is returned without duplicate intake records. Bulk acceptance cannot relocate a previously stored tube. POMS assigns or reuses the specimen's accession number and preserves each supplier barcode. A rejected received tube completes that tube's receipt handling without becoming acceptable material. The specimen becomes Accepted when at least one tube is Accepted. Complete receipt handling and scientific acceptance are separate facts. Clear selection removes the unsaved identified selection without changing any saved intake decision. Saved exceptions survive closing. Unsaved identified selections and storage entries prompt before being discarded. When all expected tubes have decisions, choose Done. Historical tubes with no intake decision are not automatically accepted: identify and inspect them explicitly in this accession dialog, or ask a supervisor to document a correction from the tube details.

sections.heading: Other specimen and label actions
sections.text: The Lab work record retains individual receipt and accession actions for supported legacy intake. Its Tubes tab shows Received tubes, with clear intake and storage information. Open a tube barcode to see its receipt evidence, storage and lineage. POMS-generated container labels are available from the detail page’s Actions menu. The label window renders the current container identity as a QR code through the browser and installed printer driver. Enter the reason, open the system print dialog, and inspect the physical label before choosing Label printed. POMS increments the print count only after that confirmation. If the label did not print correctly, enter the failure details and choose Record failed attempt; the failure remains in history without falsely counting a usable label. Every POMS-generated label reprint requires a reason and renders the same current container identity. A reprint or failed attempt adds a separate history event; it does not replace the barcode or erase an earlier print. Registered supplier tubes have no POMS print action. Verify readable text, barcode, accession, container, and adhesion using the approved bench procedure before processing continues.

sections.heading: Scan and locate a container
sections.text: Use Library prep > Scan a container to find the exact work order, accession, container status, location, parent barcode, and associated library. Place the cursor in the container-barcode field and scan either an adopted registered supplier barcode or a POMS-generated barcode. Code 39 start and stop characters and letter case are normalized; an altered checksum, incomplete barcode, or unknown barcode is rejected without opening another record. The field returns focus after the result so repeated scans remain efficient.

sections.heading: Preserve physical lineage
sections.text: Create child containers for aliquots, prepared reagents, libraries, or other derived materials. Select the immediate parent container and record the quantity and unit required by the approved procedure. POMS assigns each child container its own barcode and opens its label window after creation. The lineage must allow an operator to scan a derived container and trace it through its immediate parent to the submitted specimen. Do not reuse a barcode, move material by editing its parent, or delete a container to repair history. Record the supported correction or new derived container.

sections.heading: Apply the intake decision
sections.text: Acceptance belongs to the physical tube. A specimen is Accepted if one or more of its tubes is Accepted, even if another tube is held or rejected. With no accepted tubes, the specimen remains Received (awaiting an acceptable tube), or On hold if a tube is held. Do not use specimen intake to represent a processing hold; job holds and workflow exceptions remain separate. Routine intake is performed during accessioning. On hold and Rejected require a predefined reason: identity/labeling mismatch, damaged container, leaking container, insufficient material, unacceptable receipt condition, missing information, or Other. Other requires an explanation. POMS retains each decision, stable reason code, notes, reviewer and time. These codes describe intake, not later processing failures. An authorized Supervisor can open Tubes → tube barcode → Actions → Correct intake decision before the tube is used. Every correction requires an explanation; held or rejected decisions still require their reason code. A non-stored record can be restored to Accepted or On hold only when material actually exists and a real storage location is provided. This action does not move stored material. A used source's original intake is locked: handle later problems through the specimen attempt hold or failure actions. Historical processing without a source link retains the earlier specimen-wide lock. Customer-requested hold management is not available. Internal intake questions and attempt holds remain separate from customer requests. Customer communication uses the existing customer-safe exception workflow. Portal-generated identifiers now render as QR codes, with the exact identifier printed underneath. Shipping inserts, container labels, kit records and displayed sample/tube identifiers use the same format. Use a QR-capable 2D scanner. Existing manufacturer labels and older printed barcodes remain valid; do not relabel a tube or change its saved identity merely to match the new display. A scan still requires the correct workflow and does not by itself confirm receipt or accession.

sections.heading: Choose which tube to process
sections.text: Open the sample's identifier in Specimens to see its tubes together. For a single purchased run, use one source tube and a reserve only after failure. When the sample has multiple purchased runs, one prepared library can supply several runs. Prepare another library only when that is the recorded choice; confirm remaining material before reusing a successful source tube. See Libraries, batches, and sequencing for the repeated-run workflow. Acceptance and physical availability determine which sources can be selected; receipt itself never starts work. Tubes precedes Execution in the job navigation. Once a source attempt starts, that source's intake history is locked. Record an attempt hold or failure when processing cannot continue; unused reserve intake can be completed during accessioning or corrected by a supervisor. A specimen's intake can remain Accepted even when processing ultimately fails. See the protocol execution guide for source selection, explicit failure, reserve restart and confirmed material exhaustion.

guides.title: Scientific approval and release readiness
guides.summary: Review output packages, source-tube lineage and scientific evidence requirements, resolve performer/time reviews, and record independent scientific approval.

sections.heading: Scientific approval and release readiness
sections.text: Open Lab operations → Results & review, then select a job to inspect its scientific review. Jobs may appear before their evidence is complete; appearing here does not establish approval or release readiness. Scientific approval is the final Lab Ops decision. It confirms that the authorized laboratory work satisfied the configured execution and exception gates. It is not a Customer file publication action.

sections.heading: Enter scientific review
sections.text: Move work into Scientific review only after required receipt, accession, executions, QC, libraries, batches, and sendout facts are complete for the approved release scope. Confirm that every assigned execution is completed or explicitly abandoned, every blocking exception is resolved, and the registered final-result package has every expected checksummed, malware-clean artifact. The Scientific Reviewer should be able to trace the submitted specimen through containers, material lots, equipment, protocol versions, captured results, library preparation, batches, and provider custody as applicable. POMS checks the recorded chain from the result through its analysis inputs, sequencing output, library and successful processing attempt to the exact source tube. Every result file must identify which content belongs to that sample and analysis. Missing or conflicting links block review and release; notes cannot substitute for those links. Have the producing team register or correct the evidence before retrying. Older results remain available, but missing historical links are not guessed or filled from the most recent attempt. A replacement preserves the original package and records its correction reason. Recorded lineage identifies the producing material; it does not by itself establish scientific validity.

sections.heading: Scientific evidence requirements
sections.text: The producing team can record the required information from the specimen's Sample history, using Record sequencing output and Record analysis run. Both staff and pipeline registration pin the current scientific requirements on new analyses. File and run names open the detailed evidence; corrections and reanalysis preserve the preceding record. Reviewers retain read access without receiving capture authority. Scientific evidence requirements apply before new approvals and releases, including work already in progress. Sample history shows each analysis's saved requirement assessment. The producing team must record sequencing QC and run times, analysis software versions, settings checksum, reference versions, exact input roles/checksums and result attribution. QC needs a summary with named metrics or a referenced QC report. A meaningful Not applicable requires an explanation and is available only for QC, software, settings or references. It cannot waive the source tube, sample/run identity, times or file attribution. Missing evidence or pending performer/time review blocks approval and release. A rejected on-behalf entry remains unverified until corrected and independently approved. Review those proposals under Performer and time reviews. Recorded coverage still requires your scientific judgment. Historical analyses without a saved requirements profile remain readable; their evidence is not invented or automatically backfilled. Capture the required evidence and create an attributed replacement before approving or releasing an incomplete older result.

sections.heading: Upload scientific files
sections.text: In Record sequencing output, select the sequencing file under File and sample mapping. POMS uploads and scans the actual file, verifies the stored bytes, and records its fingerprint, size and immutable file identity automatically. Continue selecting the library, submission, purchased run and exact sample/index/lane mapping that produced the file. Use Add document for QC reports and other supporting evidence. Specify what the document represents, then select its file. For analysis settings, upload the configuration file actually used. Software and reference names and versions still describe the scientific process; they are not inferred from file contents. The picker shows the configured maximum size. Wait for uploading, verification and scanning to finish before saving evidence. A rejected upload leaves the previous selection unchanged. Files larger than the limit require an approved larger-file import workflow; entering an external reference is not a substitute in this form. Open the saved scientific record to download its managed files. POMS checks their saved fingerprint and size before returning bytes. Corrections preserve the original record and file; upload a replacement when the file changes. Uploaded files are retained as internal evidence, including uploads made before cancelling an unsaved evidence form, independently of Customer download expiry. Historical references remain visible and are explicitly labelled Not stored in POMS. They are not automatically imported or verified. Upload the original file when recording an attributed correction. A retained historical settings fingerprint also does not establish file custody.

sections.heading: Record the approval
sections.text: Choose Record scientific approval, then select the complete output package by Customer sample, version, and file count. Review its file names and manifest checksum. POMS uses the service workflow for the release definition and records the reviewer and approval time. Enter an optional Customer-visible QC summary using ordinary text. Approval pins that immutable package; it does not upload or alter artifacts. If several sample packages are ready, approve each package separately. Previously approved packages remain pinned while later packages undergo their own review. When no complete, checksummed, malware-clean package is available, the approval action remains blocked. The reviewer must be different from every actor who recorded receipt, accessioning, execution, QC, library, batch, or sendout work in scope. A protocol author cannot approve or activate that protocol version. If either actor-separation or scientific gates fail, leave the work in review and create the appropriate exception or rework action.

sections.heading: Publish readiness
sections.text: Approval moves the Lab work order to Ready for release and publishes the controlled Customer-safe milestone to Commercial. Commercial may receive the milestone, schedule health, expected timing, and safe QC projection defined by the contract.

sections.heading: Respect the release boundary
sections.text: Ready for release automatically creates the Commercial release candidate for the approved package. It does not publish the result. A Result Release Manager still controls Customer visibility, and payment/credit facts never gate PSeq release. If the Lab-to-Commercial event fails, retry the existing durable projection. Do not duplicate the approval, recreate the work order, or manually mark the Customer file released.

sections.heading: Review the Customer release
sections.text: A Result Release Manager opens Order operations > Result release, chooses the recognizable job and sample, and reviews the package detail before confirming publication. The detail joins scientific approval, file evidence, and release state. File administrators also see the retention receipt and preservation controls there; those permissions do not grant release authority.

guides.title: PSeq billing, cash, and result release
guides.summary: Review PSeq invoices, record and reconcile cash, release scientifically approved results, and distinguish disabled capabilities from loading failures.
taskKeywords: PSeq billing, cash, and result release

sections.heading: PSeq billing, cash, and result release
sections.text: POMS owns operational accounts receivable for PSeq Lab Service. Result release is scientifically governed and never gated by payment balance or credit. Partner PSeq Kit and Partner data-assembly payment/release rules remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Find the Finance record
sections.text: Finance actions depend on your assigned responsibility: Billing Operators maintain billing and invoice adjustments, Cash Operators record and allocate receipts and submit reconciliations, and Cash Reconcilers independently approve reconciliations. Result Release Manager and file-administration authority remain separate. Open Order Ops → Finance. Choose Invoices and aging, Receipts, Customer billing, Import receipts, or Reconciliation. Open a record by its invoice, receipt, Customer or reconciliation number. The detail shows its current state and permitted actions. On an invoice, Open order is available only with commercial order administration access; Billing Operators can still review and adjust the invoice within their assigned permissions. Return to Finance to keep the previous Customer filter and section. Use Search customers in the list header to filter by any part of a Customer name; matching ignores capitalization. Clear filter restores the full list. The search is retained when switching tabs or returning from a record. It narrows the displayed records; aging summarizes all Customers, and Export all invoices and Export all receipts include all Customers. If a section or its supporting Customer or aging information cannot load, use its Retry action. Other available Finance sections remain usable. A new receipt or import needs the Customer choices to load; a new reconciliation also needs its eligible receipts.
