An open adjustment, allocation, or reversal keeps the invoice and receipt information you reviewed. If another change prevents saving, the dialog automatically loads the current record and preserves your entries. Review the updated status and balances, then choose Use reviewed record, check your entries and save again. If that refresh fails, use Retry current record. An unavailable invoice must be reselected, and a receipt with no available amount cannot be allocated. When Attention queues are enabled, an overdue invoice, unapplied receipt or reconciliation difference includes Open invoice, Open receipt or Open reconciliation when your Finance responsibility permits that record. Open the record to review the facts and take the appropriate action. Following a link does not allocate cash or resolve the attention item.

sections.heading: Configure and issue PSeq documents
sections.text: Record billing contact/address and Net 30 terms by default. Record Taxable, Exempt, or NonTaxable, including the approved rate or exemption evidence. Finance approval is required before the tax determination can be used. If the profile is complete and approved at quote issuance, POMS includes calculated tax and freezes billing, tax, terms, currency, and configuration version in the quote. Zero calculated tax is valid. If the profile is not ready, issue an explicitly pre-tax quote. Complete and approve the profile before invoicing; POMS then calculates tax and freezes the current billing terms in the invoice. Job completion idempotently creates one numbered invoice and immutable PDF. Due date is completion plus the applicable snapshotted terms. Saving billing changes clears approval. After Finance approves the current profile, the approval badge and date confirm its saved state; the reminder to approve is removed. A Commercial Operator can open an In progress or Results available Job in Order Operations and choose Complete Job. Review the sample outcomes and billing details, then choose Confirm completion. An empty roster or any sample without a final Completed, Failed, Rejected, or Cancelled outcome blocks confirmation. POMS also checks current Lab outcomes and unresolved holds when you confirm. Successful processing becomes final after the applicable scientific approval. Failed processing remains billable at the accepted price; any credit or replacement requires a separate reviewed decision. If the Job changed, choose Reload Job, review its current outcomes and reopen completion. If the connection fails before completion is confirmed, retry the same open Job to recover the existing operation. POMS calculates the approved tax rate without a tax engine. Never edit an issued invoice; use an append-only credit, debit, or write-off adjustment.

sections.heading: Release PSeq results
sections.text: If Result release not enabled appears, this capability is not available in the current installation. Other available work areas remain usable. This message is different from a loading failure and does not mean there are no result packages. Attention queues not enabled has the same meaning for Attention; the dashboard omits its retry and queue shortcut while disabled. Workspace navigation remains available to explain the status. Neither message offers an activation action. Open Order Ops → Result release. The queue starts with Ready for release packages; use Package state to view another state. A link with a selected state preserves that filter. Open the package identified by its Customer, Job and sample. The detail connects scientific review, manifest, release, retention and receipt. A Customer result may be published only when the specific sample package is complete, checksummed, malware-clean, and scientifically approved. The Result Release Manager releases or withdraws a version. Other samples may remain in progress. Do not consult invoice balance or credit status for this decision. Corrections create a new package, scientific approval, and release version. Preserve notification, Customer download, retention warning/cutoff/grace/deletion, withdrawal, and authorized reissue evidence. Related-workspace links follow your access: View commercial order is available to platform administrators, while View scientific review requires laboratory access. The package still shows its Customer, Job, sample and approval context when a related workspace is unavailable to you.

sections.heading: Review governed result retention
sections.text: New PSeq releases use the effective versioned policy from File retention, including an active Organization override. The package and laboratory release share the same first release instant and freeze their policy and deadlines together. Existing schedules keep their original dates; do not change them by editing current configuration. The Customer package shows full-response download completion and the frozen standard/final dates. Grace remains usable when any artifact was undownloaded at the standard deadline; later completion does not shorten grace. New download requests close at the applicable deadline even if cleanup has not run. A request-only historical download event is not completion evidence. Success saved after the standard deadline cannot cancel grace. If download timing cannot be verified, ask technical support to recover the retained timing evidence; do not recreate the release or change its dates. This timing-recovery error is separate from the Retention notices queue. Where governed retention processing is enabled, POMS queues one warning for an incomplete package and one grace notice if grace applies. A delayed warning is skipped once all files have completed or the standard deadline has passed. Queued notices use current active Organization admins; they contain the package reference, deadline, and an authenticated Portal link. Use Owned attention queues → Retention notices to find urgent missing-recipient or delivery failures. Review the organization and administrator access, correct delivery configuration when needed, then retry the existing record in the notification workspace. Recreating a release or notification is not a recovery step. A failure can reopen the Operations item until the underlying notice is recovered. Deadlines remain unchanged. Physical cleanup remains separately controlled. A closed download window is not proof of byte deletion, and a queued message is not proof of receipt. Access withdrawal or deactivation stops a governed transfer; restoring access does not resume that transfer.

sections.heading: Record and reconcile cash
sections.text: In Receipts, choose Record receipt. Enter Customer, payer, amount, received date, payment method, bank reference and external reference. Attach evidence as PDF, PNG, JPEG or text, up to 10 MB. The file must pass the configured scanner before the receipt is recorded; an unavailable scanner leaves the receipt unsaved and preserves your entries. An optional note adds context. Open a saved receipt to download its evidence, allocate it to a same-Customer invoice, or reverse it when no allocation remains. Evidence downloads use the receipt number and retain the file extension. Imported receipts download their saved import evidence as JSON. In Import receipts, select Customer and source, then choose a CSV file or paste its contents. Required headers are source, external_id, date, amount, currency, payer, reference and memo. Preview import validates the file. Review the frozen Customer, source, rows and total, then confirm. Only the operator who reviewed that preview can confirm it. If another operator already owns the file review, ask them to complete it; do not change the file identity to bypass that ownership. If the Customer, totals, or saved version changed, review a fresh preview before confirmation. Change input returns to editing and requires a fresh preview. An earlier response cannot replace a preview for changed input. Repeating your unconfirmed preview resumes the same batch; confirmed files cannot be imported twice. Imports create unapplied receipts and retain their source evidence. Matching suggestions never apply cash. Allocate explicitly so partial, one-receipt/many-invoice, many-receipt/one-invoice, overpayment, and unapplied cash remain visible. Reversals retain actor and reason. A Cash Operator submits a balanced reconciliation; a different Cash Reconciler who contributed none of its activity approves the immutable closeout report. In Allocate to invoice, search by invoice number and use Next invoices or Previous invoices to find more open invoices for the same Customer. The selected invoice and its reviewed balance remain visible while you browse other results. Selecting or searching never records an allocation. The receipt's Allocation history shows each allocation, its invoice, amount, actor and any reversal. Use Reverse allocation on an active allocation, review its receipt and invoice, and enter the correction reason. Reversal restores the receipt's unapplied amount and the invoice's outstanding balance while preserving the original allocation. A fully reversed allocation cannot be reversed again. Reverse receipt remains available only when no allocation remains. In Reconciliation, open the batch number to review its selected receipts and other contributing records. Before submission, a Cash Operator may choose Edit draft to correct the period end, bank total or selected receipts, or Cancel draft to retain an unused batch as cancelled. Both actions require a reason and the current version. Editing recalculates totals and retains the before-and-after selections. Draft change history shows the actor, reason and changes to the period and totals. Balancing or cancelling the draft resolves its open reconciliation-difference attention item. Cancellation does not reverse receipts or allocations. Submit the batch only when balanced. Submitted and approved batches cannot be edited or cancelled through these draft actions. Independent approval excludes the creator, submitter, contributing actors and every recorded draft editor wherever dual control is enforced. A conflict preserves your entries: review the refreshed batch before applying them. The immutable closeout remains the evidence for the approved batch. After approval, Closeout report shows the saved bank and ledger totals, difference, period, included-record count and approval time. Expand Approval reference to inspect the reviewer reference and exact UTC timestamp. Download closeout report saves a readable text copy of that approval evidence, including recorded draft changes and their references. It does not change the approved reconciliation. If the saved report is unavailable or does not match the record, reload and contact support if the problem continues; a report cannot be downloaded until valid saved evidence is available.

sections.heading: Apply Partner assembly release gates
sections.text: An approved output release must reference the accepted input revision and active assembly profile. Its accounting source record is created at output approval. A Partner with approved assembly credit may receive the output under its terms; otherwise the files remain on payment hold until a separately approved payment-confirmation workflow exists.

sections.heading: Diagnose a blocked release
sections.text: Review package completeness, checksum/scan state, scientific approval, release decision, notification, and retention independently from invoice/receipt/allocation/reconciliation. Never bypass a failed package gate by attaching a file manually or changing an unrelated workflow status. Use the owned attention queues for overdue invoices, unapplied cash, and reconciliation differences.

sections.heading: Support general Lab and Assembly downloads
sections.text: Where general retention enforcement is enabled, individual files and whole ZIPs use the release's frozen policy and verified completion. A closed window prevents new requests, while an admitted transfer can finish within its time limit. Current file withdrawal, scan failure, Organization/Department access removal, or release withdrawal stops active downloads. A failed ZIP does not count its files from that attempt. Partner payment-release rules still apply. Recover missing timing evidence through technical support without recreating the release or changing dates. General download enforcement does not itself schedule warning/grace emails or activate storage cleanup. Preserve the original contract for undated historical releases. Where general Lab/Assembly retention processing is enabled, the same warning, grace, and Retention notices recovery workflow applies to those releases. The Lab notice opens the laboratory job; the Assembly notice opens its assembly request. Recipients are current active Organization admins, including admins appointed after the notice was queued. Department-only members and notification routing aliases are not recipients. Retry the existing failed notification after correcting the cause, then review the Operations item. Preserve the original release and dates. General and governed PSeq notice processing are activated separately; a disabled process does not create or dispatch its scheduled notices. Released package schedules link to retained receipts. Receipts preserve file manifests, checksums, deadline/completion/deletion facts and reissue lineage after byte deletion. For preservation, quarantine, or linking a newly approved reissue, use Configuration and recovery.

guides.title: Customer lab authorization
guides.summary: Start a Customer Job for its Department, resolve readiness by stage, issue pricing, and authorize Lab work after sample finalization.

sections.heading: Lab Service authorization
sections.text: Customer and Partner Lab Service work shares the Department-scoped Job, specimen, shipping and scientific-release workflow. Manual Customer work enters Order Ops as a Commercial request. Order Ops validates the Job-level specimen count, biological-source composition, storage, safety, and service profile before pricing. Individual samples do not exist yet.

sections.heading: Additional scope on an accepted Job
sections.text: For an active accepted Job, an authorized Commercial Operator can select Issue Change quote. Enter only additional biological-source counts and the price per additional sample. The saved quote is an immutable incremental proposal; it does not replace the original placement or authorize new work. Existing readiness and independent pricing controls remain enforced. A new proposal supersedes the previous unaccepted Change quote. The Customer or Partner organization administrator or an administrator of the assigned Department accepts or declines separately. Accepted additions open sample entry without unlocking existing authorized samples. Finalization appends a versioned authorization and creates shipping records only for new samples. Started work must preserve all existing specimens and its pinned scientific configuration; unsafe changes require laboratory review. Final billing combines accepted original and additional charges, retaining each quote's tax decision. Completed or cancelled Jobs cannot receive new additions.

sections.heading: Configured standard orders
sections.text: An eligible Customer or Partner organization administrator or an administrator of the assigned Department may select a configured offering and place its standard Lab Service bundle directly from the Job. The review includes the specimen count, frozen scientific scope, unit price, approved tax and final total. Complete billing and Finance-approved tax are required for this direct commitment; manual quote readiness remains as described below. Order Ops displays the accepted Standard PSeq Lab Service terms. Do not issue a second quote or sell assembly separately for the same bundle. The accepted Job opens exact sample-list preparation; roster finalization creates the normal Lab and shipping authorization. Partner Lab work stays within the Partner's organization and Department. Custom-work requests create a Sales Opportunity and preserve the originating order and Department. They do not place an order or approve a price. Review their scope in CRM and follow the existing Sales handoff when ready.

sections.heading: Initiate an order for a Customer
sections.text: An authorized Phaeno order-pricing user can begin the pricing profile when the Customer is already known and does not need to create the request first. Open Order operations, select Order intake, and choose New Order. Search by Company name and select the active Customer, then choose the Department that owns the Job. Customers remain visible even when setup is incomplete. Review Before starting pricing, Before issuing a quote, and Before invoicing for that Department. Starting pricing requires the active Customer, an effective Ready PSeq Lab Service entitlement, the active specimen offering, and no operational block. It does not require an online administrator yet. Setup links open in a separate tab so your order details remain here. Ask a platform administrator to complete setup if your role cannot change it, then return to the same order draft and select Refresh readiness. Enter a unique Job name, every biological source and sample count, the total Sample-sequencing runs (leave blank for one per sample), the shared storage requirements and safety declaration, and any Customer-safe Job notes. If Sales discussed a price, select Propose a price, enter the proposed USD price per sample-sequencing run, and optionally add Customer-safe pricing context. A proposal is not a quote and does not authorize work. Do not enter individual sample IDs, tube barcodes, patient identifiers, or PHI. Confirm that the pricing details contain no patient identifiers, PHI, or unnecessary personal data, then select Start pricing. POMS creates the Customer-owned Job with one immutable submitted request revision and opens it in Quote in preparation. Review the committed sample count, source composition, storage, and safety facts on the operational detail. If a price was proposed, select Review proposed price and compare the proposal, active catalog price, difference, and calculated subtotal. Approve it unchanged or amend the unit price; an amendment requires an internal reason. Before issuing the quote, complete every non-billing readiness blocker, including activating a Customer administrator who can receive and approve it. Billing readiness may be completed after acceptance but is required before invoicing. The editor preselects the required PSeq Lab Service, explains that it is priced per sample-sequencing run, and sets its read-only quantity from the Job's requested sample-sequencing run count. The required line cannot be removed. Additional active catalog lines may be added with a per-unit price and a quantity chosen for that quote. Permanent accounting codes remain available in Order settings but are not shown as quote-entry guidance. If the designated item is missing, inactive, or not priced per sample-sequencing run, quote issuance is paused until Order settings is corrected. POMS validates the item identity, unit, and committed quantity again on the server. POMS sends no Customer notice while a Phaeno-initiated Job remains Quote in preparation. Issuing or revising the quote rechecks ordering eligibility and the approver list, makes the quote available immediately, moves the Job to Quote issued, and notifies every active Customer administrator. The Customer can approve it; Phaeno cannot approve on the Customer's behalf. The accepting administrator becomes the Job's acting Customer contact for ordinary later notices. High-impact events, including cancellation by Phaeno and result release, continue to notify all active Customer administrators.

sections.heading: Review the request
sections.text: Open the Job header's Actions menu for Assignment, Request changes, and Decline request when your permissions and the Job status allow them. Open Lab work and Complete Job appear there when available. If only one header action is available, it appears as a labeled button. Selecting an action keeps its existing review or confirmation step. Confirm that the Customer has an active laboratory-service entitlement and that the selected service is currently offered. Review the requested specimen count, each source group and count, shared handling and safety declarations, and Customer notes. Request a targeted correction when information is incomplete or unsafe rather than rewriting Customer data internally. Keep internal review notes separate from the reason shown to the Customer. The initial workflow is not a PHI intake path; do not ask for or store patient-identifying information.

sections.heading: Issue and accept the quote
sections.text: The Customer or Sales price proposal is part of the submitted request revision, not a quote. POMS preserves its unit price, note, proposer, and time. The issued quote records whether Phaeno approved that proposal or amended it, along with the responsible Commercial reviewer and decision time. When dual control is enabled, a Phaeno proposer cannot review the same proposal. The quote is a versioned, immutable Commercial offer for one job. Confirm the configured service, quantities, prices, currency, expected turnaround information, and expiration before issuance. Tax is calculated by POMS: when the complete billing and tax profile is Finance-approved, the quote includes and freezes tax; otherwise the quote is explicitly pre-tax and tax is calculated from the approved profile at invoicing. Saving the issued POMS quote makes it available for Customer acceptance. Cancel, Close, or Escape asks you to keep editing or discard unsaved quote changes. Dismissal is unavailable while the quote is being issued or its current record is being refreshed. A stale-record response preserves your entries; review the refreshed Job and pricing before deliberately submitting again. Customer acceptance performs one Commercial operation that: records the accepted quote revision and frozen pricing profile; and opens post-acceptance sample-list preparation. After the Customer enters or imports the exact compliant sample list, finalization atomically creates the immutable laboratory work authorization, linked Lab work order, shipment, and physical tube slots. Do not create a Lab work order manually if finalization fails. Resolve the reported roster or shipping-configuration issue and retry the durable operation. Physical samples must not arrive before quote acceptance and exact roster finalization create the authorized shipment. Quarantine and escalate an unexpected package under the approved receiving and custody exception. Do not accession, process, bill, or attach it to executable Job work.

sections.heading: Respect the Lab boundary
sections.text: After acceptance, Order Ops continues to own Customer communication, Commercial holds, cancellation review, billing, files, and publication. Open the linked work from the order or from Lab operations > Receipt & accession. Lab Ops owns return-kit preparation, shipment identification, receipt, accession, physical lineage, controlled execution, exceptions, and scientific approval. The Lab milestone Ready for release means the scientific gate passed. It does not upload, scan, attach, or publish a result. PSeq result publication still requires the governed file and release checks. PSeq scientific result release is independent of invoice balance, credit status, and payment; Partner workflows retain their separate commercial rules.

sections.heading: Track and change expected completion
sections.text: Turnaround and progress shows first receipt, scientific acceptance, the original target, current expected completion, actual completion and receipt-to-acceptance elapsed time. Published turnaround begins at scientific acceptance. The original target is never overwritten by an operational delay. An authorized Lab operator, supervisor or Operations administrator uses Change expected completion from the order. Choose the new date and a controlled reason. Other operational delay also requires a customer-safe explanation. Keep internal investigation notes in Internal note. A later date queues a notice; an earlier date updates the Portal. The history distinguishes the timing change from notification delivery. Failed notices remain available to authorized notification recovery.

sections.heading: Delivery due date and job tracking
sections.text: Use Lab operations → Jobs to track delivery deadlines independently of the processing forecast. An authorized operator or supervisor can adjust an unfinished job’s due date with a customer-safe reason. The original delivery target and adjustment history remain; Commercial jobs receive a notice of the changed due date. Turnaround and progress also shows the delivery due date and original delivery target. Laboratory completion remains distinct from full Portal delivery: every in-scope sample needs published results, and the customer does not have to download them.

sections.heading: Sample-sequencing runs
sections.text: Unique samples, submitted tubes and purchased runs are separate quantities. One sample with 20 runs has the same run quantity as 20 samples with one run each. Configured pricing, proposed subtotals, required quote lines and accepted snapshots use the run quantity. Sample-source counts continue to count unique samples. After acceptance, each sample receives a positive run allocation; finalization requires the allocated total to match the purchased total. A Change quote for additional samples can include an explicit additional run quantity, which is allocated to the new samples after acceptance. Previously authorized samples retain their original allocations.

guides.title: Data assembly
guides.summary: Coordinate commercial quotes and decisions with Lab-owned input validation, processing, QC, and output approval.

sections.heading: Partner data assembly
sections.text: New Partner Assembly is included with a purchased PSeq Kit case. Order Ops owns the original Kit purchase and case administration. Historical standalone Assembly keeps its original Commercial quote, cancellation and accounting source record. Lab Ops owns input validation, processing milestones, quality review, and immutable output release. Inputs and outputs are manufacturing records; they are not source samples for Data Provisioning. Find the Commercial order in Order operations > Assembly. Open Lab operations > Data assembly > Assembly cases to validate the submitted input and perform the manufacturing workflow. For included cases, accepted intake proceeds to the processing queue without another quote or purchase. Historical standalone requests retain their quote and Partner-acceptance steps.

sections.heading: Validate the submission
sections.text: Confirm the active Partner, project reference, purchase-order requirement, included frozen assembly profile, or the historical request profile, required metadata, and uploaded input revision. Validate file type, size, completeness, malware-scan state, and every profile-specific requirement. When the submission cannot pass input validation, Lab staff place the manufacturing record on hold and document the issue. Commercial staff use the linked order to request a targeted Partner correction or reject work that is unsafe, unsupported, or outside the offered profile. A correction creates a new input revision; it must not rewrite the revision that was reviewed previously.

sections.heading: Historical standalone quotes
sections.text: Prepare the per-job quote from the current assembly offering and preserve its profile, price, currency, and expiration snapshot. Issuing the POMS quote makes it available to the Partner immediately. Acceptance records the immutable Commercial commitment and queues the work.

sections.heading: Process and review
sections.text: Record processing milestones against the accepted input revision and selected profile. Internal implementation details and intermediate files remain internal. When processing is complete, perform the configured quality review and document any hold or required correction. Open Review outputs to inspect every uploaded output and its scan state, including files uploaded in an earlier session. POMS builds the output manifest from the uploaded files and pinned processing run; operators do not type a manifest or repeat the pipeline provenance.

sections.heading: Approve an output release
sections.text: An output release is immutable and identifies: the exact source input revision; the assembly profile and version; the output manifest and included files; checksums, scan state, and generation time; and the quality-review and approval facts. Approve a new release rather than replacing a prior release. Included outputs use the original Kit shipment commercial source; they create no second invoice, commercial source or sale. Historical standalone output approval retains its original accounting-source step. Both apply the appropriate recorded balance or Partner assembly-credit gate. Credit-approved work can be released under Net 30; work without approved credit remains on payment hold because manual payment confirmation is not yet implemented.

guides.title: Holds, cancellations, and adjustments
guides.summary: Pause work safely, decide cancellation requests, preserve completed work, and account for adjustments.

sections.heading: Holds, cancellations, and adjustments
sections.text: Holds and cancellation decisions preserve work already performed. They do not erase shipments, Lab execution, input revisions, output releases, Commercial documents, or audit history.

sections.heading: Place and release holds
sections.text: Phaeno may place an active workflow on hold for an operational, Commercial, validation, shipping, or Customer-action reason. Record a concise tenant-safe explanation and separate internal notes. A hold pauses the affected next action; it does not silently change quote, payment, scientific, or release state. Release a hold only after the blocking condition is resolved. The release is an audited Phaeno action and should reference the corrected fact or approved exception.

sections.heading: Handle cancellation timing
sections.text: A draft or other unaccepted commitment may be withdrawn under its workflow rules. After quote acceptance or reagent-order acceptance, cancellation becomes a request for Phaeno review. Decide the request as approved, partially approved, or declined based on work performed, material committed, quantities shipped, and outputs already released. For Customer laboratory work with a finalized sample roster, open the cancellation request, choose Partially approve, and select the specific samples awaiting receipt. Record a reason for the Customer and choose Save decision. POMS checks the latest Lab and shipment records before saving. Received work cannot be selected for this action. Dispatched shipments or containers mixing selected and unaffected samples require shipping review and separation first. If records change while you review, reopen the current Job and review the selection again. The selected samples and their eligible unshipped shipments become Cancelled. Remaining work resumes its previous Job state. The accepted quote stays unchanged, and any credit is a separate Finance decision. Unsaved selections and reasons are protected when closing the dialog.

sections.heading: Preserve unaffected work
sections.text: A partial cancellation can retain completed samples, shipped reagent quantities, or accepted assembly work while removing only the approved remainder. Preserve prior revisions, manifests, packing slips, releases, and Customer-visible history.

sections.heading: Record Commercial adjustments
sections.text: Record the portal cancellation decision without editing the original Commercial snapshot. For PSeq Customer Jobs, Finance records the applicable credit, debit, or write-off in Order operations → Finance; issued invoices and accepted quotes retain their original snapshots. Partner workflows retain their manual accounting handoff using the stable commercial source references. Reconcile the correction in the workflow that owns the original document.

guides.title: Integration failures and recovery
guides.summary: Recover original invitations and notices, inspect failed projections, and recognize unavailable historical connectors.

sections.heading: Accounting and notification recovery
sections.text: A failed notice or integration remains attached to the original business record with its attempts and error history. Use Company People for invitation access and delivery recovery, Attention for operational follow-up, and the owning Lab, Trial, or release record for scientific publication. Native PSeq accounts receivable is maintained in Finance; retained accounting connectors serve historical or non-PSeq work.

sections.heading: Triage the failure
sections.text: Open Attention for the owned cross-workflow exception or Legacy integrations for a retained connector/notification event. Identify the affected record, current delivery state, owner, age, attempts, next action, and tenant-visible consequence. Determine whether the local operation committed successfully before taking recovery action. Common states include: Invitation queued/failed/bounced/needs attention while access remains separately pending, accepted, expired, or revoked; Projection or scan failed while the immutable result package remains unreleased; failed notification delivery after the underlying portal action already succeeded.

sections.heading: Retry safely
sections.text: For a configured Lab order or Kit bundle, a platform administrator can open Order Ops → Attention → CRM sale summaries. Follow the order link, correct the reported commercial setup problem, then choose Retry publication. The original order stays committed while the same summary is queued again. Publication updates first-party CRM; it does not create another purchase or transmit specimen details, internal Lab notes or batch membership. Refresh the workflow before investigating a missing accounting row. Do not recreate the order, quote, shipment, output approval, or result completion to force another row. Use the stable source ID when reconciling repeated report downloads. If an invitation hard-bounced, revoke and reissue to a corrected address rather than retrying it. If a result or delivery already exists, inspect that original record instead of creating another package or delivery. If a notification failed, retry it without repeating the underlying business transition. If QuickBooks is not configured, catalog, document, or payment recovery reports the connector as unavailable and records Needs attention. It does not create an invoice, payment, or successful zero balance. Preserve the existing record and ask the responsible administrator to resolve the connector; repeating the request cannot configure it. Maintain the active Service catalog directly in Order settings → Service catalog. Partner Assembly credit settings remain applicable to their own workflow.

sections.heading: Communicate the boundary
sections.text: Keep operational state, accounting-source readiness, credit, file release, and notification delivery separate. An accounting question does not undo an issued quote or scientific completion. A failed email does not reverse the order action recorded in the portal. Escalate only after the operational record, report range, stable entry ID, and notification history have been reviewed. Include safe identifiers; never include credentials, payment data, or customer-confidential scientific detail in support notes.

guides.title: Order operations
guides.summary: Find the Order operations workspace available to your role, manage commercial decisions, and continue Lab, Finance, and release work in their owning screens.

sections.heading: Order operations
sections.text: Order operations is the Commercial workspace for Customer and Partner laboratory orders, Partner PSeq Kit orders, and Partner data assembly requests. Use it for each order's pricing, commercial decisions, follow-up, Finance, and result publication. Reusable defaults and scientific offerings are maintained in Order settings. On the dashboard, staff without commercial administration access see links to their assigned Order operations workspaces, such as Finance or Result release. Commercial administrators see the active intake summary. When starting a Customer Job, select its Company and Department. A single available Department is selected automatically. The Department owns the Job and determines Customer access and the applicable service rule; a Blocked Department rule cannot be bypassed by a Ready organization default. Use the far-left sidebar beneath the toolbar to move among Order intake, Trial projects, PSeq kits, Assembly, Attention, Result release, Finance, and Legacy integrations, subject to your explicit roles. Order intake owns staff-assisted Customer order creation, Sales handoffs, commercial review, pricing and manual quotes. Eligible organizations can place a configured standard Lab Service bundle from their own Job; that accepted commitment is shown on the same order. Trial projects handles no-charge evaluations. Choose New Order in the Commercial order intake list header, which also contains the view and search filters. Select the Customer and Department, then review Customer readiness. Active Customers remain selectable even when their setup is incomplete. Requirements under Before starting pricing must be resolved first. Expand Later requirements for additional quote and invoice setup; those items do not block creating the order for pricing. Retry a failed readiness check without discarding your entries. Enter the Job name, sample counts by biological source, shared storage requirements, and safety declaration. You may also record a proposed price and optional notes. Start pricing saves the order and opens its detail workspace. An active Customer administrator is required before quote issuance. Exact sample IDs and tube counts are entered after quote acceptance; sample-list finalization authorizes the laboratory and shipping workflow. Billing setup may be completed after acceptance, before invoicing. Order intake owns this per-order process; reusable setup is maintained in Order settings and the Company workspace. The sidebar header identifies Order operations and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the edge tab. Choosing a section closes an unpinned sidebar.

sections.heading: Enter and find orders
sections.text: Order ops opens an available workspace for your responsibilities. Result Release Managers start at Result release when they do not also have commercial administration access; Finance staff start at Finance when they do not also have release or commercial administration access. A saved link to an unavailable section opens your available starting workspace. An explicitly selected available section is preserved. Order intake is available to platform administrators and assigned Commercial Operators. Commercial Operators can open Lab Service orders, select an active Customer and Department, check readiness, start pricing, and manage quotes. When business roles are enforced, platform administration alone does not grant pricing authority. PSeq kits, Assembly, Legacy integrations, and configuration administration retain their separate administrator access. Laboratory review and release/Finance roles alone do not grant Order intake access. Attention keeps two responsibilities distinct. Assigned commercial, release or Finance roles can use the operational attention queues when enabled. Platform administrators can access CRM sale summaries there even without those business roles. The dashboard shows operational Attention counts and shortcuts only when your assigned role permits that queue; platform administration alone does not grant that permission when business roles are enforced. Order intake covers Customer and Partner commercial requests through review, pricing, quote issuance, and Customer acceptance. Held orders remain in active intake. Use On hold to focus on blockers and All orders and history to find accepted, completed or cancelled work. Laboratory execution continues in Lab Ops. PSeq kits shows commercial status and opens the same order in Lab Ops for review, substitutions, backorders, shipments and fulfillment. Assembly shows commercial context and opens the same request in Lab Ops for processing, quality review and output release. Attention owns invitation, readiness, staged-order, projection/scan, unreleased-result, overdue-invoice, unapplied-cash, and reconciliation-difference exceptions. Result release publishes a scientifically approved, complete PSeq package per sample without a payment gate. Finance owns PSeq invoices, receipts/import, explicit allocation, aging, and reconciliation. Legacy integrations covers retained accounting-connector and notification recovery outside the active native PSeq AR workflow. Search Order intake by order, Job, Company, or request number. Order search runs across all matching records, with 25 orders per page. Pending CRM handoffs appear on the first active-intake page. The view, search and page stay in the address so you can return to the same queue. Clear filters restores active intake. A PSeq Lab Service row identifies an optional proposed price so Commercial users can find pricing decisions without opening every record. On the order, Review proposed price compares the proposed USD price per specimen with the active catalog price, requested quantity, difference, and subtotal. Approve price and issue quote preserves the proposal unchanged; Amend price and issue quote requires an internal reason. Tax is system-calculated: include and freeze it when the billing and tax profile is complete and Finance-approved, or issue an explicitly pre-tax quote and calculate tax at invoicing. The issued quote, not the proposal, is the offer a Customer administrator may accept. The operational detail shows the current quote value, revision, and status. Internal context in the audit timeline explains Phaeno-only decisions; it is informational, not a Customer-facing warning. Assign an owner and due date when the workflow supports them. A queue assignment coordinates work; it does not grant authorization or change the workflow state.

sections.heading: Review quote extension requests
sections.text: An Extension requested marker in active Order intake identifies a Lab Service quote that needs review. Open the Job to read the request and its optional reason. A Phaeno user with Order Operations access and quote-issuance authority can select Review extension to prepare a new quote revision. Reissue quote is also available while an issued manual quote awaits the organization's decision. Reissuing starts with the saved quote's line items and unit prices. Review them, choose a future expiration date, and issue the new revision through the normal commercial review. POMS checks that the source quote and Job are still current. Successful issuance resolves the extension request and supersedes the old quote while preserving its original facts. The organization receives the normal quote-ready notice and must review and accept the new revision separately. A request never changes the old deadline or grants automatic acceptance.

sections.heading: Review configured bundles
sections.text: A standard Lab Service order includes specimen processing and data assembly in one accepted scope. Review its saved offering version, final price and Turnaround and progress on the order. Exact sample entry still follows commitment; roster finalization owns Lab and shipping authorization. A PSeq Kit purchase includes one assembly case per whole kit unit. Its order shows unit shipment facts, frozen profiles, deadlines and case history. Partner input corrections stay with the same case; included Assembly does not create a second quote or sale. Open Lab work leads to the existing execution workspace.

sections.heading: Keep state boundaries visible
sections.text: Operational status, quote status, accounting-source readiness, payment, scientific readiness, file scanning, and publication are separate facts. Do not mark one complete merely because another succeeded. External users receive a limited timeline, so record a reason suitable for the affected Customer or Partner separately from internal notes whenever an action can be seen outside Phaeno. Order Ops ends at the Commercial boundary for a Customer laboratory order: it remains in Order intake while pricing and quote decisions are active. After acceptance and exact sample-roster finalization authorize that work, use Lab Ops for return-kit preparation, shipment-packet and tube comparison, specimen receipt and accession, protocol execution, materials, equipment, libraries, batches, sequencing sendouts, exceptions, and scientific approval. The PSeq kits and Assembly sections show the commercial record and link to their owning Lab Ops execution screen; the same physical action is recorded once. Lab readiness never publishes a file by itself.

sections.heading: Triage safely
sections.text: Confirm the active organization and workflow before opening a record. Review operational readiness, invitation delivery, scientific package, release, invoice, receipt, allocation, reconciliation, and notification states independently. Check open holds, cancellation requests, overdue actions, and failed deliveries. Assign the work and due date when ownership is unclear. Perform the smallest valid next action and preserve the existing record. POMS checks the latest Job immediately before issuing a quote. If the record changes after that check, POMS reloads it and preserves the entered quote lines; review those values, then issue the quote again. Never repair a failed workflow by creating a duplicate order, quote, invoice, receipt, result package, Lab work order, shipment, or release. Assign an attention item, preserve attempts, and record its resolution.

sections.heading: Review queued notifications
sections.text: Order notices check the current active organization, department, user, and administrator assignments when dispatched. The department notification address is included when configured; otherwise the organization notification default applies. An inactive or mismatched department cannot use either route. Review failed notices with no eligible recipients before retrying them; changing an assignment after a notice was queued changes who can receive it.

sections.heading: Use Finance
sections.text: Choose Invoices and aging, Receipts, Customer billing, Import receipts, or Reconciliation. A Customer filter carries into the record and back. Open the invoice, receipt, Customer, or batch number to review its details, then choose the relevant action. Editing happens in a dialog and errors retain the entered values. Invoice adjustments and receipt reversals retain a required reason. The dashboard summarizes recorded commercial and laboratory work and links to the owning screens. If data is unavailable, refresh or use the workspace directly; an unavailable count is not zero work.

guides.title: PSeq kit fulfillment
guides.summary: Review Partner kit orders commercially, then open Lab work for substitutions, backorders, and shipment fulfillment.

sections.heading: Partner PSeq Kit fulfillment
sections.text: Partner reagent orders use the offering and negotiated price available to the active Partner at placement. The placed order preserves an immutable Commercial snapshot even if catalog or pricing configuration changes later. Find the Commercial order in Order operations > PSeq kits. Perform the Commercial review and order acceptance there. After acceptance, perform physical preparation, substitutions, shipping, and fulfillment in Lab operations > PSeq kits. The Lab workflow consumes the Commercial snapshot; it does not rewrite the ordered items or negotiated price.

sections.heading: Included bundle scope
sections.text: Every new whole Kit unit includes one assembly case. PSeq kits configuration binds the negotiated offering to an active, validated Assembly profile. The draft retains the reviewed offering and profile versions; changed price or scope requires another review before placement. A Partner organization administrator or an administrator of the assigned Department may commit the new Kit purchase.

sections.heading: Review a placed order
sections.text: Confirm the Partner, purchase-order number, shipping address, ordered items, selling units, quantities, negotiated prices, currency, and placement totals. Verify that the shipping destination and requested service satisfy the configured restrictions. In Order operations, move valid work through review and acceptance. Reject it with a Partner-safe reason when the address, eligibility, quantity, or Commercial facts require correction. Keep internal investigation details in the internal record. Lab staff see the order as awaiting Commercial review and cannot start fulfillment until it is accepted.

sections.heading: Handle substitutions and backorders
sections.text: Never substitute a different reagent silently. Record the original item, proposed item, quantity, price effect, and reason. A Partner organization administrator or an administrator of the order's Department must explicitly approve the substitution. If the change increases the total, complete the required Commercial approval and preserve the adjustment for the manual accounting handoff before acceptance. Backorders remain part of the original order. Record the unshipped quantity and expected next action without changing quantities already shipped.

sections.heading: Create shipments
sections.text: Create a partial or complete shipment with: shipped quantities for each original order line; carrier, service, tracking number, and ship date; reagent lot or batch identifier; expiration date when the supplied reagent has one; and the packing-slip facts. Shipped quantities are immutable. Correct future fulfillment with a new shipment or documented adjustment; do not edit shipment history.

sections.heading: Complete fulfillment
sections.text: Reagent fulfillment creates a separate journal-entry source record for each shipment. Partial shipments therefore produce separate source rows tied to the same portal order. Finance completes invoice creation, account selection, tax treatment, and posting outside POMS. The order reaches fulfillment only when the accepted quantities are shipped, backordered quantities are resolved, and no blocking hold remains.

sections.heading: Move between Commercial and Lab work
sections.text: Use the Commercial order to accept or reject the kit order and decide Partner-facing changes or cancellation. Choose Open Lab work to prepare, substitute, ship, and complete the kit. The same order identity and history remain visible on both sides; fulfillment actions appear only in Lab operations.

sections.heading: Manage the included cases
sections.text: The Commercial order's Included assembly cases panel shows each purchased unit, current case, frozen profile, shipment facts, submission deadline and event history. After shipment, the Partner prepares inputs from that exact case. Input corrections preserve the case and request; intake validation and processing continue in the existing Lab Assembly workspace without another quote or sale. Unused cases expire 90 days after labeled kit expiration, or 12 months after shipment if no expiration was recorded. An authorized operator may Extend deadline, Replace kit, or Cancel unused case only when the case permits the action. Review the current case and deadline, and record a reason suitable for the Partner history. Replacement requires actual lot, ship date, carrier and tracking facts; it transfers the existing case to the replacement kit without another purchase, billing source or entitlement. The operational summary keeps fulfillment and assembly progress separate. A shipped Kit may still have pending assembly. Completion requires the included cases to finish or close; an unused expired or cancelled case does not automatically create a refund. Finance history remains separate.

guides.title: Company access and user administration
guides.summary: Manage Company access, staged Department readiness, service entitlements, invitation recovery, and membership lifecycle.

sections.heading: Company access and user administration
sections.text: An organization administrator is optional. A Company can operate through administrators of its active Departments. Department administrators act only within their assigned Departments; ask Phaeno to handle company-wide setup, invitations or roles when no organization administrator is available. Phaeno administrators manage Portal access, readiness, service entitlements, integration requests, and global access from the canonical CRM Company. Prospect, Customer, and Partner administrators manage membership only within their own access scope. Access is invitation-based and every durable administrative change is audited.

sections.heading: Know which administration surface owns each record
sections.text: The CRM Companies directory is the only customer directory. A Company may exist before Portal access is approved. After approval, the same Company workspace displays its relationship type, readiness, services, members, invitations, requests, and retention settings. The internal Organization identifier used for tenant isolation is not a second customer record and does not appear in a separate directory. User management is also connected to durable account APIs. In the Phaeno context, active accounts and invited people appear in one list alongside global account status and every enforced Phaeno role. A Pending invitation status means the invitation has not been accepted and has not activated the offered access; the person may already have a sign-in account. Open a card’s actions menu to edit an active user, deactivate another active user, reactivate a disabled user, or resend or revoke a pending invitation. A Phaeno administrator cannot deactivate their own account. Edit one active user to update their name, Platform administrator assignment, and additive laboratory roles together. Platform administrators retain bootstrap access to every laboratory capability even when no explicit laboratory role is assigned. The role picker contains only roles enforced by the current authorization model: Platform administrator, Lab operator, Lab supervisor, Protocol administrator, Scientific reviewer, and Lab operations administrator. Authentication-provider metadata and unsupported job-title labels do not grant Portal access. Cards marked Pending invitation still represent invitation records, not accepted user records. Enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, then select the Platform administrator and additive laboratory roles they should receive. The pending role intent grants no access. It becomes active only when the recipient accepts and becomes an active Phaeno member.

sections.heading: Review and maintain Companies
sections.text: Create the Company first, then request the approved Portal relationship when access is needed: Prospect for an external organization that may receive explicitly granted curated data or participate in an approved no-charge Trial, but cannot place paid orders. Customer for organizations that request laboratory services. Partner for organizations that submit specimens for PSeq Lab Service or purchase the PSeq Kit, which includes data assembly. Internal employee invitations use the existing Phaeno organization in User management; Company requests create only the approved external relationship. If an invitation shows a Hard bounce, review and revoke it, correct the Contact email, and issue a new invitation from Company People. Resend is unavailable for that bounced invitation. Email delivery status and acceptance are separate: a provider-accepted message does not activate membership. Do not use Company lifecycle or Portal readiness as a shortcut for access. Curated package access requires an exact-version grant, member access requires an accepted invitation, and commercial work requires a current service entitlement. Open CRM and select Companies to search durable external customer records. Select the Company name to open its workspace. Use its Requests tab to propose online access, a product or service change, a relationship change, or reviewed work. Use CRM's central Requests section for requests that still need a Phaeno decision. The Company tab preserves request history but does not duplicate the decision controls. There is no standalone customer-creation action outside CRM. For a pending onboarding or evaluation request, select Approve and enable Portal access and record the approval reason. POMS atomically approves the request, creates the Company's internal tenant scope with Pending readiness, and attaches it to the existing Company. Online-access approval never adds or removes a product or service entitlement, creates another customer record, or creates a user. If an older approved onboarding or evaluation request shows Portal access incomplete, select Complete Portal access. POMS creates and attaches the missing tenant scope without changing product or service entitlements. This recovery does not create another Company, invite users, create an order, or complete the request. If POMS finds an active, compatible access scope with the exact Company name that is not linked to another Company, it pauses and shows Existing access scope found. Review the displayed name and relationship, then select Use existing access scope to reconnect it. Reuse preserves existing users, orders, invitations, and history. Existing Company requests are attached to the scope so they can be fulfilled through their separate owning workflows; attaching them does not grant product or service access. POMS will not offer this shortcut when the scope is inactive, belongs to another Company, or has a different relationship kind; resolve those cases before approving access. For a Customer, open Services → Overview and choose the Department in Department readiness. The same derived checks used by Order Intake separate requirements before pricing, quote issuance, and invoicing. Follow each setup link to its owning screen. Historical readiness notes are retained as context; no manually selected Ready label authorizes work. When inviting an external Company contact, review the selected access. For a Member invitation, select at least one Department. If you clear all Departments and select Send invitation, the form returns focus to Department access and explains what to select. Your entries are retained and no invitation is sent until the required information is valid.

sections.heading: Review Company requests
sections.text: In Completed / history, use Search completed requests to find a Company, request number, summary, decision, or completed-work note. Search ignores capitalization and covers the full history. Previous and Next move through 25 requests per page, newest updated first. A new search starts at page 1; the search and page remain in the address when returning to the queue. Clear filter restores the full history. The active decision and work tabs remain unpaginated. Use CRM's central Requests section to decide pending onboarding, evaluation, product and service, relationship, sales-assisted order, and offboarding requests created by the first-party CRM. Use Needs decision, Approved / needs work, and Completed / history to follow a request through completion. Approved requests stay actionable until completed or cancelled, and the Company's Requests tab links to the same queue. Historical imported requests remain readable alongside requests created in CRM; use the current queue to review their recorded state and available actions. Approve or decline a pending request with a reason. For onboarding or evaluation, approval also creates and attaches the Company's pending-readiness access scope while leaving product and service entitlements unchanged. Other request types record the decision only. Complete each approved invitation, entitlement, or order change through its owning workflow, verify the outcome, and then select Complete request in the central Requests queue and record what was completed. Never put specimen, scientific, downstream-customer, credential, or other sensitive operational details in an external reference or request summary.

sections.heading: Invite administrators and members
sections.text: First-time recipients use the invitation email to set up their account, create the required password, and complete any required multi-factor authentication. Existing users sign in with the invited address. After account setup, recipients return to their saved invitation for review. Access begins only after Accept invitation. If setup is interrupted, reopen the same valid invitation; if an account-setup error offers Restart account setup, use it to try again. A replacement invitation is needed only when the original link is no longer valid. When creating their password, recipients enter it once and can use Show password or Hide password to check their entry. After accepting, recipients see a welcome message naming their organization and select Open Portal to continue. The Company People view shows their Portal access as active. From Company detail, open People. Use New person to create and associate a Contact in one save, or Add existing person to associate an existing Contact. Select Invite to Portal and choose Organization administrator or explicit Department membership and Department-admin roles. The Contact identity is filled in; edit the Contact first if its email or name is incorrect. Assign organization-wide administrator access only when the person must govern every Department; otherwise use Department membership and grant Department administrator access only where needed. A CRM Contact remains separate from a Portal user and grants no access until the invitation is accepted. The invitation page shows the invited name, organization, and email before sign-in. The recipient selects Continue with their email, completes verification for that fixed address without entering or editing the email, and then selects Accept invitation. If another account is signed in, Switch account preserves the invitation while they sign in with the invited address. Viewing the invitation grants no access. The recipient sees Access after acceptance before confirming. If that access changed after their review, the page refreshes it and requires them to review and select Accept invitation again. Open the person's Actions menu. For active members, Manage access changes their Organization role or Department access, or deactivates membership. These changes take effect immediately and queue an informational email to the affected person; there is no new invitation to accept. For an unaccepted invitation, choose Edit invited access, Resend invite, or Revoke invite. Each opens a focused dialog for that action. Edit relationship remains separate from Portal permissions. Expired invitations display Invitation expired; People refreshes the state while it stays open. Use Edit relationship to change their Company-specific title, commercial role, or effective dates. Use Departments to create or rename operational units, choose the default, and record typed configuration overrides. Every Organization begins with General. Organization administrators can edit the five Organization defaults for PO, billing and notification email, shipping, and result instructions. A blank Department override inherits the Organization default, then the commercial profile or system rule. The system PO rule is not required; either level can explicitly require or waive it. Existing saved shipping and accepted-quote snapshots retain their values. Result-delivery instructions are retained with the commercial commitment, not an automatic change to storage destinations. Organization administrators can access every active Department; other users must retain at least one active Department assignment. When one business unit must not be discoverable or governed by another—or it has separate contracting, tax, legal, ownership, or retention obligations—create a separate Company/Organization instead of a Department. When adding a department, enter its name and optional settings. The system assigns a reference such as DEPT-000123 when you save; you do not enter a Code. References are unique within the organization and stay the same when a department is renamed or deactivated. The department name remains its main label. Existing references, including GENERAL, are retained and shown as read-only context when editing. External Organization and Department administrators can use Departments in the user menu. Organization administrators own structure, default selection, lifecycle, organization defaults, new invitations, and organization roles. Department administrators own settings and member access only within assigned Departments. Add existing members by exact email lookup; review each assignment or role change. One person may administer Research, belong to Operations as a member, and have no Finance access. Rights remain independent in each Organization. Department changes use review dialogs. Deactivation requires affected active members to have another Department assignment and retains historical records. Reactivation does not restore revoked assignments automatically. Changing the default affects future default selections, not existing records or memberships. A conflict reloads the latest Department version while preserving your form entries for review. Contact invitation access must still be valid when the invitation is resent or accepted. Use Edit invited access to correct Department or Organization-role choices on the same pending invitation. Saving preserves its recipient, link, expiry, and delivery history without sending email or activating membership. An expired invitation remains expired until you explicitly resend it. Correcting the recipient email still requires revoking and reissuing the invitation. If another administrator changed it, your draft is preserved; Reload invitation replaces the draft with the latest saved access for a fresh review. Service entitlements and curated-data packages may be organization-wide or limited to one Department. A Department-specific service entitlement takes precedence over the Organization default for that Department. In Data provisioning, choose an explicit access scope when assigning a package; users in other Departments cannot list or download that Department's grant. Users with more than one available Department select the working Department from the user menu. The header shows the Organization and Department currently in force. Do not rely on a browser URL or a previously opened page to establish access; the API validates both scopes on every protected operation. Do not create a normal membership directly. Invitation acceptance provides the user-facing consent point and the audit link between invitation, user, and membership. For an internal employee, select the Phaeno organization and open User management. Use Add Phaeno user, enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, and select the narrowest roles needed for their work. Grant Platform administrator only when platform-wide administration is required. The card remains marked Pending invitation until acceptance; afterward, open its actions menu and choose Edit whenever the profile or roles must change. To follow up before acceptance, find the card marked Pending invitation, open its actions menu, and choose Resend invitation. Resending rotates the private link and is subject to a cooldown. Revoke an invitation that should not be accepted.

sections.heading: Convert a Prospect
sections.text: In the Prospect Company’s Requests tab, create Change the relationship and choose Customer or Partner. The form shows the current relationship and records your requested target. A reviewer approves it in Needs decision, then selects Apply Customer relationship or Apply Partner relationship in Approved / needs work and records the completed work. Applying the approved request performs the conversion and completes the request together. Customer-to-Partner and Partner-to-Customer reclassification are not supported by this action. Conversion preserves the Company, internal access identifier, users, memberships, grants, and audit history. It does not create an order, assign broad data access, or configure prices automatically. After conversion, complete the applicable operational setup: analysis availability and the billing and tax profile for a Customer, or offerings, negotiated reagent pricing, assembly profiles, and Partner assembly credit for a Partner.

sections.heading: Manage service entitlements
sections.text: From the Company, open Services, then select Entitlements to record dated commercial permission: Customers may receive PSeq Lab Service. Partners may receive PSeq Lab Service and PSeq Kit. Prospects and Phaeno organizations do not receive commercial service entitlements. Set configuration to Pending, Ready, or Blocked. A service is usable only when its entitlement is effective and configuration is Ready. Overlapping periods for the same service are rejected. If a service already has a non-ended entitlement, select Edit on that entitlement instead of adding another overlapping period. Preserve the service and existing effective date unless the commercial authorization changed, set the current configuration, attach the eligible approved source request, and save. Editing updates the existing audited record; it does not create a duplicate. Ended historical entitlements remain read-only. Online access does not imply a product or service entitlement. Add a dated entitlement here only after the corresponding product or service authorization is approved. When the entitlement implements an approved Portal request, select that request as its source. The selector shows only approved or applied requests for this organization that include the selected service. Leave the source blank only for a documented manual exception; do not attach an onboarding-only request to a service entitlement. Use End now instead of deleting an entitlement. Review the consequence dialog and record why the entitlement is ending. The Portal retains and displays that reason with the ended entitlement. PSeq Kit includes kit fulfillment followed by data submission and assembly. Do not create a separate data-assembly entitlement or sell data assembly without the kit.

sections.heading: Deactivate and restore access
sections.text: Deactivate a membership in Company detail to remove one access relationship. Deactivate the Company when none of its memberships should be usable; this suspends its attached Portal access scope. Reactivating the Company restores that scope. Each action opens a consequence dialog; verify the named Company or person before confirming. A deactivated membership is restored through a fresh invitation and acceptance. When all Portal access for another person must stop, select Deactivate on that Phaeno user and confirm the named person. The account, memberships, assigned roles, and audit history remain, but the user immediately loses effective access. A Phaeno administrator cannot deactivate their own account. Use Reactivate to restore an authorized disabled account; then review its memberships and roles before considering access complete. Preserve historical records; do not delete users, memberships, or organizations to resolve access problems.

sections.heading: Triage access safely
sections.text: Confirm the person’s email, session state, selected organization, active membership, role, and organization status. Use record identifiers and audit events to trace changes. Do not ask for passwords, sign-in codes, invitation tokens, browser storage, or another tenant’s records. For a user who has lost both the authenticator and all one-time backup codes, verify the person's identity and organization through the approved support procedure. In Clerk, reset the user's MFA enrollments and revoke every active session. Record the administrative recovery without storing codes, authenticator secrets, or recovery links. Tell the user to sign in again and connect a new authenticator; required MFA keeps the session pending until enrollment is complete. An email request starts the review but is not sufficient by itself to authorize the reset. If two administrators update the same record, the portal can reject the stale action. Reload the latest version, review the intervening change, and then make a deliberate new update rather than overwriting it.

guides.title: Statuses and recovery
guides.summary: Find each owning workspace and recover readiness, Lab work, releases, Finance, notifications, and retained history.

sections.heading: Statuses and recovery
sections.text: Recover the failed step from the record that owns it. Company access, order pricing, laboratory work, scientific release, billing, notifications, and retention have separate lifecycles. Repeating a successful earlier action can create duplicate work without fixing the failure.

sections.heading: Find the owning workspace
sections.text: | Work needing attention | Where to continue | | --- | --- | | Company access, invitation, or relationship request | CRM → Companies → People or the central Requests queue. Use Approved / needs work for approved requests awaiting completion. | | Customer pricing, quote, hold, or cancellation | Order operations → Order intake, then the Job. New Order starts each order; it is not configuration. | | Trial scope, approvals, acceptance, allowance, or closure | Order operations → Trial projects, then the Trial. | | Partner reagent or Assembly commercial review | Order operations → PSeq kits or Assembly. Open Lab work continues fulfillment or execution. | | Package, tube match, accession, execution, or scientific exception | The linked record in Lab operations. | | Scientifically approved PSeq package awaiting publication | Order operations → Result release, then the package. | | PSeq invoice, receipt, allocation, or reconciliation | The appropriate tab in Order operations → Finance. | | Cross-workflow follow-up or failed notice | Order operations → Attention; follow the item to its record. | | Curated-package grants, quarantine, or governance | Data provisioning, separate from the Customer Job's results. | Check search, status, date, owner, and Department filters before creating another record. A failed load differs from an empty list. Active intake includes held work; use On hold to focus on it, or All orders and history for accepted and terminal records. Lists preserve filters when you return from a record.

sections.heading: Recover Company readiness
sections.text: Open the Company's Services → Overview and select the affected Department in Department readiness. The same checks appear during New Order. Requirements are separated into before pricing, before quote issuance, and before invoicing. Follow the setup link beside the requirement; a historical readiness label does not satisfy it. An active Customer, effective Ready service entitlement, valid offering, and no operational block allow pricing to begin. Quote issuance also requires operational configuration and an active Customer organization administrator or an administrator of the Job’s Department. Billing and Finance approval may follow acceptance but must be complete before invoicing. See Customer lab authorization.

sections.heading: Recover laboratory and release work
sections.text: Packet and tube matching identifies authorized work; it does not record receipt. Continue to the linked Lab work, Record receipt, then Confirm accession. Resolve an unmatched or unsafe item through the receipt exception process. Resolve blocked execution and scientific exceptions in Lab operations using the authorized role. Keep internal investigation detail separate from the Customer summary. If a milestone publication fails, retry the existing event where recovery is offered; do not recreate the authorization, approval, or Lab work order. Review the complete, checksummed, malware-clean package and scientific approval in Result release before publication. Payment, invoice balance, and Customer credit do not gate PSeq results. Partner Assembly retains its separate credit and payment-hold rules. See Scientific approval and Data assembly review. Do not mark rejected files clean or change an order status to bypass a file gate. Correct the storage or scanning issue for failed or unavailable scans. Use the owning release action to withdraw a package that must no longer be delivered.

sections.heading: Recover Finance and notifications
sections.text: Use Finance for native PSeq invoices, receipts, allocations, corrections, imports, and reconciliation. An export does not record payment or mark an invoice posted elsewhere. Partner reagent shipments and Assembly outputs retain separate commercial source records for the manual accounting handoff. Before retrying a receipt or import, check whether it succeeded. Correct changed import input and preview it again; only the operator who reviewed the preview can confirm it. A receipt is recorded from accepted evidence, not from a successful email or connector retry. See Billing, payment, and release. Failed notifications do not reverse the underlying action. Correct eligible recipients or delivery issues and retry the existing notice where offered. For a hard-bounced invitation, use Company People to revoke it and issue a new invitation to the corrected Contact address. A queued recovery request is not proof of delivery or an available accounting connector.

sections.heading: Respect retained history
sections.text: Expired quotes require a current quote. Customer and Partner organization or department administrators can request an extension of a current expired Lab Service quote. Review Extension requested in Order intake and issue a new revision when approved. Accepted quotes keep their accepted status after their former deadline. Cancelled work, closed Trials, withdrawn files, completed Tasks, and expired downloads retain their history; follow the applicable new request, replacement, reissue, or correction workflow. Retention holds preserve or quarantine a release without extending its dates. Escalate with the record number, status, safe error, time, and action attempted. Keep credentials, invitation tokens, patient identifiers, investigations, and scientific files out of ordinary support notes.

guides.title: Trial Projects
guides.summary: Configure authorities and deliverables, approve scope, oversee samples and Lab work, release results, and close Trials.

sections.heading: Operate Trial Projects
sections.text: Trial Projects provide no-charge, closed-ended PSeq evaluations of extracted RNA. POMS owns the scientific scope, approvals, sample authorization, laboratory execution, and release. CRM owns the commercial request and follow-up. Trial work creates no order, quote, invoice, payment gate, or QuickBooks transaction. For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.
