Never request PHI. Use coded sample references, and keep suspected prohibited information out of ordinary notes, notifications, and CRM summaries. Place affected Trial work on hold and follow the authorized incident process when prohibited information is suspected.

sections.heading: Find Trial projects
sections.text: Open Order ops, then choose Trial projects in the workspace sidebar. Search by Trial number or company, filter by status or Sales owner, and use Clear all to reset the list. An empty list is shown separately from a search with no matches. Select a Trial number to open its workspace; existing Trial links continue to work.

sections.heading: Prepare the commercial request and scope
sections.text: From a CRM Company's Requests tab, create a Work → Trial Project request linked to an active Opportunity. Include commercial context only. Prepare the Company's active Prospect Portal access and department through the separate access workflow. A CRM request or an approved access request does not approve scientific Trial work. Select Start Trial beside the Company's request to carry that request into Trial creation and retain a route back to the Company. From Trial projects, you can also search and page through eligible requests. A request can create only one Trial; its link opens the existing workspace once started. Select Define scope. The dedicated scope page captures the objective, numeric original sample allowance, explicit submission window, current production PSeq workflow, active PSeq analysis definitions, and versioned deliverables. FASTQ, FASTA, and BAM are configurable initial defaults. Select the deliverables required for this evaluation; approved scopes preserve the selected definitions and versions. Record RNA submission instructions, success criteria, Prospect terms, residual-material retention and disposition, and internal estimated retail value and anticipated cost. Return arrangements require destination, handling, and shipping payer. They become immutable after the first sample submission. Internal costs never appear in the Prospect view. Choose Save draft to keep unfinished scope work and return to the Trial. Drafts may omit fields required for approval, including dates, scientific selections, return arrangements, terms, and the revision reason. Entered numbers and text still need to be valid. The draft is shared with authorized Phaeno Trial staff; the workspace shows who last saved it and when. Choose Resume draft to continue. Prospect users cannot see the draft. Saving does not change the current scope, existing approvals or acceptance, or authorize samples or laboratory work. Choose Submit scope for approval only when all required fields and scientific choices are complete. Submission creates a scope revision for review and clears the saved draft. An amendment then needs new approval and acceptance. A failed save or submission preserves your entries; if someone else changed the Trial or shared draft, reload the current record and review it before retrying. Scope planning remains available during a hold, but the hold still blocks approval and operational work. Closed Trials cannot save or submit scope changes.

sections.heading: Assign and record approval responsibilities
sections.text: Trial configuration shows primary and delegated authorities by Commercial and Scientific Operations domain. A Phaeno platform administrator assigns or revokes the primary approvers; the defaults are the CBO and COO responsibilities. Each primary may explicitly designate and revoke delegates for their own domain. Assigning a primary or designating a delegate supports an optional note; you can save without entering one. Searchable choices open above the form without expanding it. Use arrow keys and Enter to choose, Tab to move to the next field, or Escape to close the choices before closing the dialog. Revoking a primary also revokes their delegates. Past decisions remain intact. Each scope revision needs two affirmative decisions from two different people. A person authorized in both domains cannot approve both sides of the same revision. Request changes requires a new scope revision. Amend scope preserves the previous scope and requires two new approvals plus acceptance by a Prospect organization administrator or an administrator of the assigned Department. Scientific Operations authorities maintain the Deliverable catalog in Trial configuration. Choose Define revision, enter the deliverable key and display name, choose whether it is selected by default for new scopes, and give the reason. Reuse the existing key to create its next revision; the key must match the scientific output role. Saving retires the prior definition for new selection. Retire removes a definition from future selection and requires a reason. Neither action rewrites an approved scope.

sections.heading: Execute the approved work
sections.text: A Prospect organization administrator or an administrator of the assigned Department accepts the approved RUO/no-PHI terms and submits samples during the agreed window. Submit samples lets the administrator prepare a roster sharing one RNA type and shipping destination; submitting the roster creates one authorization and shipment. Each sample checks allowance, extracted-RNA metadata, approved analysis inputs, configured quantity units and limits, and active shipping instructions. The form identifies concentration and other inputs required by the approved analyses. Changed forms ask before discarding entries through Cancel, Escape, or browser navigation. Reloading the browser also warns about unsaved changes. During a save or explicit reload, editing, repeat actions, dismissal, and navigation are blocked until the operation finishes. Required fields in approval, configuration, and other short action dialogs show an issue when you leave them, and clear that issue as you correct it. A failed Trial configuration refresh preserves an open assignment or catalog draft; Retry configuration reloads the configuration. Reload current Trial; keep my entries refreshes scope-dependent choices and preserves entries for review, including when the reload fails; a changed scope requires a fresh acceptance confirmation. The shared Lab Operations provider creates Trial-authorized work pinned to the approved workflow version. Existing registered-tube, packet, receipt, accession, protocol, QC, sequencing, and scientific-review controls apply. Use Shipping and packets and each sample's Open laboratory work link. Trial holds and approval changes stop scientific progress and shipping mutations; custody facts and exception handling remain recordable. Schedule estimate communicates an estimate without changing scope. Authorize replacement records the failed sample, responsibility, reason, and approving authority. It permits exactly one replacement and never increases the frozen original allowance. Prospect-caused problems need the same explicit exception approval.

sections.heading: Review and release results
sections.text: The governed PSeq pipeline supplies immutable output packages tied to the Trial, submitted sample, and Lab work order. Complete checksums and clean scans precede scientific review. Scientific approval and release retain the existing PSeq separation of duties. A release manager selects one scientifically approved package per sample, with every frozen deliverable and no unapproved output role. Choose Partial when only some approved results are ready. Choose Complete only when the full approved package for every submitted sample, including approved replacements, is available. A complete release closes the Trial and freezes the shared global/organization retention policy. No payment or credit gate applies. The result archive includes a Trial manifest with the exact RUO statement, scope revision, sample/file lineage, and checksums. After complete release, earlier partial archives remain historical and direct members to the current complete package. Download controls show progress and availability, including closed retention access, and refresh after transfer attempts. Internal downloads do not satisfy the organization's retention condition. Retention and receipt supports the shared warning, grace, hold, deletion, and reissue workflow. A complete reissue after byte deletion requires newly transferred, scientifically approved packages for the same Trial samples and retains the original closure/material dates. Release and physical shipping remain subject to configured operational readiness. A visible workflow or a passing software test does not activate real storage, scanning, automated byte deletion, or validate laboratory packing instructions.

sections.heading: Close and follow up
sections.text: Successful completion is recorded by complete result release. Otherwise use Close Trial with the appropriate outcome and a Prospect-safe reason. Closure blocks new submissions and requests cancellation of unfinished Lab authorizations while preserving custody and history. Residual RNA retention starts at terminal closure. Record material disposition records actual exhaustion, return, or destruction once under the frozen terms; a due date does not record physical destruction automatically. A hold blocks disposition. Commercial outcome is separate: schedule owned and dated follow-up, record closed without conversion, or record conversion only after the explicit CRM relationship workflow changes the same organization to Customer or Partner. Conversion never extends Trial file deadlines or starts new Trial work. Use the existing organization closeout workflow for any deliberate deactivation after reviewing other active Trials, grants, and relationships. Trial milestones publish to CRM as relationship-safe summaries and a deep link. Scientific details and sample identifiers stay in the Trial/Lab workspaces. Failed publication retries without blocking Trial operations; the Trial workspace shows pending milestones and provides Retry CRM publication.

sections.heading: Close Prospect access
sections.text: After all Trial and commercial evaluation work is closed without conversion, a platform administrator can use Close Prospect access in the Trial. The action requires a reason and checks all Company Trials, holds, open Opportunities, data grants, and service access. Resolve those relationships before retrying. This deactivates the Company and Prospect organization while preserving Trial history and existing retention deadlines. Byte deletion never performs this deactivation automatically.

guides.title: Account and access
guides.summary: Accept invitations, protect sign-in, select a Department, and manage access within organization and Department roles.

sections.heading: Account and access
sections.text: An organization administrator is optional. A Company can operate through administrators of its active Departments. Department administrators act only within their assigned Departments; ask Phaeno to handle company-wide setup, invitations or roles when no organization administrator is available. Your Portal access is created through an invitation to a specific Prospect organization. The current organization, your active membership, and your role determine which data and administrative information is available.

sections.heading: Accept an invitation
sections.text: Open the newest invitation link sent for your Prospect organization. Review your name, organization, invited email, and Access after acceptance on the invitation page. Select Continue with your email. This goes directly to verification for the invited address; the email cannot be edited. Complete any required password or authenticator steps. Portal then returns you to the invitation for review and acceptance. Select Accept invitation to join, or Decline invitation. Known names do not need to be entered again. After accepting, the welcome message confirms your organization. Select Open Portal to continue. When creating your password, enter it once and use Show password or Hide password to check your entry. The invitation page shows the email address currently signed in. If it is not the invited email, choose Switch account, then sign in with the correct account. The invitation remains available in that browser while you switch accounts, and the identity service returns you to the invitation page after sign-in or account creation. Invitation links are private. A link can expire, be revoked, or be replaced by a newer invitation. If it is unavailable, ask your organization administrator or Phaeno to send a new invitation. The identity service handles password verification and recovery. Complete the secure sign-in steps shown in Portal, and use Forgot password? when offered to recover access. Phaeno can adjust the proposed Organization role or Department access on your existing pending invitation. The same link remains valid until its original expiry; changing access does not send another invitation. If the access changes after you review it, Portal displays the updated access and asks you to select Accept invitation again. An expired invitation must be resent before it can be accepted. Once your membership is active, authorized role and Department-access changes apply immediately. You receive an informational email and do not need to accept another invitation. A deactivated membership still requires a fresh invitation and acceptance to restore access.

sections.heading: Protect your account
sections.text: After your first sign-in step, connect an authenticator app and confirm the code it displays. Save the one-time backup codes shown during setup somewhere private and separate from the device running the authenticator. Never send an authenticator or backup code to Phaeno or your organization administrator. If you lose the authenticator but still have a backup code, use that code to sign in, then contact Phaeno to reset the authenticator enrollment. If you lose both the authenticator and every backup code, contact Phaeno directly. Phaeno will verify your identity and organization before resetting MFA; all active sessions are revoked and you must connect a new authenticator before Portal access resumes. Email can start the support request but does not itself bypass MFA.

sections.heading: Confirm the current organization
sections.text: The header shows the organization active in your current session. Every package, download, and administrative view is scoped to it. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is shown, stop and contact Phaeno before opening or downloading data.

sections.heading: Work within a department
sections.text: The header identifies your current organization and department. If you have access to more than one department, open the user menu and choose Department before opening or creating work. With a single available department, it is selected for you. Changing departments closes the previous workspace; finish or save your work before switching. Members see only their assigned departments. Organization administrators can select any active department in their organization, but the selected department still determines the records displayed. A department administrator's operational authority applies only to that department; it is not organization-wide access. Organization-wide data grants may be available in each department. If a department is unavailable or an expected Prospect record is missing, ask your organization administrator or Phaeno to review the assignment. Do not change URLs to try to access another department. Organization and department administrators can open Departments from the user menu to manage the departments within their authority.

sections.heading: Manage department access and settings
sections.text: When adding a department, enter its name and optional settings. The system assigns a reference such as DEPT-000123 when you save; you do not enter a Code. References are unique within the organization and stay the same when a department is renamed or deactivated. The department name remains its main label. Existing references, including GENERAL, are retained and shown as read-only context when editing. Organization administrators manage all departments, organization defaults, the default department, and department lifecycle. Department administrators manage settings and member access only in their assigned departments. A person can be an administrator in Research and a member in Operations; granting one department role does not grant organization-wide administrator rights. In Departments, use a department's actions menu to Edit settings or Manage members. To add an existing organization member, enter their exact email, choose Find member, and review the access change before confirming. Only an organization administrator can invite someone new through User management or change an organization role. Organization administrators already have access to every department and cannot be restricted by a department admin. An active member must retain at least one active department assignment. Organization administrators use Edit organization defaults to set the purchase-order rule, billing and notification email, and shipping and result instructions. A department override takes precedence; a blank override inherits the organization value, then the existing system or commercial fallback. Saved shipping and accepted-quote snapshots retain their recorded values. Result instructions do not change the storage destination or grant an ordering service. Invitations require reviewed department access for members. Select each department and grant its administrator role only when needed. Organization administrators receive access to every department, including future additions. If settings changed while you were editing, review your preserved entries against the latest version before saving again. Closing an unsaved form asks whether to discard the changes.

sections.heading: Understand roles
sections.text: Member can review and download package versions explicitly granted to the current Prospect organization. Organization administrator can also review organization download history and respond to applicable package-governance instructions. Prospect organization administrators manage membership only for their current organization. In User management, active members and invited people appear in one list. A Pending invitation status means the invitation has not been accepted and the offered access is not active. The person may already have a sign-in account. Use the card’s actions menu to resend or revoke that invitation, edit an active member’s organization role, or deactivate another member’s membership. An administrator cannot deactivate their own membership from User management. Restoring a deactivated membership requires a fresh invitation and acceptance. Contact Phaeno for a globally disabled account or an action the organization administrator cannot complete. For a Member invitation, select at least one Department. If you clear all Departments and select Send invitation, the form returns focus to Department access and explains what to select. Your entries are retained and no invitation is sent until the required information is valid.

sections.heading: Resolve common access states
sections.text: | What you see | What to do | | --- | --- | | Access unavailable after sign-in | Choose Continue invitation if it is shown, then review and accept the saved invitation. Otherwise, sign out and reopen the newest invitation link. | | Invitation link unavailable | Ask an administrator to confirm that the invitation is still pending and resend it. Use only the newest link. | | Email does not match | Sign out and use the email address that received the invitation, or request a corrected invitation. | | No active memberships | Ask your Prospect administrator to coordinate a fresh invitation with Phaeno. | | Wrong organization shown | Stop before opening data and contact Phaeno to verify the active membership. | | Organization unavailable | Ask Phaeno whether the organization is inactive. | | Account disabled | Contact Phaeno. A Prospect administrator cannot override a globally disabled account. | | Authenticator lost, backup code available | Use one backup code to sign in, then contact Phaeno for an MFA reset. | | Authenticator and backup codes lost | Contact Phaeno for identity verification and an MFA reset. Do not send old codes. | Never send a password, sign-in code, invitation token, or browser storage value in a support message.

guides.title: Data governance and downloads
guides.summary: Understand revocation, quarantine, retirement, download history, and safe governance responses.

sections.heading: Data governance and downloads
sections.text: Phaeno may revoke a grant, quarantine a package version, or retire a package as scientific, contractual, or governance needs change. Revocation and quarantine block future viewing and downloads but cannot recall files already downloaded. Retirement prevents new grants while preserving existing active grants.

sections.heading: Respond to a package notice
sections.text: When Phaeno sends a package-governance instruction: Confirm the package name and exact version. Stop new use or distribution when the notice requires it. Follow the safe action stated by Phaeno for copies already held by your organization. If an attestation is requested, an organization administrator should record the organization’s response in the portal. Do not include downloaded data, confidential scientific content, credentials, or internal investigation details in an attestation or support message.

sections.heading: Understand package states
sections.text: | State or event | Effect on your organization | | --- | --- | | Grant revoked | Future access to the granted package version stops. Earlier downloads are not recalled. | | Version quarantined | Future access is blocked while Phaeno investigates or resolves the issue. | | Package retired | The version is unavailable for new grants; existing active grants remain subject to their access and governance rules. | | New version published | Existing grants do not move automatically; Phaeno must grant the new version separately. |

sections.heading: Review download history
sections.text: Organization and department administrators can review curated download history for the selected department. This includes downloads from packages shared across the organization. Organization administrators can switch departments to review each department's activity. Department administrators see only activity within their assigned departments. Older download records without a recorded department remain available only to organization administrators, for organization-wide grants or grants assigned to the selected department. Changing a person's department assignments does not move or erase their earlier download records. Use download history to determine which package version and file were downloaded, by whom, and when. Download history does not prove that every local copy was deleted or that downstream use stopped; follow your organization’s governance process and any instruction from Phaeno. Phaeno retains audit history for grants, downloads, and governance actions. Do not ask support to delete history to conceal an access or download event. Safety and withdrawal instructions about previously supplied data continue to go to current organization administrators during an organization suspension. These notices do not restore Portal access. Contact Phaeno if you cannot record a required response in the portal.

guides.title: Use the Data Library
guides.summary: Review explicitly granted package versions and verify file or archive downloads.

sections.heading: Use the Data Library
sections.text: The Data Library is a read-only catalog of Phaeno-owned curated data package versions explicitly granted organization-wide or to your selected Department. A grant applies only to the named package version; access to one version does not automatically include earlier or later versions.

sections.heading: Review a granted package
sections.text: Confirm the Prospect organization and selected Department, then open Data Library. Select a package to review its summary and granted version. Review the manifest, file names, sizes, and checksums before downloading. Download an individual file or the package archive when needed. Preserve the package version and checksum with your internal record of the download. The package summary and manifest describe the curated release. They do not create a service request, place an order, or authorize use beyond the terms agreed with Phaeno.

sections.heading: Understand access boundaries
sections.text: Phaeno must explicitly grant each package version organization-wide or to the selected Department. A Department grant is unavailable in other Departments. A newly published version does not replace or extend an existing grant. Members of another organization cannot use your organization’s grant. The portal does not allow a Prospect to upload, edit, publish, or grant packages. Download activity is recorded for governance and support. If a package you expected is absent, provide Phaeno with the organization, package name, and expected version. Do not request access by sending copied data or another organization’s package details.

sections.heading: Verify a download
sections.text: Use the displayed checksum to verify that a downloaded file or archive is complete and unchanged. If a checksum does not match, delete the incomplete copy and retry once. If the second download also fails, stop and contact Phaeno with the package version, file name, time of the attempt, and the safe error message shown by the portal.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.summary: Find approved Trials, authorized shipping, curated data, and access for the selected Department.

sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: Portal gives a Prospect organization access to explicitly granted Phaeno-owned curated data and approved Trial Projects. Organization and assigned-Department administrators can accept frozen Trial scope and submit coded research RNA under the approved allowance and dates. Prospect access does not include paid laboratory requests, reagent orders, data-assembly requests, or other commercial ordering.

sections.heading: Navigate the help center
sections.text: Open the user dropdown menu in the toolbar and choose Documentation under Resources. This entry is available on both wide and narrow screens. On smaller screens, the Documentation tab sits below the toolbar and organization details. Guide navigation opens beneath the toolbar from the far-left edge of the screen. Its header identifies Documentation and, on wider screens, provides the pin or unpin icon. Pointer users can preview an unpinned sidebar by approaching the left edge; keyboard and touch users open it from the tab. Choosing a guide closes an unpinned sidebar and displays the article.

sections.heading: Confirm the current organization
sections.text: The header shows the organization active in your current session. That organization controls every record and action you can see, and information never carries between organizations. Self-service switching between multiple external organization memberships is not currently available. If the wrong organization is active, or your account belongs to more than one external organization, contact Phaeno before continuing.

sections.heading: Know your access level
sections.text: Active Prospect members can review and download the exact curated package versions granted organization-wide or to their selected Department. Organization administrators can also review organization download history and may be asked to respond to a package-governance notice. Prospect organization administrators use User management for durable invitations, Member or Organization administrator roles, and membership deactivation. Other members do not receive those controls.

sections.heading: Find your work
sections.text: Dashboard shows current Trial acceptance or sample-submission attention, Trial history, assigned data, authorized shipments, and administrator user access for the selected Department. Trial Projects opens approved scope, sample submission, laboratory progress, released results, and retention receipts. Read Trial Projects before accepting a scope. Data Library contains curated package versions explicitly granted to the Prospect. Samples & shipping contains authorized Trial Project return kits, tube matching, and shipping packets when Phaeno has prepared a shipment. For organization administrators, User management manages organization invitations, roles, and memberships. Documentation in the user dropdown menu opens these Prospect guides. Prospect organizations do not receive order or service workspaces. Phaeno alone can change the organization relationship after business approval.

sections.heading: Get help safely
sections.text: When contacting Phaeno, provide the organization name, package name and version, and a description of the step you were performing. Do not send passwords, sign-in codes, invitation links, authentication tokens, or downloaded data in a support message.

sections.heading: Search and browse guides
sections.text: Use Search documentation at the top of Documentation to find a guide or a matching section. Results update after a short pause; use at least two characters. Try “Trial acceptance” or “download grace”. Choose Filters to narrow results by Topic, Workflow, or Guide type. Clear filters removes those selections. Browse by topic opens guides for a topic without requiring search words. Workflow links and Related guides at the end of an article provide other ways to find relevant instructions. Select a result title to open its matching section. Your browser’s Back action restores the search and filters. Search uses the guides for your current organization; it does not include the public Website or operational records. A guide’s instructions do not change your account permissions. If no guides match, try fewer words or clear the filters. If search is temporarily unavailable, use Try again or Browse all guides. A documentation update may require Refresh page; guide browsing remains available while the update finishes.

guides.title: Organization access and transition
guides.summary: Manage Prospect membership and understand the Trial history, grants, and deadlines preserved after conversion.

sections.heading: Organization access and transition
sections.text: A Prospect organization may receive explicitly granted curated data and participate in an approved no-charge Trial. It cannot place paid commercial orders. Its users, memberships, grants, downloads, and audit history remain scoped to that organization.

sections.heading: Manage organization access
sections.text: Organization administrators manage access from User management. Enter the person’s first name, last name, and exact sign-in email, then choose Member or Organization administrator. Invited people appear in the same list with a Pending invitation status. Open a card’s actions menu to resend or revoke an invitation, edit an active member’s organization role, or deactivate another member’s organization membership. An administrator cannot deactivate their own membership from User management. Never copy or request an invitation token. A deactivated membership is restored only through a fresh invitation and acceptance. Contact Phaeno when the entire user account is disabled or when an invitation or membership action cannot be completed.

sections.heading: Understand a relationship change
sections.text: Only Phaeno can convert a Prospect organization to Customer or Partner, and only after the business relationship is approved. Conversion preserves the same organization, users, Department memberships, package grants, download history, approved Trial history, and audit history. Existing Trial results remain in their original Department under their existing retention dates. Conversion does not reopen a Trial or authorize additional Trial samples. Conversion does not automatically: create or authorize an order; grant additional package versions; configure prices, credit, offerings, or analyses; accept commercial terms on the organization’s behalf; or change a user’s role. After conversion, Phaeno completes the applicable service and commercial setup before order actions become available. Until then, continue to use only the capabilities visible in the portal.

sections.heading: Protect organization boundaries
sections.text: Do not use another organization’s invitation, package link, downloaded file, or commercial reference. If the current organization name is wrong, stop before opening data and contact Phaeno.

guides.title: Prepare and ship samples
guides.summary: Choose Trial containers, retain tube identities, print shipping inserts and record dispatch.

sections.heading: Prepare and ship Trial Project samples
sections.text: Open the approved Trial and its Shipping containers section. Phaeno creates and approves the Trial scope. A Prospect organization administrator or an administrator of the selected Department accepts the Trial scope and submits coded samples before shipping is authorized. These administrators may then prepare the resulting shipments within that Department. See Trial Projects.

sections.heading: Choose compatible containers
sections.text: Open Choose containers for tubes awaiting allocation. Review the recommended sizes by common name, SKU and usable tube capacity. The recommendation prefers the fewest containers and then the least spare capacity; it does not verify or reserve stock. Open Assign containers to review Containers to use. The recommendation starts as one row per container, with a compatible size selector, SKU/capacity and tube count. Add container chooses a size for the capacity still needed and assigns the remaining tubes up to its capacity. A row's Remove action removes only that container; changing or removing it preserves the other rows' tube counts. Size choices include smaller containers and the smallest size that covers the remaining capacity needed, excluding choices that make another selected container unnecessary. With sizes 5/10/20, three remaining tubes offer only a 5. For 30 tubes, 20+10 or six 5s are valid; two 20s are not offered. With 10+5 already selected, Add chooses another 10 and then a 5. Add container is disabled once selected capacity covers all tubes. Use recommendation replaces the current rows and tube counts. Stock requirements apply automatically; no manual stock quantities are entered here. The preview shows tubes, containers, capacity, spare slots and unallocated tubes. Confirm assignment creates one shipment for each container with allocated tubes. A partly filled container is valid and empty containers do not become shipments. If capacity is insufficient, Confirm partial assignment prepares the allocated tubes while the remaining tubes stay visible. The accepted Trial sample count and no-charge scope do not change. Tubes from one sample may occupy different containers. Adjust each row's tube count as needed. Counts must be whole numbers, fit each container and together equal the tubes allocated in the preview. The Summary stays visible while updating; confirmation becomes available when the current allocation has been checked.

sections.heading: Scan permanent tube barcodes
sections.text: Use Shipping container at the top of the shipment page to switch between this Trial's containers or return to remaining tubes awaiting containers. Each option shows the container identity, tube count and status. Switching with an unsaved scan asks whether to discard it; switching is blocked while saving. Before scanning starts, an organization or Department administrator can use Reset container configuration beside the Shipping container selector. The confirmation covers all containers and tubes for the Trial's shipment plan, not just the shipment you opened. The submitted sample list stays intact, and the previous configurations remain in the records and audit history for support. Retired configurations are not shown in your Shipping containers panel. Cancelling the confirmation changes nothing. Reset container configuration is also unavailable while a barcode entry is unsaved or saving. Discard an unsaved entry before revising the plan; saving the first scan locks the plan as described below. The action is locked once any container in that plan has a scan, linked physical kit, shipping insert, dispatch or receipt. Clearing a scan does not restore it. If work starts while your confirmation is open, the change is rejected; refresh and review the current state. A successful change returns you to container selection while preserving approved Trial scope, tube identities and physical kit inventory. Your organization must retain the connection between each coded sample ID and its own sample record. Do not enter patient names, medical-record numbers, dates of birth or other direct identifiers. Phaeno retains the permanent-tube-to-sample crosswalk used for shipping and intake. Select Open shipment for a prepared container and use Scan tubes into this shipment. Use the barcode field inside the active tube row. Scan the physical tube for that sample and tube number, then press Enter or Save scan. A successful match shows the saved number and barcode graphic, updates progress and advances to the next tube. The next active row scrolls into view and receives focus. Failed scans remain in their row for correction. Saved matches survive leaving the page. Paging away retains an unfinished barcode; Return to active tube restores its inline field. Previous tubes and Next tubes review long lists without expanding the whole page. Use tubes registered in a fulfilled kit for this Trial. The first successful scan associates the physical kit with this container; subsequent tubes must come from that kit. Unknown, ineligible, duplicate and already-used barcodes cannot advance scanning. A failed scan retains the barcode and current sample for correction and retry. Do not cover, alter or remove a permanent manufacturer barcode. Use Change tube or Correct tube to fix an assignment before dispatch and explain the correction. History is retained. When a shipping insert has already been confirmed, the correction voids it and issues a corrected revision. Destroy unused copies of the old shipping insert.

sections.heading: Confirm, print and dispatch each shipment
sections.text: When the shipment header has more than one action, open Actions to find them, including Review packing instructions, Print shipping insert, Download tube list (CSV) and Record shipment when permitted. If only one header action is available, it appears directly. Your permissions and the shipment's stage determine which actions appear. Use Print shipping insert again if you need another copy of the current revision. Review every declared tube, then select Review and confirm shipping insert. Confirmation distinguishes samples from tubes and freezes that shipment's destination, packing instructions and crosswalk. Spare slots do not create expected returns. Print one receiving sheet for each physical container and place it inside that container. It shows the Customer, Job/Trial and shipment references, sample and tube totals, essential handling notes and two widely separated scan targets: the large Scan to receive this shipment PH-P- insert barcode and, when assigned, the physical container barcode. Follow the full preparation and packing instructions in the Portal before shipping. Follow the approved temperature-control method, amount and packing steps for the actual container. Instructions may call for regular ice, dry ice, cold packs, another method or no cooling. Do not substitute methods or multiply the amount by the number of samples. Contact Phaeno if the instructions are missing or conflict. Full packing instructions and sample / tube list on the insert page retains the confirmed manifest, every sample and tube barcode, and split-sample references; these details do not print with the receiving sheet. Use Download tube list (CSV) to retain the complete crosswalk. Choose Actions → Review packing instructions to read the saved destination, common steps, sample requirements and actual container’s packing instructions. Check its cooling method and amount before packing, then select Print shipping insert. You can reopen these instructions without leaving the shipment. Print shipping insert checks the current revision, then opens the browser print dialog while keeping your shipment page open. Cancelling printing leaves you on the same shipment with your saved tube matches intact. If the insert cannot be checked, review the message on the shipment page, reconnect if needed and select Try again. Failed confirmation keeps the dialog entries for retry. Retain the shipping insert or use Download tube list (CSV) for your records. The shipping insert does not purchase postage or replace the carrier label. After handing each package to the carrier, record its carrier, tracking number and shipment time. Receipt progress aggregates tubes across shipments. In the Trial's Shipping containers panel, expand Sample receipt progress to review each sample. The first received package does not mark all tubes of a split sample received, and a barcode lookup is not proof that physical material arrived. Use Back to Trial for approved scope and current progress or Shipping container to move between its containers. Contact Phaeno with the Trial and shipment references if no compatible container exists, a tube cannot be matched confidently, or existing assignments need repacking. Do not guess a tube identity or change approved scope through shipping. Portal-generated identifiers now render as QR codes, with the exact identifier printed underneath. Shipping inserts, container labels, kit records and displayed sample/tube identifiers use the same format. Use a QR-capable 2D scanner. Existing manufacturer labels and older printed barcodes remain valid; do not relabel a tube or change its saved identity merely to match the new display. A scan still requires the correct workflow and does not by itself confirm receipt or accession. With one container, the tube count is assigned automatically up to its capacity and shown in a read-only text box. Any remaining tubes stay unallocated. With multiple containers, edit the tube counts to split the allocation. Returning to one container restores its automatic allocation. Samples are ordered by ID alphabetically and digit by digit, rather than by numeric value. In the Job, biological-source groups stay together. Tube matching follows that sample order, with each sample’s tubes in tube-number order. Saving a match advances to the next unmatched tube.

guides.title: Statuses and troubleshooting
guides.summary: Resolve Trial acceptance, sample allowance, shipping, result availability, and curated-data access problems.

sections.heading: Statuses and troubleshooting
sections.text: Use the visible organization, package version, grant state, and safe portal message to understand a problem before contacting Phaeno. | What you see | Meaning | What to do | | --- | --- | --- | | No packages | No active package version is granted organization-wide or to the selected Department, or its grant is unavailable. | Confirm the organization and Department shown in the header, clear filters, then ask Phaeno to review the exact package version. | | Package or version missing | Grants are version-specific and do not move automatically to a new release. | Provide Phaeno with the expected package and version. | | Access revoked | Phaeno ended the organization’s future access to that version. | Stop retrying and follow any governance instruction from Phaeno. | | Version quarantined | Future access is blocked while Phaeno reviews the release. | Do not use another link or another organization’s copy. Wait for Phaeno’s instruction. | | Package retired | The version is unavailable for new grants; an existing active grant may remain usable. | Ask Phaeno whether an approved replacement exists. | | Download failed | The file or archive did not complete successfully. | Retry once. If it fails again, report the file name, package version, time, and safe error message. | | Checksum mismatch | The downloaded content is incomplete or changed. | Delete that copy, retry once, and contact Phaeno if the second checksum also fails. | | Wrong organization shown | The current session is scoped to a different membership. | Stop before opening or downloading data and contact Phaeno. | | Order action missing | Prospect organizations cannot place paid laboratory, reagent, or data-assembly orders. Approved no-charge Trials use their own workflow. | Contact Phaeno if the business relationship should be reviewed. |

sections.heading: Trial and shipment questions
sections.text: | What you see | What to do | | --- | --- | | Trial awaiting approval | Phaeno Commercial and Scientific Operations must approve the same scope revision before acceptance is available. | | Acceptance needed | A Prospect organization administrator or an administrator of the selected Department must review and accept the exact approved scope and terms. | | Sample submission unavailable | Check scope acceptance, submission dates, remaining allowance, and any hold. Use the approved replacement action only when Phaeno authorized a specific failed sample. | | Shipping is unavailable | The accepted Trial must have authorized samples and a prepared return kit. An organization or authorized Department administrator manages the shared shipment after that handoff. | | Results are not downloadable | Check release, withdrawal, and retention status. Trial results have no payment or credit gate. | | Trial no longer accepts changes | Closed or completed Trials retain their history. A relationship conversion does not reopen them or extend result-download dates. | Open the Trial number for its exact scope and status. Clear search and status filters if it is missing from the list. A failed load is different from no matching records; use the displayed retry action before assuming that work is absent. See Trial Projects and Sample shipping.

sections.heading: Report a problem safely
sections.text: Include the organization name, package name and version, file name when applicable, time of the event, and the portal’s safe error message. Do not attach downloaded data or send passwords, sign-in codes, invitation tokens, access tokens, browser storage, or another organization’s information.

guides.title: Trial Projects
guides.summary: Review and accept approved Trial scope, submit coded RNA, and download released results.

sections.heading: Your Trial Project
sections.text: A Trial Project is a no-charge, closed-ended PSeq evaluation of extracted RNA. Phaeno defines and approves its scope with you. It does not create a paid laboratory order, quote, invoice, or payment obligation. For Research Use Only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures. Do not enter protected health information (PHI), patient identifiers, medical record numbers, dates of birth, or direct personal identifiers. Use coded research references and keep any identity mapping outside the Portal.

sections.heading: Review and accept the scope
sections.text: Open Trial projects and select the Trial number. Confirm the selected organization and department. Active members can view approved Trials in their department; an organization administrator or an administrator of that Department can accept scope or submit samples. Ordinary members cannot perform these actions. The workspace shows the objective, original sample allowance, submission opening and closing times, approved PSeq analyses, deliverables, acceptance criteria, material handling, and terms. Dates are displayed in your local time zone. Commercial and Scientific Operations approvals must come from two different authorized Phaeno people. Select Review and accept scope, read the complete approved scope in the dialog, and affirm the RUO/no-PHI terms. Acceptance applies to that scope revision. A later amendment requires new Phaeno approvals and your organization's acceptance again. Previous approved revisions remain available in the workspace.

sections.heading: Submit extracted RNA
sections.text: An organization or assigned-Department administrator selects Submit samples while the approved submission window is open. In Submit extracted RNA samples, choose the extracted-RNA type and shipping destination for the batch. The form shows the required quantity unit and limits. Enter a unique coded reference, biological source, tube count, quantity, storage requirements, safety declaration, and the inputs required by the approved analyses for each sample. Concentration is required when an approved analysis requires it. Use Add another sample to prepare the roster, review each sample, and confirm RUO and no PHI. Submit the roster together to create one laboratory authorization and shipment for samples sharing that type and destination. Prepare separate submissions for different types or destinations. The submit button shows how many samples will be submitted. The original sample allowance is specific to this Trial. There is no automatic renewal or universal sample cap. If submission is unavailable, the workspace explains whether approval, acceptance, a hold, the time window, closure, or the allowance is responsible. Submitting creates the authorized laboratory work and a shipment awaiting Phaeno's return-kit preparation. Open this Trial's Return kit and shipment section for the related shipment and follow Prepare and ship samples. Follow the approved packing and receiving instructions; submitting a record does not mean the material has been received. If Phaeno authorizes a replacement, choose the failed original sample in Approved replacement for. Each authorization allows one replacement and preserves the original history. A failed sample never grants an unapproved extra slot.

sections.heading: Follow progress and download results
sections.text: The workspace shows sample progress, customer-safe updates, and any schedule estimate. Trial estimates are not guaranteed turnaround times. A hold stops scientific progress and delivery while Phaeno resolves the issue. Partial results may become available before the entire Trial finishes. Their release does not start the complete-package retention period. When Phaeno releases all approved deliverables for the submitted samples, the Trial becomes Completed and the complete package receives its frozen retention policy. If the approved work cannot be completed, Phaeno records Closed incomplete with a reason. Use Download package for an available release archive, including its RUO manifest, or download an individual file. Download controls show progress and explain unavailable results. After complete release, earlier partial archives remain in history with a link to the complete package. Retention and receipt shows the package's manifest, frozen deadlines, download state, and retained lineage. The workspace refreshes after a transfer so availability and receipt information reflect the latest state. The initial file policy is 30 exact 24-hour days from complete release, with a warning five days before deletion if files remain undownloaded and a five-day grace period when required. Phaeno may configure organization overrides; the receipt shows your package's actual policy. A successful download by any authorized organization member satisfies that file for the organization. Failed or partial transfers do not count. Access may close earlier if the release is withdrawn or held. Deletion removes bytes; history and receipts remain and do not promise restoration.

sections.heading: Material, closure, and next steps
sections.text: Residual RNA normally remains for 30 days after terminal Trial closure, using the exact duration frozen in your scope. Phaeno records actual destruction, return, or exhaustion separately. Return is available only under arrangements approved before submission, including destination, handling, and shipping responsibility. Trial material is not reused for another purpose through this workflow. Trial completion does not convert your organization automatically. If Phaeno later converts it to Customer or Partner, approved Trial history remains under the same organization and department. Conversion does not extend download deadlines or permit new submissions to the old Trial. Further work requires a separate approved workflow. If a record changes while you are entering information, select Reload current Trial; keep my entries, review the updated scope and available choices, and resolve any entries that are no longer valid. A changed scope clears the acceptance confirmation so you must read and affirm the current terms before retrying. Your entries are kept if the reload fails. Editing, repeat actions, and dismissal are temporarily blocked while a submission or explicit reload finishes. Closing a form with changed entries asks whether to discard them. Contact Phaeno with the Trial number and the step that failed; do not send sample identity mappings or confidential scientific files in a support message.

sections.heading: Multiple tubes in a Trial submission
sections.text: When submitting the sample roster, review and confirm Run one tube per specimen; use a reserve only after the current attempt fails. Extra tubes remain reserves and do not increase the approved analysis allowance. Phaeno selects a suitable source after receipt and review; no reserve starts automatically. This instruction is retained with the laboratory authorization for that submission.
